stories.title: ₹2-8 crore for a ticket in UP elections:Rajbhar, Nishad and Anupriya's parties selling MLA tickets; watch the on-camera negotiations
stories.summary: An MLA ticket in the Nishad Party costs ₹5 crore. Pay half now and the rest before the ticket is announced. Last time, rates were ₹7-8 crore in some places and ₹2-3 crore in others. This is what a senior Nishad Party leader tells our undercover reporters. Even before the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections are officially announced, allegations of ticket selling have surfaced within political parties. The price of a ticket appears to depend on the party's strength and its prospects on a particular seat. Sources claim that tickets for weaker seats can be secured for around ₹2 crore, while strong and winnable seats may cost up to ₹8 crore. Office-bearers linked to parties represented by ministers in the Yogi Adityanath government are allegedly involved in these deals. Compared to the previous election, ticket rates have reportedly increased by one-and-a-half to two times. Opposition-linked parties are also alleged to be following a similar practice. To investigate these claims, Dainik Bhaskar sent two undercover reporters into four political parties in Uttar Pradesh. Posing as social workers and aspiring political leaders, they spent nearly one-and-a-half months building contacts within party organisations. During this period, several office-bearers allegedly demanded money in exchange for Assembly election tickets. The investigation began with the Nishad Party, led by Dr Sanjay Nishad, a Cabinet minister in the Uttar Pradesh government and an ally of the BJP. One of his sons is also an MLA, and party affairs are largely handled by family members. After joining party activities, the reporters developed contacts with Ravindramani Nishad, Dr Sanjay Nishad's brother-in-law. Ravindramani has previously served as the party's state president. He currently holds the position of Uttar Pradesh election in-charge and is also a member of the state's Backward Classes Commission. After several rounds of interaction, Ravindramani called the reporters to Hamirpur. It was there that discussions regarding an Assembly election ticket and the alleged financial terms took place. Reporter: We want the Fazilnagar (Kushinagar district) seat because your vote base is there. Ravindramani: Since you have expressed your wish, we will fight your battle. Look, this is our first meeting. When we meet again, we will discuss it further. Reporter: But there is not much time left either. Ravindramani: The Chief Minister has also said that the Model Code of Conduct will be imposed by December 15. Reporter: Our request is that if we had known earlier, we would have started preparations. Ravindramani: Last time, the calculation was such that whoever was told, that's what happened. Even the Minister (Dr Sanjay Nishad) used to tell us that you should speak to people. But this time, the election is at a very different level. Reporter: Yes, there will be a tough fight. Ravindramani: Yes, the party will prepare accordingly. You can assume that Rs 5 crore will be required. If it reaches that amount, there will be no ifs and buts. Reporter: If we pay the amount in one go, will it be confirmed immediately, or should we pay half first? What needs to be done? Ravindramani: That's up to you. Pay half first and the remaining half before the announcement, when election time comes. The party should not feel that after making the announcement, you might back out. Last time, everyone was announced at the last moment, so everything happened in one go. Reporter: What was the rate last time? Ravindramani: It varied. In some places, it was Rs 7-8 crore, in others Rs 2-3 crore, and elsewhere Rs 5-6 crore. It was decided seat-wise. Reporter: Okay, will it be Rs 5 crore for the Fazilnagar seat as well, or will it be less? Ravindramani: Now the rate is almost the same everywhere. Reporter: What if someone else meets Doctor Sahab? Will my ticket get cancelled? Ravindramani: One thing is certain. There are only six months left before the election. Even if someone meets Doctor Sahab, they will still have to come through us. Reporter: What should be our next step? Ravindramani: On the 7th, it is Minister ji's birthday. To make a good impression, come with a gift. The meeting will happen that day itself. We will introduce you. Reporter: Should we gift gold or something else? Ravindramani: That's up to you. We just say that the first impression is the last impression. After that, we will arrange a 10-minute meeting with him, either the same day or the next day. Reporter: All this is fine, but what can we do for you? Ravindramani: Whatever 5% or 10% comes our way will be fine. This means the Nishad Party, which is part of the ruling alliance in UP, is allegedly selling tickets. Are other parties associated with the government doing the same? To find out, we entered the Suheldev Bharatiya Samaj Party (SBSP) posing as a party worker. The party's national president is Om Prakash Rajbhar, who is also a Cabinet minister in the UP government. To negotiate for a ticket, we contacted National Organisation Minister Salik Yadav. He called us to Ghazipur, where the following conversation took place: Reporter: How much funding will be required? Salik Yadav: We will discuss it and decide how much money will be needed. That will become clear. Reporter: Can you tell us roughly? Salik Yadav: Let the meeting with the Minister happen on the 7th. It is not right to discuss money everywhere. Reporter: We will do whatever is required. We just want the ticket. Salik Yadav: Now that you have put this in my mind, I have become your lawyer. The final decision is in someone else's hands, but we will be there. Nothing will happen without consulting us. Reporter: What is your estimate? How much will it cost? Salik Yadav: Brother, the matter may be settled for Rs 5-6 crore, but we will have to assess the situation. The meeting ended with Salik Yadav saying he would speak to National President Om Prakash Rajbhar. He said he would later inform us about the ticket rate. A few days later, we called him again. He said he had spoken to Arvind Rajbhar, son of the national president. He then revealed the conversation: Salik Yadav: I spoke to Arvind. Reporter: What did he say about funding? Salik Yadav: He said that Rs 10-15 crore is being spent in the BJP. We told him that we have nothing to do with the BJP. We are only talking about our side. Reporter: What did you tell him? Salik Yadav: We told him that our estimate is only this much (Rs 5-6 crore). We have to contest the election within that budget. Reporter: What did he say? Salik Yadav: We told him that the overall budget was Rs 10-12 crore and that a share would also have to go to the party. We wanted to gauge Arvind's estimate, so we told him it would be Rs 5-7 crore. But he said it would not happen at that amount. Reporter: So how much should be agreed upon finally? Salik Yadav: We told you already, it has to be done within Rs 6 crore. Arvind has not revealed much yet. Reporter: Did he say anything specific? Salik Yadav: Yes, they were talking about Rs 7-8 crore or even Rs 10-12 crore. We said we would not go that high. We also told them that we would get a new car from you. There is no point hiding these things. If they find out later, they may feel bad. Reporter: So it could go up to Rs 8 crore? Salik Yadav: It will be less than that, but their intention is around Rs 8 crore. Reporter: Last time it was Rs 5 crore, and this time you have proposed Rs 6 crore. Salik Yadav: Yes, you had asked us to tell them up to Rs 6 crore. Reporter: What did they say? Salik Yadav: They said, "Okay, talk to Babuji (Om Prakash Rajbhar)." After this, we contacted officials of Apna Dal (Sonelal). The party's national president, Anupriya Patel, is a Union minister, while her husband Ashish Patel is a minister in the UP government. His home district is Chitrakoot. The district president there, Hemraj Singh, is considered close to the party's national vice-president Ashish Patel. When we contacted Hemraj Singh, he called us to the party office in Chitrakoot. The following conversation took place there: Reporter: What will have to be done? Hemraj Singh: Here, 2 is going on. Reporter: Two crore rupees? Hemraj Singh: No. Last time, the MLA from Mau (Avinash Chandra Dwivedi) paid Rs 8 crore. Right now, there is competition between two people, he was saying. Reporter: Did the MLA really pay Rs 8 crore? Hemraj Singh: Yes, that same Avinash Chandra Dwivedi. Reporter: Rs 8 crore is a huge amount. Hemraj Singh: That's what was paid. A man named Narendra Patel had offered Rs 7 crore. He was from Mau. Even then, he did not get the ticket. They gave it to Avinash ji because he paid Rs 8 crore directly. Reporter: If you give us a rough figure, it will be easier. Hemraj Singh: I already told you, our MLA paid Rs 8 crore. Reporter: So should we arrange a similar amount? Hemraj Singh: They will not take less than that now. Are opposition parties also selling tickets? To find out, we approached the Janvadi Party (Socialist). The party was allied with the Samajwadi Party in the last Assembly election and also in the 2024 Lok Sabha election. To infiltrate the party, we met General Secretary Umesh Singh Chauhan. After several meetings, he became convinced that we genuinely wanted a ticket. He then called us to Gorakhpur and introduced us to the party's national president, Dr Sanjay Singh Chauhan, at his residence. Reporter: We had spoken with General Secretary Umesh Singh Chauhan about the Padrauna or Fazilnagar Assembly seat. We can also bring Brahmin votes there. Sanjay Singh: Padrauna will be easier. It can be managed. I cannot guarantee Fazilnagar because Akhilesh ji has an emotional attachment to that seat. It may still be available, but Akhilesh ji could face difficulty because he is an emotional leader. Reporter: Okay, wherever you think best. Sanjay Singh: Look, if you join us, your goal is to become an MLA. My goal is to strengthen my party. By the Banaras rally on September 14, I will change the entire political atmosphere of Purvanchal. Reporter: Last time, Doctor Sahab (General Secretary Umesh Chauhan) had mentioned Rs 1 crore. Sanjay Singh: If you do that much now, it will provide us some relief. Reporter: What will need to be done next? There was also talk of making me a state-level office-bearer. Sanjay Singh: Yes, that will be done. Reporter: If I contest the election, what will be my total expense? Sanjay Singh: (Looking towards the General Secretary) You and Doctor Sahab can sit together and discuss that. Reporter: You are the supreme authority, the party chief. That is why we are asking you. Sanjay Singh: Start with Padrauna and rest assured. Whether there is an alliance with the SP or the BJP, that seat will remain with us. Do one thing—arrange Rs 1 crore right now. Then, for our Banaras rally on September 14, arrange another Rs 1 crore. That is the Prime Minister's constituency, and every report from there reaches the Prime Minister's Office. Reporter: One crore or one and a half crore? Sanjay Singh: Arrange Rs 1 crore. Reporter: After that, what happens? Sanjay Singh: After that, whatever makes you happy. Your ticket will be confirmed. Reporter: Does that mean Rs 2 crore in total? Sanjay Singh: (Nods in agreement) Rs 2 crore. If I ever get into a serious difficulty, I will remember you. Apna Dal (S) leads on both fronts here, the largest claimed vote bank at roughly 8% and the most MLAs (13) along with a cabinet seat. SBSP and Nishad Party sit close together with 4-6 MLAs each despite smaller vote-bank shares, while Janwadi Party (Socialist) has the thinnest base (around 1%) and no seats in government at all. Worth noting the table itself flags that the Apna Dal and SBSP percentages aren't fully consolidated vote blocs, so the raw numbers may overstate how reliably those votes translate into seats. Why such ticket deals are illegal Tomorrow in Part 2: An undercover investigation reveals the alleged price of power in Uttar Pradesh — from an MLA ticket to a minister's post. Find out which national party is at the centre of the claims, and how much money is allegedly being demanded behind closed doors.

stories.title: Monsoon to enter UP through Purvanchal after delay:Sonbhadra and Ballia likely to receive first rains between June 20 and 25
stories.summary: The southwest monsoon is expected to enter Uttar Pradesh four to five days later than usual this year, with its arrival now likely between June 20 and 25. Unlike the past two years, when it advanced into the state through the Bundelkhand region, this year the monsoon is expected to make its first entry through eastern Uttar Pradesh (Purvanchal), particularly via Sonbhadra and Ballia. According to meteorologists, satellite imagery captured by INSAT-3DS on June 17 showed largely clear skies over Uttar Pradesh, mainly because a strong low-pressure system has not yet developed over the Bay of Bengal. Monsoon advancing slowly towards Uttar Pradesh After making landfall in Kerala on June 4, the monsoon covered 19 states within 14 days. Weather experts say it has already crossed Muzaffarpur in Bihar and is now very close to the Uttar Pradesh border. Although the normal onset date for the monsoon in Uttar Pradesh is between June 18 and 20, experts note that from 2022 to 2024 it reached the state only around June 24–25, and a similar pattern is expected this year. Expected timeline of monsoon progression The monsoon typically advances into Uttar Pradesh through two branches—one from the Arabian Sea and the other from the Bay of Bengal. This year, moisture-laden winds from the Bay of Bengal are expected to move through Bangladesh and Bihar before entering eastern Uttar Pradesh. Western UP records excess rainfall despite delayed monsoon The India Meteorological Department (IMD) had earlier forecast that Uttar Pradesh would receive around 8% below-normal rainfall during the monsoon season. However, in the absence of a strong low-pressure system, estimates now suggest rainfall could be around 10% below normal. Interestingly, western and central Uttar Pradesh have already recorded significantly higher rainfall between June 1 and 16 due to active western disturbances: Rainfall in western and central UP was 37% above normal, with 31.6 mm recorded against the usual 23.1 mm. In contrast, eastern Uttar Pradesh experienced 28% below-normal rainfall, receiving only 22.2 mm compared to the average 30.8 mm. Heatwave alert continues for eastern Uttar Pradesh Before the monsoon arrives, different parts of Uttar Pradesh are experiencing contrasting weather conditions. In eastern districts, where rainfall has been delayed, temperatures are once again climbing to 42–45°C. Severe heatwave warnings have been issued for Prayagraj, Varanasi, Ballia, and nearby areas over the next three to four days. Meanwhile, central and western regions—including Lucknow, Kanpur, and Noida—are witnessing high humidity and uncomfortable, sticky conditions despite relatively lower temperatures ranging between 38°C and 40°C. Meteorologists expect substantial relief only after the first widespread monsoon showers around June 24–25. Farmers advised to avoid long-duration paddy varieties Amid concerns over reduced rainfall, agricultural experts are urging farmers to opt for short-duration, water-efficient paddy varieties. Speaking to Dainik Bhaskar, Professor P.K. Singh from the Department of Agriculture at BHU said that lower rainfall could reduce paddy production in Uttar Pradesh by up to 20%. Delayed rains in June and July may also postpone transplantation and reduce the total cultivated area. He advised farmers to avoid traditional paddy varieties that require abundant water and take more than 150 days to mature. Instead, they should prefer improved varieties that mature within 110–120 days and require less water, helping minimize the impact of a weak monsoon.

stories.title: Hazrat Umar’s contributions discussed in Gorakhpur:Blood donation camp on June 16, DIG says one drop of blood can save a life
stories.summary: In Gorakhpur’s Turkmanpur area, religious programmes were organised on Sunday at Maktab Islamiat and Madrasa Raza-e-Mustafa. The 33rd monthly women’s seminar focused on the life and contributions of the second Caliph of Islam, Hazrat Syedna Umar (RA). Meanwhile, during the Dars-e-Quran session, the significance of Surah Kausar and its teachings were discussed. Speakers Muazzama Quraishi and Shifa Khatoon said that Hazrat Umar (RA) was among the closest companions of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH). They noted that he devoted his entire life to spreading the message of Islam. He is credited with introducing the Islamic Hijri calendar and is remembered for strong leadership, efficient administration, a fair justice system, and support for the needy. Writers from around the world have also mentioned Hazrat Umar Chief speaker Qari Muhammad Anas Naqshbandi said that the life and work of Hazrat Umar (RA) have been widely referenced by several authors in their writings. His decisions and governance continue to serve as a model even today. He added that Hazrat Umar’s life conveys a message of justice, humanity, and social welfare. Dars-e-Quran explains message of Surah Kausar During the Dars-e-Quran session, Hafiz Rahmat Ali Nizami said that although Surah Kausar is the shortest chapter in the Holy Quran, it carries a deeply important message. It teaches gratitude towards Allah’s blessings, devotion in worship, and adherence to the right path. Qari Muhammad Anas Naqshbandi further said that Surah Kausar also teaches patience and trust during difficult times. He added that no matter how challenging circumstances become, one should not lose courage and must continue to follow the path of righteousness. Maintain patience and faith in difficult times At the end of the programme, participants recited Durood and Salam and prayed for peace, prosperity, and brotherhood in the country. A large number of women, including Mubassira Quraishi, Ayesha Khatoon, Tania Akhtar, Sana Fatima, Fiza Khatoon, Asma Khatoon, Noorjahan, Saniya, and Adiba, were present.

stories.title: 4 passengers from UP killed by passing train in MP:Got off Intercity Express after panic spread over mobile blast rumour
stories.summary: Four people from Uttar Pradesh were killed in a train accident in Madhya Pradesh’s Morena on Sunday. The deceased included a mother and her son. Following rumours that a mobile phone had exploded and caused a fire, some passengers panicked and got off the Udaipur Intercity Express. Four of them were then hit by another train. The victims were identified as Kanchan Singh (25), wife of Mohit Singh and a resident of Meerut; Shakuntala Singh (60), wife of Bhura Singh from Runakta in Agra; Afreen (35), wife of Nadeem; and Asad (4), son of Nadeem Khan, both residents of Agra. Afreen and Asad were mother and son. According to railway authorities, the accident occurred on the Hetampur-Dholpur rail section under the Jhansi Division of North Central Railway. Train number 19665, the Khajuraho-Udaipur Intercity Express, had stopped between Hetampur and Dholpur stations at around 4:15 pm on Sunday after its emergency chain was pulled. See 2 pictures related to the accident Passengers fled after chain pulling and rumor According to railway officials, the alarm chain was pulled in one of the coaches, forcing the train to stop in the middle of the section. Around the same time, rumours spread that a mobile phone had exploded inside a coach. The rumour triggered panic among passengers, prompting several of them to hurriedly get off the train. Got down on the track and came under another train Some of the passengers who had disembarked from the Udaipur Intercity Express moved onto the adjacent up-line track. At that moment, train number 20424, the Firozpur-Seoni Patalkot Express, was passing through the section at high speed. Four passengers standing on the track were struck by the train and died on the spot. Passengers panicked after mobile blast alert According to passenger Pooja, who was returning from Bageshwar Dham, chaos erupted in the coach after rumours of a mobile phone blast spread. As soon as the train stopped following the chain pulling, frightened passengers got off and began running towards the tracks. Teams from the Railway Protection Force (RPF), Government Railway Police (GRP) and the local administration rushed to the scene after receiving information about the incident. A rescue operation was launched. All bodies sent for post-mortem Morena SP Dharmraj Meena said - Our team was taking action on sand storage in Sarai Chhola and Civil Line area. During this time, information was received from a shepherd villager that a train was stopped and some incident had occurred. As soon as the information was received, both police teams were dispatched to the spot. This incident occurred in the Dholpur and Morena border area. All bodies have been taken into custody. Necessary legal procedures are being carried out. Every possible assistance will be provided to the relatives of the deceased. Currently, the bodies are being sent for post-mortem. Bodies sent for post-mortem Morena SP Dharmaraj Meena said that police teams were carrying out action against illegal sand storage in the Sarai Chhola and Civil Lines areas when a shepherd informed them that a train had stopped and an incident had taken place. Police teams from both areas immediately rushed to the spot. The accident occurred near the Dholpur-Morena border region. All four bodies have been taken into custody and the necessary legal procedures are being carried out. The families of the deceased will be provided all possible assistance. The bodies have been sent for post-mortem examination. Shakuntala Singh, a resident of Agra, was also among those killed in the accident. (File photo)

stories.title: Shamli's Ayush Malik seen without beard, hair after conversion row:Claims Hindu groups forcibly shaved him; says decision to convert was his own
stories.summary: A fresh twist has emerged in the alleged religious conversion case involving the son of a wealthy pharmaceutical businessman in Shamli. A photograph of Ayush Malik alias Rahman without a beard and with his head shaved has surfaced on social media. The image shows Ayush without the beard and hair he had previously been seen with. There is speculation that some Hindu organisations shaved Ayush’s beard and head and facilitated his return to Hinduism after a purification ritual at a temple. However, neither the police nor the family has officially confirmed these claims. Discussions about Ayush’s alleged “ghar wapsi” are currently circulating on social media. A social media user named Munawwar Shah shared the photograph and claimed that Mohammad Ali alias Ayush Malik had been in police custody for the past three days. The post alleged that his beard and hair had been removed and that he would return to Hinduism after prayers at an Arya Samaj temple. The user also wrote that faith is a matter of the heart and urged people to avoid making inappropriate comments and instead pray for him. Father says Ayush is staying with his sister Ayush’s father, Deoraj Malik, said he had neither spoken to nor met his son over the past three days. According to him, Ayush is currently staying with his sister in Noida. Shamli SP N.P. Singh said only the family could provide accurate information about the matter. Ayush’s wife Chandni Qureshi and her father Islam Qureshi have already been sent to jail by police. On Saturday, police also arrested Chandni’s cousin Taufiq alias Bhola. How the case unfolded The case is linked to Dayanand Nagar and Qureshi Basti in Shamli. Deoraj Malik, a pharmaceutical businessman and president of the Shamli Chemists Association, lives in Dayanand Nagar. His daughter is married and lives in Noida, while his son Ayush, a B-Pharma graduate, runs a medical store. According to police, Ayush joined Qureshi Plus Gym around five years ago, where Chandni Qureshi, a resident of Qureshi Basti, worked as a trainer. Deoraj Malik alleged that Chandni trapped his son in a romantic relationship and secretly had him undergo an Islamic marriage ceremony four years ago. He claimed Ayush began changing his appearance around six months ago, first growing a beard and later regularly visiting a mosque. Photographs later surfaced showing Ayush offering namaz in a mosque and wearing a skullcap and kurta-pyjama at his medical store. On June 6, Deoraj Malik filed an FIR against the gym trainer, six members of her family and three clerics, accusing them of forced religious conversion and extortion. Mahant’s video brought the issue into the spotlight The controversy came to light after Mahant Swami Yashveer of Yog Sadhana Ashram in Muzaffarnagar released a video on June 4. He alleged that Chandni Qureshi had trapped the only son of a medical store owner and that the entire family had converted under pressure. Following the video, Hindu organisations began protesting and threatened demonstrations outside the gym trainer’s residence. Two days later, Deoraj Malik approached police and lodged a formal complaint. Mahant alleges ‘property jihad’ Yashveer Maharaj claimed the case was not merely “love jihad” but also a case of “property jihad” aimed at grabbing assets worth ₹60-70 crore. He alleged that Chandni Qureshi had extracted nearly ₹1.5 crore from Ayush and suggested the conspiracy could have links to religious figures in Delhi, Mumbai and Pakistan. Ayush had earlier said conversion was his own decision Before the latest developments, Ayush Malik alias Rahman had publicly defended his decision to embrace Islam. He stated that nobody had pressured him into converting and that he accepted Islam of his own free will. He said his parents continued their Hindu religious practices while he offered namaz five times a day and maintained a beard because it is considered Sunnah in Islam. Ayush claimed he had been studying Islam and Muslim traditions for around 13 years and had married Chandni Qureshi under Islamic customs four years ago. He said the marriage was initially kept secret because his sister had not yet been married. He also said he had been learning about Islam since his school days and became more deeply interested around 2012–13. According to him, he watched videos of Pakistani Islamic scholar Dr Israr Ahmed, which further strengthened his interest in the faith. Ayush maintained that he never visited temples regularly because he already felt drawn towards Islam. He insisted that neither Chandni nor her family pressured him into converting and that the decision was entirely his own. He acknowledged that his family was unhappy about his conversion but said it remained his personal choice. He added that he had hidden the conversion for some time due to family circumstances, particularly his sister’s pending marriage, before publicly revealing it earlier this year. Ayush further said that while Islam considers lying a sin, it allows a person to conceal certain matters if circumstances are hostile or if disclosure could cause harm. He said this was one reason he initially kept the conversion private. He also stated that both his own family and Chandni’s family were equally important to him and that he would not abandon either side. Referring to the allegations against Chandni and her father, Ayush said he would stand by them and support them with what he described as the truth. At the time, he had declared that he was happy as a Muslim and had no intention of changing his religion again, regardless of external pressure. Pictures of accused Chandni Qureshi Father had alleged years of brainwashing Deoraj Malik had earlier alleged that his son had been brainwashed over several years and that the process was part of a planned effort. He claimed Ayush was once a well-mannered and devoted son but changed completely after coming into contact with Chandni Qureshi and others. He alleged that money had been extracted from Ayush for years and named several individuals, including local clerics, as part of the conspiracy. He also claimed he received threatening messages demanding property transfers and money, along with warnings that the family could be implicated in criminal cases. Despite the dispute, Deoraj had repeatedly said he hoped his son would eventually return to Hinduism and reunite with the family.

stories.title: Dehradun BJP leader’s murder sparks unrest:Stones hurled at media, police; 3 houses, 1 tractor torched; ITBP deployed to restore order
stories.summary: Tension remained high in Bairagiwala village of Dehradun late into the evening following the murder of BJP leader Vinod Kumar. After incidents of arson, stone-pelting and police baton charge earlier in the day, the administration deployed ITBP personnel, PAC units and heavy police forces to bring the situation under control. Continuous flag marches are being carried out in the area. A protest on the Dehradun–Herbertpur Highway has been continuing for several hours. Police and administrative officials are holding talks with the victim’s family members and villagers, who are staging a sit-in on the road. However, the family has remained firm on its demand for strict action against the accused and says the protest will end only after concrete action is taken. The administration has already carried out bulldozer action on the main accused’s shop and boundary wall. A case has been registered against 12 named accused and several others in connection with the murder. So far, four accused have been arrested. The entire dispute in 6 points Six key points of the case 1. Dispute over money and irrigation water: According to the victim’s family, tensions existed over a ₹14,000 payment related to shuttering work and a disagreement over drawing water from a tubewell. 2. Armed group allegedly attacked family: The family alleges that 15–20 people armed with shovels, hammers and other weapons stormed Vinod’s house and field and carried out the assault. 3. One dead, three seriously injured: Vinod died from severe head injuries, while his brother Rajesh Kumar, Ashok and Sushma sustained serious injuries and are undergoing treatment. 4. Protesters demanded arrests and bulldozer action: Following the murder, villagers and Hindu organisation members refused to allow the body to be moved until arrests were made and action was taken against the accused. 5. MLA issued warning to police: MLA Munna Singh Chauhan said complaints had previously been made against criminal elements in the area and warned that any police officer found negligent would face action. 6. Massive security deployment: PAC personnel and police forces from multiple stations were deployed under the supervision of SP Rural Pankaj Gairola to prevent further violence and maintain law and order. Officials continue to appeal for peace, while security forces remain on high alert across the area. Highway partially reopened, talks with family continue The administration has partially reopened the Dehradun–Herbertpur Highway amid a protest that had blocked the road for several hours. Police and administrative officials are continuing talks with the family of slain BJP leader Vinod Kumar, urging them to end the sit-in. However, the family remains firm that the protest will continue until concrete action is taken against all the accused. Earlier, officials warned protesters to clear the highway or face police action. ITBP personnel and police teams carried out flag marches in the area as authorities worked to restore normalcy. The highway remained blocked for nearly five hours, with protesters placing stones on the road and refusing to allow vehicles to pass. Demonstrations also affected the Himachal Pradesh and Yamunotri routes for several hours. CM Dhami assures strict action Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami said the accused would not be spared. Local MLA Munna Singh Chauhan said the Chief Minister was continuously monitoring the situation and assured strict action against everyone involved in the murder and subsequent violence. Father alleges mob attack over payment dispute Vinod Kumar’s father alleged that two men arrived at their house carrying hammers on Saturday and began abusing family members while Vinod was carrying out plaster work with a mason. He claimed the men then called around 60–70 people, including 20–25 youths, who allegedly surrounded the family and attacked Vinod with wooden planks and hammers. According to him, the dispute stemmed from ₹16,000–17,000 allegedly owed for shuttering material hired about a year ago. He said tensions escalated after a mason demanded payment from the accused a few days earlier. The father also accused police of ignoring previous complaints and claimed this was the fifth attack by the same group. He demanded the strictest possible action against the main accused. Wife, mother among grieving family members As tensions escalated, Vinod Kumar’s wife was seen approaching the accused persons’ houses and allegedly throwing bricks. Police later escorted her away from the area. Family members said Vinod’s mother repeatedly lost consciousness after learning of his death. Who was Vinod Kumar? Vinod Kumar, also known as Vinod Kashyap, was a resident of Bairagiwala village in Sahaspur, Dehradun. He was an RTI activist and district media in-charge of the BJP OBC Morcha. The eldest of three brothers, he is survived by his wife and two daughters aged three and six. He sustained severe head injuries during Saturday evening’s attack, allegedly triggered by a dispute over irrigation water, and was declared dead at hospital. See the pictures- RTI activism angle raised Village head Vicky Kashyap claimed Vinod had been receiving threats for nearly a year because he had filed RTI applications regarding alleged encroachment on village land. He said the murder appeared to be pre-planned and could not be explained by a simple dispute over irrigation water alone. Police launch crackdown, village sealed Authorities sealed the village and deployed heavy police and PAC personnel following the violence. Bulldozers were used to demolish structures linked to the accused, while police continued search operations. Dehradun SSP Pramod Singh Dobal said the clash began over irrigation water between two groups in Bairagiwala village. He confirmed that Vinod Kumar died after being attacked and that several others were injured. A case has been registered against 12 named accused and 30–40 unidentified persons under serious charges. Four accused have been arrested so far, while teams continue raids to apprehend others. SP Crime Jitendra Chaudhary said police acted immediately after receiving the complaint and formed multiple teams to trace the accused. He added that further arrests would be announced as soon as they are made. Arson, stone-pelting and highway blockade The murder triggered widespread unrest across the area. Crowds allegedly set fire to houses, shops and a tractor linked to the accused. Thick smoke was visible from nearly half a kilometre away as fire brigade teams battled the flames. Stone-pelting incidents were also reported, with police personnel and journalists seen taking cover behind walls. Several people demanded police encounters against the accused, while angry villagers confronted senior officers and local leaders during the protest.

stories.title: Delhi IPS officer reaches Ayodhya to probe donation theft:₹2 crore recovered, 5 questioned; Katiyar says, ‘All are thieves'
stories.summary: Ayodhya Ram Temple’s alleged ₹7-crore donation theft controversy has intensified, with Samajwadi Party MP Awadhesh Prasad on Sunday demanding that trust office-bearers facing allegations be removed from their posts until the investigation is completed. He also called for the current trust committee to be dissolved and replaced with a new arrangement. Prasad said the entire matter should be investigated under the supervision of judges of the Supreme Court of India. Earlier on Saturday, BJP leader Vinay Katiyar, who was associated with the Ram Temple movement, had said, “Everyone here is a thief. Remove them. Who will remove them? Vinay Katiyar will.” According to sources, the Central Government had sent an IPS officer to Ayodhya three days ago. A confidential inquiry into the alleged donation theft is reportedly being conducted under his supervision. However, officials have remained tight-lipped on the matter. Members of the SIT constituted to probe the case were also expected to reach Ayodhya by Sunday night. So far, five names — Lavkush, Avneesh, Anukalp, Karune and Ramashankar — have surfaced in connection with the alleged theft. Around ₹2 crore has been recovered based on information provided by them. All five were associated with the counting of donations. The recoveries made so far were facilitated by these individuals, who have also reportedly confessed to the theft. Lavkush and Anukalp are currently in police custody. SP MP demands impartial probe Speaking to the media at a hotel in Ayodhya, Awadhesh Prasad said the Ram Temple is a centre of faith for millions of Hindus and allegations related to donations and offerings are extremely serious. He said issues raised by SP chief Akhilesh Yadav are not merely political but are linked to the sentiments of crores of devotees. Therefore, the matter should be investigated in a fair and transparent manner. Prasad said all those facing allegations, including Champat Rai, should be kept away from the temple and the entire matter until the investigation is completed. He added that the exact amount allegedly misappropriated is still unclear, making an impartial probe essential. He further alleged that a lack of transparency in such a sensitive matter could erode public trust and said the truth should be established through an investigation at the highest level. Vinay Katiyar said - All these thieves will go to jail or flee Speaking to the media on Saturday, Vinay Katiyar said the alleged theft is a serious matter and not something that can be taken lightly. “People sacrificed their lives for this temple. People like us and Kalyan Singh went to jail. Kalyan Singh resigned, and only then did the temple construction begin. We will ask the DIG to arrest all of them and send them to jail,” he said. Katiyar added that those involved would either end up in jail or flee. Nripendra Mishra said- Government has formed SIT On Sunday, Nripendra Mishra attended a meeting of the Ram Temple Construction Committee in Ayodhya. Speaking to reporters at the Circuit House, Mishra said the government has constituted an SIT to investigate the alleged donation scam. He said the team will submit a preliminary report within a week and a final report within 15 days. Mishra also said a nearly 4-km-long modern boundary wall is being constructed around the temple complex to enhance security and beautification. Twenty-five watchtowers are also being built. The projects have been assigned to Engineers India Limited, with a target of completion by August 2026. He added that 20 galleries are being developed at the Ram Katha Museum. The brother-in-law duo in police custody 1. Lavkush: Worked at Ram Temple for 4–5 months Lavkush is a resident of Minapur Thakuran Phagauli village in the Rudauli area of Ayodhya. His father, Bachchulal, said his son had been working at the Ram Temple for the past four to five months. He said a team searching for evidence visited their home and recovered ₹10 lakh. “Whatever had to happen has happened now,” he said, adding that a house being constructed in Faizabad had no connection to his son and was being built using money raised by mortgaging 10–12 bighas of farmland. Villagers claimed six people had visited the house — two in police uniform and four in plain clothes. Cash was allegedly found in cupboards and trunks, while some money had reportedly been hidden in a heap of cow dung. Lavkush earlier worked as a car mechanic. Villagers claimed his financial condition improved rapidly after he got the temple job. They alleged he spent lavishly and once spent ₹50,000 at a liquor shop to treat villagers. Lavkush’s father works in the iron market in Ghaziabad. The family includes three daughters and one son, Lavkush. He married eight years ago and has a six-year-old son and a two-year-old daughter. 2. Anukalp Mishra: Temple employee Anukalp Mishra (20), Lavkush’s brother-in-law, is the son of property dealer Ravindra Mishra. The family has one son and two daughters. Anukalp lives with his family in Kaushalpuri, Ayodhya. Sources said the family purchased a house near Manas Dental Hospital for around ₹64–65 lakh from a Bhojpuri singer and later shifted there. A farmhouse has also reportedly been built around 300 metres from the family’s ancestral house in Baswa village of Inayatnagar. The family owns around 5–6 bighas of ancestral agricultural land. Government formed SIT, 3 officers included in it The SIT includes Lucknow Divisional Commissioner Vijay Vishwas Pant, IG Range Kiran S and Special Secretary (Finance) Neelratan. Pant will chair the SIT and examine the donation and offering management system. Kiran S., who has extensive experience in criminal investigations, will probe the theft allegations from the policing angle. Neelratan will oversee financial scrutiny, audits and donation-related transactions. Vijay Vishwas Pant: A B.Tech graduate from IIT Kanpur, currently serving as Lucknow Divisional Commissioner. He will chair the SIT, study the donation and offering management system and suggest improvements. Kiran S.: Has extensive experience in criminal investigations and will examine the theft allegations from the policing perspective. Neelratan: As Special Secretary in the Finance Department, he will scrutinise temple audits, donations and financial transactions and prepare a report. SP leader Pawan Pandey said - Those responsible should resign on moral grounds Former minister and SP leader Pawan Pandey released a video on Saturday. He said Mahipal Singh, who was associated with the RSS, had levelled allegations of theft and robbery involving temple donations. Therefore, an impartial investigation should be conducted. Pandey said all trustees and office-bearers named by Mahipal Singh should resign on moral grounds. “The Ram Temple is linked to the faith of crores of people and the identity of the nation. Therefore, transparency is essential in this matter,” he said. “If those responsible do not resign and refuse to face the investigation, it will be assumed that they are partners in the robbery of Lord Ram’s offerings. They are beneficiaries of the loot.” “This is Ayodhya. Even Lord Ram had to undergo trials. When allegations were made against Sita, she had to go into exile. These people engage in politics in Lord Ram’s name day and night. If they stop taking Lord Ram’s name, perhaps they would lose their deposits in elections. If they invoke Ram 24 hours a day, they should also follow his ideals in their own lives.” PIL filed in High Court for CBI investigation A Public Interest Litigation (PIL) was filed before the Lucknow Bench of the Allahabad High Court on Friday seeking a CBI investigation into the alleged theft of temple donations. The petition was filed by local advocate Mohit Ashok. The PIL seeks a CBI inquiry into the alleged theft and also demands that the donations be audited by the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG). The matter is likely to come up for hearing next week. How the Controversy Began Former SP minister Pawan Pandey had claimed on 7 June that between ₹5 crore and ₹7.5 crore had been stolen from Ram Temple donations. Akhilesh Yadav had also questioned the government’s silence, saying the courts should examine the matter. Champat Rai had rejected the allegations, saying no such issue had come to light. As the controversy intensified, BJP leader Dr Rajneesh Singh wrote to the Prime Minister on 9 June seeking a CBI inquiry. The following day, the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) sought a report from the temple trust. Ram Temple donation counting system and alleged loopholes Donations received at the Ram Temple are counted daily under CCTV surveillance. Alleged loophole: Ordinary devotees cannot witness the counting process and CCTV footage is not made public. After counting, the money is entered into registers and stored in lockers inside the temple premises. The amount is deposited in a bank the following day. Alleged loophole: No regular public disclosure is made regarding the amount of donations received. The Ram Temple Trust periodically shares donation figures during its meetings. During the last trust meeting held in December 2025, it was disclosed that total donations received since the trust’s formation had reached ₹4,575 crore. Alleged loophole: There is no public information about how much donation has been received between December 2025 and June 2026. In most major temples across India, audits are conducted either by internal bodies or government agencies. For example, donations at the Shirdi Sai Baba Temple are audited by the Maharashtra Government’s Local Fund Audit Department. Alleged loophole: At the Ram Temple, the entire audit process is handled by Tata Consultancy Services, a private company.

stories.title: Six youths drown in separate incidents:Rewa, Jabalpur and Gwalior incidents leave grieving families across MP, UP Bihar
stories.summary: Six men lost their lives in three separate drowning incidents across Madhya Pradesh over the weekend. Two friends each drowned while bathing in the Tamas River in Rewa and the Narmada River in Jabalpur, while two MBBS students died after slipping into deep water at Tigra Dam in Gwalior. The victims included two residents of Uttar Pradesh, one resident of Bihar, and three from Madhya Pradesh. Authorities have recovered all six bodies. Two youths from Uttar Pradesh drown in Rewa’s Tamas river The first incident occurred on Sunday at the Gaura stretch of the Tamas River in Rewa district, near the Madhya Pradesh–Uttar Pradesh border. Around six members of a family from Bharat Nagar in Shankargarh, Uttar Pradesh, had gone to the river for a bath. During the outing, Kunal Mishra (19) accidentally entered deep water and began drowning. Vishesh Mishra (18) jumped in to rescue him, but both were pulled under by the depth of the river. Villagers rushed to help after hearing cries for assistance and managed to rescue one individual safely. However, Kunal and Vishesh could not be saved. Their bodies were later recovered during a rescue operation. Locals said the accident site contains deep pits created by earlier stone-blasting activity, making the water deceptively dangerous. MP and UP police respond Police teams from Madhya Pradesh’s Chakghat station and Uttar Pradesh reached the scene, as the incident occurred near the inter-state boundary. Jurisdictional procedures are being followed for further legal action. Rescue attempt ends in double tragedy in Jabalpur In the second incident, Dhruv Patel (19) and Sagar Patel (17) drowned while bathing in the Narmada River at Silua Ghat in Jabalpur’s Gaur police outpost area. The two friends had visited the river with three others on Sunday morning. Dhruv reportedly drifted into deep water, prompting Sagar to enter the river in an attempt to rescue him. Both became trapped in a strong current and disappeared beneath the surface. Boatmen at the ghat and emergency responders launched rescue efforts after being alerted by their companions. Bodies recovered after three-hour search Police and State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) personnel conducted a search operation lasting nearly three hours before recovering both bodies approximately 50 metres from the site, lodged near rocks in the river. The bodies were sent for post-mortem examination, and an investigation is underway. Two MBBS students die at Gwalior’s Tigra dam The third incident involved Gopal Agrawal from Bina in Madhya Pradesh’s Sagar district and Ayush Srivastava from Muzaffarpur, Bihar, both second-year MBBS students at Gajra Raja Medical College in Gwalior. The pair had visited Tigra Dam on Saturday evening as part of a group of eight students. According to eyewitnesses, they entered the water near a restricted rocky area around 7 p.m. and reportedly slipped, losing their balance before being swept into deep water. Overnight rescue operation When the students failed to return, their friends searched the area and found their shoes and clothes neatly placed on the shore before informing the police. Rescue teams comprising police personnel, SDRF members, and local divers recovered Gopal’s body late Saturday night. Ayush’s body was found the following afternoon, trapped among rocks and bushes nearly 50 feet below the water’s surface. Promising medical student had cleared NEET on first attempt Family members said Gopal Agrawal was the youngest among five siblings and had successfully cleared the NEET examination on his first attempt in 2024 to pursue his dream of becoming a doctor. His education was reportedly supported by his elder brother, and he often expressed his desire to become a doctor and support his family in return. His untimely death has left the family devastated. Ayush Srivastava’s family was informed immediately after the incident and travelled from Bihar to Gwalior. Medical college dean calls incident an irreparable loss Dr. R.K.S. Dhakad, Dean of Gajra Raja Medical College, described the tragedy as deeply painful, stating that the institution had lost two bright and promising students. He said the incident had caused immense grief to both the college community and the families of the deceased, calling it a loss that could not be compensated.

stories.title: ‘Switch off cameras, return the offerings’:Akhilesh calls Ram Temple probe a ‘misfortune’; says Lord Ram will forgive
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav on Sunday said it was unfortunate that government officials would now investigate the Ram Temple and saints following allegations of theft in temple offerings. “After allegations of theft in donations made to the Ram Temple, it is unfortunate that officials will now investigate the temple and saints. What could be more unfortunate for Sanatan Dharma? This is an insult to Sanatan Dharma. If something has happened, switch off the cameras, sit together and resolve it. Return the offerings and Lord Ram will forgive you,” he said. Taking a swipe at the controversy, Akhilesh added, “Switch off the cameras and the lights. In front of Lord Ram, someone will automatically return the offerings. Put the donations back and Lord Ram will forgive you.” The remarks came after the Uttar Pradesh government constituted a Special Investigation Team (SIT) to probe the alleged theft of donations at the Ram Temple. The SIT includes IAS officer Vijay Vishwas Pant, IPS officer Kiran S., and Finance Department Special Secretary Neelratan. Akhilesh was speaking at the Vision India programme in Agra before addressing a press conference. He also mocked the allocation of the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) portfolio to minister Bhupendra Chaudhary. “He is such a senior leader, and what department did he get? ‘Micro’. That too when there is no budget in it,” he remarked. Akhilesh on early Assembly Poll speculation Responding to speculation about early Assembly elections in Uttar Pradesh, Akhilesh said: “Those who are unable to conduct village head elections, will they hold Assembly elections in November? They are trying to confuse people. They think by talking about November they can understand the Samajwadi Party’s strategy. We are not going to reveal our strategy. I want to tell the younger generation that only the Samajwadis can find the path for Uttar Pradesh’s development.” He also said he wanted Agra’s famous petha sweet to achieve global recognition. Akhilesh's 4 big points- 1- Fake encounter conducted in Ghazipur Commenting on the encounter of Kamlesh Bind in Ghazipur, Akhilesh alleged that it was a fake encounter. “The government is an expert in fake encounters. The victims of such encounters are mostly PDA people. Even people within the system say the current arrangement is the worst. Since the commissionerate system was introduced, it has become a system of loot. The police have increased their rates,” he claimed. 2- Fire set to EVMs in Bengal due to fear of secrets being revealed Referring to reports of an EVM-related fire in West Bengal, Akhilesh alleged that the incident was aimed at preventing secrets from being exposed. “There was a fear that certain facts would come out, so the fire was set. BJP leaders get fires started to vacate land. First it happened in Lucknow and then in Ghaziabad,” he alleged. On the Congress preparing for all 403 Assembly seats, he said: “If they are preparing for all 403 seats and we are also preparing for all 403 seats, then it means double preparation. Together, with this double preparation, we will defeat the BJP.” 3- BJP practices negative politics Responding to Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath’s recent remarks about his supporters, Akhilesh said he did not want to engage in negative politics. “I do not want to discuss that issue because the BJP practises negative politics. It spends crores of rupees on it. Before 2017, even journalists did not know much about Yogi ji. He had no major identity,” he said. On Saturday, Chief Minister Yogi had said: “Akhilesh ji advises others. He should also advise his followers to exercise restraint in their language and think before making comments.” 4- 500 primary schools closed in Agra Akhilesh claimed that the BJP had already lost public support in Uttar Pradesh and would now resort to unfair practices. “Five hundred primary schools have closed in Agra. If McDonald’s and Pizza Hut can reach countries across the world, why can’t Agra’s petha?” he asked. He also offered a new expansion of the PDA acronym, saying it stood for “Prem (love), Daya (compassion) and Apnapan (affection).” “The more love, compassion and affection there is in society, the faster the state will progress,” he said.

stories.title: Elderly man shoots cancer-patient wife, then kills self:Daughter says he was worried about going to jail in embezzlement case
stories.summary: In a shocking incident in Firozabad on Saturday night, the son of former Congress MLA Jagdish Yadav allegedly shot dead his wife before taking his own life. According to the family, he had been under severe stress after attending a court hearing earlier in the day in connection with an embezzlement case. The couple’s daughter said her father had returned from court deeply disturbed and repeatedly worried about who would look after his cancer-stricken wife if he were sent to jail. According to the family, the incident took place around 9:15 pm. The daughters heard a gunshot from their mother’s room and rushed inside, only to find both parents lying in pools of blood. After post-mortem examinations, the bodies of Rakesh Yadav (67) and his wife Rammoorti Devi (66) were brought back to their village on Sunday morning. Both daughters broke down on seeing the bodies. The husband and wife were cremated on adjacent pyres, with their nephew Gaurav Yadav performing the last rites. Daughter Garima says father was depressed for years Daughter Garima Yadav said her mother had been battling cancer for a long time, while her father had been suffering from depression for the past two years. She said that in May 2025, former village head and Rakesh Yadav’s cousin Rahul Yadav had filed a case alleging embezzlement of ₹2.5 lakh. The complaint accused him of misappropriating income from agricultural land belonging to a school and of becoming its manager through fraudulent means. According to Garima, the case further increased her father’s mental stress. SHO Anuj Kumar Rana said preliminary investigation suggests the incident appears to be a case of a man killing his wife before ending his own life. However, police are examining all possible angles and recording statements of relatives and close associates. See 3 pictures- Left police job when he became MLA Rakesh Yadav, a resident of Dahini village, was the son of former Congress MLA Jagdish Yadav, who represented the constituency between 1980 and 1985. Rakesh later lived at Subhash Tiraha in Shikohabad. He married Rammoorti Devi, daughter of landlord Chintamani Yadav of Kanaua village in Jasrana, in 1972. The couple had two daughters, both of whom are married. Rakesh was appointed as a sub-inspector in Uttar Pradesh Police in 1979. However, after his father became an MLA in 1980, he resigned from the force and entered politics. He later became village head of Dahini and contested the Shikohabad Assembly seat in 1991 and 1993 on a Janata Dal ticket during the tenure of late Mulayam Singh Yadav. He also served as manager of Adarsh Krishna Inter College. Nephew had filed ₹2.5 lakh embezzlement case According to officials, around 35 bighas of agricultural land belonging to Adarsh Krishna Inter College had been leased to a villager named Arjun Singh Yadav. Allegations later emerged that the land remained under occupation even after the lease period ended. In May 2025, following a court order, former village head, advocate and Rakesh Yadav’s nephew Rahul Yadav filed an embezzlement case against him. The complaint alleged misappropriation of income from the school’s agricultural land and questioned his appointment as manager. Shot wife in the chest, then took his own life Rakesh Yadav had attended a court hearing in the same case on Saturday. According to police, after returning home, he allegedly shot his wife in the chest with his licensed revolver before shooting himself in the head. Family members rushed to the room after hearing gunshots. Both were taken to the Shikohabad Community Health Centre. Doctors declared Rakesh Yadav dead on arrival, while Rammoorti Devi was referred to a medical college, where she later succumbed to her injuries. Police reached the scene soon after receiving information and launched an investigation. A forensic team collected evidence, and the licensed revolver was recovered from the spot. Daughter said - My cousin brother ruined my family Garima Yadav alleged that the legal case filed by her cousin Rahul Yadav had devastated the family. She claimed her father had been depressed for the last two years and believed the allegations against him were false. According to her, he feared severe punishment if convicted and had become increasingly anxious despite securing bail. Father had refused to go to court Garima said the family had little understanding of legal procedures and received no support from relatives. She recalled that before the court hearing on June 12, she had offered to accompany her father. He reportedly told her not to come, saying she should stay with her child rather than get involved in court proceedings. According to her, he returned from court visibly distressed and later carried out the fatal act. Father used to talk about going to Nepal Garima further said her father often spoke about selling all the family’s property and moving elsewhere, even mentioning Nepal as a possible destination. Family members tried to reassure him that he had committed no crime, but he remained worried that the case had tarnished the reputation of a family once represented by an MLA. Both daughters married, lived alone with wife Rakesh and Rammoorti Yadav had two daughters — Pratima Yadav and Garima Yadav. Pratima works as a government school teacher. After both daughters got married, the elderly couple had been living alone.

stories.title: Clashes erupt between NSUI workers and police in Lucknow:Activist faints, protesters allege lathi blow; demonstrators attempt Raj Bhavan march
stories.summary: A fierce clash broke out between NSUI workers and police in Lucknow during a protest over the paper leak issue. During the scuffle, one activist fainted and was rushed to hospital by four to five fellow workers. NSUI members were marching to gherao Jan Bhavan over the paper leak issue when police stopped them outside the Congress office with a four-layer barricade. The protesters climbed onto the barricades and began raising slogans. The demonstration was being led by NSUI National President Vinod Jakhar. Vinod Jakhar said: "Even before today's protest began, NSUI workers in Uttar Pradesh were placed under house arrest. A large police force was deployed outside our hotel. This clearly shows the fear within the BJP government. It appears the government is protecting the paper mafia." Workers accompanying the unconscious activist alleged that police struck him on the head with a baton, causing him to collapse. See 5 pictures- “We were treated like animals” Rana Sudhanshu Sharma, President of the Lucknow University NSUI unit who participated in the protest, levelled serious allegations against the police. He said, “These policemen may themselves be victims of paper leaks. Their children must also be studying. Yet they treated us like animals. We were beaten during the protest, our clothes were torn and abusive language was used against us.” Clash erupts between NSUI workers and police NSUI activists and police personnel repeatedly pushed each other during the protest, leading to several flashpoints and clashes. Protesters attempted to cross the barricades and march towards Raj Bhavan, triggering a major confrontation with police. Officers pushed demonstrators back as tensions escalated. During the clash, one activist reportedly fainted and was taken to hospital by fellow protesters. Reporter Faridul Hasan said the worker was from Delhi. Protesters also climbed all four layers of police barricades while waving flags and raising slogans. The barricades were damaged during the demonstration. NSUI National President Vinod Jakhar was seen leading the march and standing on the barricades along with party workers and office-bearers. Congress alleges suppression of protest Congress spokesperson Sachin alleged that the government was frightened and trying to suppress the protest. “This government is scared. Our office has been turned into a fortress. Forces have been deployed everywhere. Our workers are being dragged away and misbehaved with,” he claimed. See images from the protest Heavy security, house arrest allegations Ahead of the protest, a large number of police personnel were deployed outside the Congress office, while a four-layer barricading system was set up around 100 metres away on the route leading to Raj Bhavan. Amethi Youth Congress district president Shubham Singh was also reportedly placed under house arrest in Amethi at midnight. Sharing a video on social media, he said they wanted to raise their voice for students but were prevented from doing so. Jakhar demands resignation of Education Ministers NSUI National President Vinod Jakhar said the organisation had come to Lucknow with a clear message that the BJP government had failed to conduct examinations fairly in Uttar Pradesh and across the country. Referring to the NEET paper leak issue, he said students were on the streets protesting and demanded the resignation of both the Uttar Pradesh Education Minister and Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan. Claims of political protection for paper leak accused Jakhar alleged that NSUI workers in several districts of Uttar Pradesh had been placed under house arrest before the protest and that a large police force had been deployed outside their hotel. He claimed the BJP government was afraid and accused it of protecting the paper leak mafia. He further alleged that photographs showing alleged paper leak accused with the Chief Ministers of Maharashtra and Rajasthan indicated political patronage for those involved. Compensation, NTA ban among key demands Jakhar said NSUI leaders had met families who lost their children due to the paper leak issue and shared their grief. According to him, many families had been intimidated, making it difficult to contact them. He added that Rahul Gandhi had provided economic and emotional support to some of the affected families. Jakhar demanded ₹5 crore compensation for the families of deceased students, free education for their siblings, a ban on the NTA and the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan. ‘The protest will definitely continue’ NSUI state president Anas Rahman said the protest would continue despite police action. He said Congress workers from across Uttar Pradesh were reaching Lucknow to raise the concerns of students and unemployed youth. “We are soldiers of Rahul Gandhi and we will not stop. This protest will definitely happen,” he said, adding that party workers would march towards Raj Bhavan to strengthen the voice of students and unemployed youth.

stories.title: Owaisi arrives in Lucknow to ‘Sher aa gaya’ slogans:AIMIM eyes 200 seats in UP elections; BJP dismisses move
stories.summary: AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi will hold a rally in Matera, Bahraich on Sunday. Owaisi arrived in Lucknow on Sunday morning to participate in the rally. Supporters raised slogans at the airport, ‘Sher aaya sher aaya’ Owaisi has a program from 5 PM to 10 PM in Matera assembly constituency of Bahraich, SP's stronghold. He will address a public meeting at Shankarpur Chowk. During this, he may announce contesting elections on 200 seats in the UP Assembly elections. Party's state president Shaukat Ali had hinted at this on Friday after reaching Bahraich. He had said - The party will contest elections on 200 seats, however the final decision will be taken by the national president. Deputy CM's taunt on rally, ‘Their plan is not going to work’ Deputy CM Brajesh Pathak said on Owaisi's UP tour - These are people who do polarization politics. These are people who do politics on the basis of religion and caste, their plan is not going to work. BJP has succeeded in taking PM Modi's welfare schemes for the poor to every person under 'Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas and Sabka Vishwas'. The blessings of every person are with Prime Minister Modi. Why did Owaisi choose Matera in Bahraich There are two reasons for this. First- Matera assembly seat is considered Muslim-dominated. The population of Muslim voters on this seat is approximately 45%. The total number of voters here is more than approximately 3.4 lakh. The number of Muslim voters is between about 1.5 lakh to 1.55 lakh. SP has held this seat continuously for three times. Currently, SP's Maria Shah is the MLA from here. Before this, her husband Yasar Shah has also been MLA from this seat twice. Second- In Bahraich, in the 11th century (around 1033-1034 AD), a historic battle took place between Maharaja Suheldev (King of Shravasti) and Syed Salar Masud Ghazi (Ghazi Mian), the nephew of Mahmud Ghaznavi. In this battle, Maharaja Suheldev killed Salar Masud. After Ghazi Mian's death, his tomb was built in Bahraich city. This dargah is a major historical-religious site of the region. The dargah of Salar Masud Ghazi has influence in areas adjacent to the Matera region. The Jeth fair and annual Urs held at Syed Salar Masud Ghazi's dargah had been banned. stories.title: Dimple Yadav on Aditi remark row: ‘BJP created this controversy’:Accuses party of personal attacks to deviate from Ram Mandir issue
stories.summary: “Aditi bitiya ke liye jo bayanbaazi hui hai, usse bahut pareshan hain. Ye BJP wale hi keh rahe hain. Ye saare log aap logon ko bargala rahe hain. Jo bayanbaazi hui hai, woh BJP ke logon ne hi karvai hai. Lekin humein apna dhyan nahi bhatakana hai, kyunki iske peeche asal wajah Ram Mandir mein hui chori hai. Usi se dhyan hatane ke liye yeh mudda uthaya gaya hai.” Dimple Yadav reacted for the first time to the case involving objectionable remarks made against her daughter. She was speaking on Saturday during the inauguration of Samajwadi Party leader Dr Naval Kishore Shakya’s Empire Resort. Akhilesh Yadav also posted on X, saying, “The root of this conspiracy is not far away, so there will be no need to go far to take real action. If the police are unable to identify the culprit, we can help.” The remarks are being seen as a response to Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath’s statement made earlier on Saturday in Azamgarh. Referring to the controversy, the Chief Minister had said, “A daughter is a daughter. No derogatory remark will be tolerated.” Political observers believe that both Dimple Yadav and Akhilesh Yadav were reacting directly to the Chief Minister’s statement and the ongoing controversy surrounding the remarks against Aditi. First, read what the CM had said “A daughter is a daughter, and she should be respected. I was seeing in recent days that some people had made inappropriate comments against the daughter of the SP chief. I immediately told the police to register an FIR. No derogatory comment against a daughter will be tolerated.” said Yogi Adityanath. "We have grown up in a culture where it is said that the daughter of the village is everyone's daughter, the sister of the village is everyone's sister. We have not discriminated. Akhilesh ji, if you preach to others, then preach to your followers as well to exercise some restraint in their language. They should also think before making comments," he said. “What kind of language do SP people use towards sisters, deceased people, senior leaders, daughters, and elders? Akhilesh ji, explain it to them. If they don't understand, then hand them over to us, we will make them understand,” Yogi added. Dimple said - No need to divert attention Mainpuri MP Dimple said, “When a daughter is burnt in Hathras, these people do not come forward. When a daughter's father is beaten to death in the police station in Kanpur, did these people say anything? Such big heinous incidents happen, but not a single person from BJP comes forward. Therefore, there is no need to divert attention.” FIR against 4 in Aditi Yadav comment case An FIR was registered in Kanpur-Pratapgarh on Thursday in the case of objectionable posts on social media regarding Aditi Yadav (23). In Kanpur, a case was registered against Bharat Patel, Nageshwar Singh Baghel, and Vinod Yadav on the complaint of Praveen Yadav, National Secretary of the Advocates' Council. Additionally, in Pratapgarh, a case was registered against an ID named Sheetla Sujan Kavi on the complaint of SP General Secretary Abdul Qadir Jilani. All four are accused of making objectionable posts against Aditi on social media. This tarnished the image of Akhilesh Yadav and his family in society. SP leader filed an application in court in Prayagraj This matter has reached the court in Prayagraj. Former SP district president Yogesh Chandra Yadav has filed an application in the ACJM court. It has been stated that the related posts and comments are not only damaging to the reputation of individuals, but can also create an atmosphere of ill-will and tension in society. Such social media accounts should be identified and action should be taken against their operators. SP chief Akhilesh Yadav had said- This is happening because the two people sitting at the top. They don't have a family, only family members understand the pain of other family members. Those sitting on the chair have no concern for families. stories.title: Haryanvi dancer alleges UP police protecting accused:Claims pressure bribery; seeks justice from Yogi govt
stories.summary: The Haryanvi dancer has expressed strong dissatisfaction with the Uttar Pradesh Police over the alleged waist-touching incident during a stage performance in Hathras on June 3, claiming that the matter has been “whitewashed.” She released a video stating that police initially acted on the basis of a viral clip and detained members of the organising committee, even though she had not filed any complaint at that time. She said that she was later contacted by the police and called to the police station, where she was asked to lodge a formal complaint. Despite doing so, she alleged that no concrete action was taken. She has now said she will seek justice from Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath. According to officials, a case under Section 74 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) has been registered at Sasni police station based on her complaint. Hathras City CO Himanshu Mathur said the incident took place during a birthday event organised without permission by Devendrapal Singh and Shripal Singh, and that three people, including Devendrapal Singh, Shripal Singh and Suresh Kumar, have been arrested in the case. The dancer further alleged that despite identifying the accused, he is being protected. She claimed that police officials showed her the accused’s Aadhaar details at the station and were fully aware of his identity, yet no arrest was made initially. She also alleged influence and pressure from powerful individuals behind the delay in action. She further accused the police of pressuring her not to speak to the media or post on social media, claiming she and others were kept in separate rooms and isolated for days to prevent public communication. She also alleged that attempts were made to suppress the matter and that money was taken in exchange for a settlement to protect the accused, who she claimed is employed in a government job. The dancer also said that only those linked to event management have been arrested so far, while the main accused in the molestation case is still being shielded. However, Sasni police station in-charge Vipin Chaudhary rejected the allegations, calling them baseless. He said a chargesheet has already been filed and a copy was provided to the complainant. He added that the section invoked in the case is bailable and that the police acted promptly based on the viral video before registering the complaint and proceeding as per due process.
