stories.title: Ram Mandir caretaker denies theft allegations:Claims sons bought property; SIT formed over donation probe
stories.summary: The case of alleged theft of ₹7 crore in donations at the Ayodhya Ram Mandir is escalating, with the government constituting a three-member SIT to investigate the matter. Meanwhile, amid the allegations, sevak Krishna Dev Tiwari, also known as KD, has come forward and strongly denied all charges against him. In an exclusive conversation with Dainik Bhaskar, he said that the allegations regarding the purchase of land worth ₹1.5 crore are completely false. He clarified that the Pran Pratishtha ceremony at the Ram Mandir took place on January 22, 2024, and he began his service as a sevak from March 2024. He further stated that before joining temple service, in December 2023, both his sons had purchased land in their own names. Therefore, he said, linking these property transactions to his role at the temple is incorrect. What else did KD Tiwari say, read on... I used to weigh the jewelry and give a receipt to the donor KD Tiwari said - My responsibility was only to collect gold-silver jewelry, other ornaments and gems donated by devotees in the temple premises. The work was to weigh the jewelry and give a receipt to the donor. Then there was the responsibility to safely deliver those jewels to the responsible officers of the trust. I have no information about what process is adopted with those jewels after that. Two sons are doing other jobs after retiring from the army KD Tiwari said - My eldest son is currently working in the Intelligence Bureau (IB) after retiring from the post of officer in the Indian Air Force. The second son retired from the army and is a Sub-Inspector in UP Police. The youngest son is a computer operator in Milkipur, while the daughter is a teacher. KD Tiwari also claimed that the house he is currently living in is in the name of his younger son. He said that he has been a teacher for a long time at Vidya Bharti's Saraswati Shishu Mandir in several districts. He is a resident of Gauran Ka Purwa in the district. Santosh Dubey said - Donation boxes have disappeared before as well Dharmasena chief and Babri demolition case accused Santosh Dubey has leveled serious allegations against some office bearers and employees of the trust. In a conversation with Dainik Bhaskar, he claimed that major irregularities occurred in the preservation of valuable stones, donations and other properties collected during the Ram Mandir movement. Santosh Dubey said - On December 6, 1992, during the Babri structure demolition, I was shot 4 times. I was in a coma for 22 days. Champat Rai's tenure has always been suspicious. He was also a co-accused in the Babri demolition case. He has been accused of misappropriation of donations before as well. Incidents like disappearance of donation boxes have happened earlier too. More than 1200 consecrated stones went missing Santosh Dubey said - During the Ram Mandir movement in 1989, consecrated stones were brought to Ayodhya from villages across the country. Apart from ordinary stones, these also included stones made of gold, silver, diamonds, rubies and other precious gems. He claims that he himself used to count these stones. They were kept safely. But in the year 2000, more than 1200 stones mysteriously disappeared. Dubey alleged that at that time, Champat Rai was responsible for looking after these stones. The late Paramhans Ramchandra Das also used to say that Champat Rai sold these stones. He had also complained about this to former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee. This theft is not recent, it is years old Santosh Dubey alleged that the series of alleged irregularities is not new, but has been going on for years. Champat Rai had also betrayed Ashok Singhal. The person who ordered firing on kar sevaks is today playing an important role in the Ram Temple management. Santosh Dubey also made allegations against Ram Shankar Yadav alias Tinnu Santosh Dubey said - Ram Shankar Yadav alias Tinnu earlier worked in the Vishwa Hindu Parishad office at a monthly salary of 2200 rupees. Later he started getting 3000 rupees. His allegation is that after the trust was formed, his salary increased to more than 22 thousand rupees. But, despite this, he has accumulated property worth crores of rupees. Dubey claimed that Tinnu Yadav bought several VIP vehicles in different names. He extorted large amounts of money from people in the name of getting VIP darshan passes made. A temple in the Santoshi Akhara premises was removed and a hotel was built there Santosh Dubey said - naming trust members Dr. Anil Mishra, Tinnu Yadav, Gopal Rao and Nripendra Mishra, he alleged that honesty cannot be expected in the presence of these people. He also claimed that Dr. Anil Mishra demolished a temple located in the Santoshi Akhara premises and built a hotel there. Whereas, it was located on the route leading to Ram Mandir. Trust is operating in an extremely secretive manner The scope of the investigation into claims of theft from Ram Mandir donations is continuously expanding. The entire operation is being conducted in an extremely confidential manner. So far, no FIR has been filed with the police in this matter. The Trust is carrying out the entire operation in a highly secretive way. The Trust is calling and interrogating those people whose names are coming to light. The suspect employees who have been caught and are being interrogated used to work in the same shift. In this context, there is talk of collusion to get duty assigned in one shift for those counting the donations. Rudauli resident Lavkush Mishra (27) and his brother-in-law Milkipur resident Anukalp Mishra (20) used to work in the same shift. Lavkush has purchased a plot worth 40 lakh rupees in Ayodhya, where a house is now being built. Meanwhile, Anukalp Mishra has purchased a house in Ayodhya for approximately 65 lakhs. The Trust recovered 10 lakh cash from Lavkush Mishra's house Lavkush Mishra is a resident of Minapur Thakuran Fagauli village in the Rudauli area of Ayodhya. His father Bachhulal said - My son had been working at Ram Temple for 4-5 months. During this time, a theft incident occurred there. Some people came to our house in connection with the investigation and conducted a search. During this, 10 lakh rupees were recovered. Now whatever had to happen, has happened. The house being built in Faizabad has no connection with my son. To build the house, I have mortgaged 10-12 bighas of land. Meanwhile, the father says that there were a total of 6 people in the team. Among them, 2 were in police uniform and 4 were in plain clothes. The money was kept in the cupboard-boxes at home, some money was hidden by burying it in cow dung. Lovkush was previously a car mechanic. After getting a job at the temple, his financial condition changed rapidly. When he came to the village, he would spend a lot of money. Once he spent 50 thousand rupees at a liquor shop to treat the villagers to drinks. Lovkush's father Bacchulal works in the iron market of Ghaziabad. Bacchulal has 3 daughters and one son, Lovkush. Lovkush got married 8 years ago. He has a 6-year-old son and a 2-year-old daughter. Anukalp Mishra built a farmhouse in the village, bought a house worth 65 lakhs in Ayodhya Anukalp Mishra (20), brother-in-law of Lavkush, has a father Ravindra Mishra who is a property dealer. He has one son and 2 daughters. The elder daughter is married. While the younger daughter is still studying. Anukalp lives with his family in Kaushalpuri, Ayodhya. According to sources, there is a house near Manas Dental Hospital in Kaushalpuri. This house previously belonged to a Bhojpuri singer. It was purchased by Anukalp Mishra's family for 64 to 65 lakh rupees. After this, the family started living there. Meanwhile, a farmhouse has also been built at a distance of about 300 meters from his house in Anukalp's ancestral village. At this very place, Shrimad Bhagavat Katha was held from April 23 to 30, 2026. Anukalp displayed his opulence at the Bhagavat Katha and wedding by distributing sarees. The family also has about 5 to 6 bighas of ancestral farmland. SIT formed to investigate Ram Temple donations The temple trust on Saturday demanded from CM Yogi that the theft claim be investigated by SIT (Special Investigation Team). Just a few hours later, the government formed a 3-member SIT. The SIT will submit a preliminary report in 7 days and a final report in 15 days. The SIT will also give suggestions to prevent further irregularities. Why these 3 officers were included The SIT includes Lucknow Commissioner Vijay Vishwas Pant (IAS), Kiran S. (IPS, IG Range) and Neelratan (Special Secretary, Finance). Kiran S. has served as DIG in CBI. This means the Commissioner will lead experts in finance and law. SP chief and former minister had raised the issue of theft Pawan Pandey, who has been a minister in the SP government, claimed on Sunday, June 7, that theft of 5 to 7.5 crore rupees has taken place from the Ram Temple. Akhilesh had also said that the government's silence on the matter is suspicious. The court should look into the matter. Champat Rai had clarified that no such thing has come to light so far. When the controversy escalated, BJP leader Dr. Rajnish Singh wrote a letter to the Prime Minister on June 9 demanding a CBI inquiry. The next day, i.e., on June 10, the Prime Minister's Office (PMO) sought a report on the matter from the temple trust.

stories.title: Storm alert in 21 UP districts:Winds up to 70 kmph, 5 deaths in 24 hours; monsoon likely by June 17
stories.summary: The pre-monsoon has become active in UP. On Sunday, most districts of the state have sunshine. Humidity and heat have increased. Today, there is a rain alert in 5 districts - Jalaun, Jhansi, Hamirpur, Mahoba and Lalitpur. Storm warnings have been issued in 21 cities. During this time, winds will blow at a speed of 60-70 km per hour. Lucknow meteorologist Atul Singh said - 'Western disturbance is active around Haryana. Due to this, pre-monsoon rains are occurring. By June 17, the monsoon can enter UP through Sonbhadra and Lalitpur routes. The monsoon will reach Lucknow by June 20. The monsoon has already reached Bihar.' Usually, the monsoon arrives in UP by June 20. This means the monsoon may arrive 3 days early this time. 5 die in last 24 hours In the last 24 hours, 5 people have died in storm and rain-related accidents. In Unnao and Ghazipur, one farmer each lost their lives due to lightning strikes. Meanwhile, in Kasganj, a husband, wife and daughter died when a house lintel fell during a storm. Talking about Saturday, it rained in 25 districts of the state. The highest rainfall was recorded at 6.8 mm in Shravasti and Siddharthnagar. Storms hit Prayagraj-Lucknow. Water entered homes in Kanpur. How will the weather be for the next 5 days

stories.title: How an auto driver entered the Ram Mandir's administration:Trust Secretary's close aide Tinnu Yadav under scrutiny over donation theft
stories.summary: Tinnu Yadav’s name has recently come under the spotlight following allegations linked to the theft of offerings at the Shri Ram Temple in Ayodhya. He is reportedly believed to be a close associate of Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust’s General Secretary, Champat Rai. At the same time, he is said to hold significant influence within the temple administration. According to reports, Tinnu Yadav has been involved in key operational responsibilities, including security management and the handling and deposition of offerings in banks. However, the Ram Temple Trust has not filed an FIR in the matter so far. Meanwhile, the government has constituted an SIT to investigate the alleged irregularities. In this special story, read how Tinnu Yadav, once an auto driver, became such an important figure in the Ramjanmabhoomi premises A VHP-associated official said that Tinnu’s full name is Ram Shankar Yadav. His father used to sell tea at Naya Ghat in Ayodhya. His journey reportedly began around 1994–95, when he worked as a tempo driver in the city. During this period, he came in contact with Mahesh Narayan, then minister of the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Mukti Yagya Samiti, who hired him as a driver. From there, he began visiting Karsevakpuram along with him. After Mahesh Narayan’s demise, Tinnu gradually came closer to Champat Rai and continued working in the Karsevakpuram ecosystem. Over time, he is said to have developed strong relations within the administrative circle and was considered a hardworking associate. Champat Rai was appointed regional organization minister in 1991, sent to Ayodhya, later became VHP central minister in 1996, and was made joint general secretary in 2002, eventually rising to international general secretary. Tinnu Yadav came into contact with him in 1998, and after Mahesh Narayan’s death on May 31, 2002, he continued working in various operational roles in Karsevakpuram, handling different vehicles including jeeps and cargo transport. This is when he is said to have become one of Champat Rai’s trusted aides. Following the Supreme Court’s 2019 verdict on the Ram Temple and the start of construction work, Tinnu began handling responsibilities on behalf of the Trust and was appointed as an internal salaried worker. His monthly salary is said to be around ₹16,000, though his influence within temple operations is considered more significant than his formal designation. He was also provided with communication equipment such as walkie-talkies used for security coordination. He has mainly been involved in manpower management within the temple premises. Several Trust insiders reportedly consider him one of the most trusted associates of General Secretary Champat Rai. A former accounts in-charge has alleged that Tinnu was responsible for depositing offerings from donation boxes into the bank. Around 14 donation boxes are installed in the temple premises, with daily offerings reportedly exceeding ₹1 crore, along with gold, silver, and diamond jewellery offered by devotees. The counting of offerings is conducted in a secured room under CCTV surveillance by nine people, including Trust officials, bank representatives, and TCS staff. Former accounts in-charge Mahipal Singh said that after counting, the cash was stored in a locker within the Ram Janmabhoomi premises and later taken to the bank by Tinnu for deposit. He also alleged that jewellery was often recorded only on an estimated basis without proper weighing, and claimed that Tinnu was seen photographing donated jewellery and sending images to Champat Rai. According to him, there is no clear record of such jewellery being deposited in the bank, although Tinnu has denied these allegations and stated that all cash and jewellery were duly deposited. Mahipal Singh further alleged irregularities in 2021 during the counting process, claiming that discrepancies were found in cash bundling. After his complaint, additional staff were deployed and he was later removed from counting duties. He also alleged that Tinnu, along with a private employee, deleted around eight months of CCTV footage. Shortly after these events, Mahipal resigned from his position, reportedly without taking any remuneration from the Trust. Tinnu's ancestral house is just 1.5 km away from Ram Temple After understanding Tinnu Yadav's character, we attempted to speak with him. Tinnu's ancestral home is in Swargdwari locality behind Tulsi Park. This place is only 1.5 km away from Ram Mandir. From the front, this house is about 7 feet wide. In the 3-story building, we met Tinnu's brother. During the conversation, we learned that Tinnu is about 55 years old. Of his 2 children, one daughter passed away 8 years ago. His only son Ravi Yadav works on contract in PWD. We got Tinnu's mobile number from his brother. Upon calling, we found out that he was at the Trust office in Shri Ram Mandir premises. He called us to meet him there. New locker installed in trust office Upon reaching Shri Ram Temple, our team reached the trust office mentioned by Tinnu. Demolition work was going on in one room. Brick pieces were being cleaned from inside. Trust General Secretary Champat Rai was sitting on a chair in the same room. Tinnu, former Sangh Prant Pracharak Bholendra and other employees were standing there. A new locker had also been installed in the room. Perhaps arrangements were being made to keep the cash and metals (gold-silver, diamonds-jewelry) coming out of donation boxes in this locker. Bhaskar team thrown out upon being spotted Trust employees did not let the Bhaskar team stay for long. They started questioning. Upon stating our identity, we were asked how we reached here? As soon as we took Tinnu's name, Bholendra brought us outside. He said that Tinnu is not here, he has gone towards Sita Rasoi. Our colleague also pointed out that you are misleading us, this is a good way to get us out. (At this, Bholendra kept smiling.) We said that Tinnu was present inside, where will he be found near Sita Rasoi? Anyway, he dropped us near Sita Rasoi. We called Tinnu, but he did not pick up the call. Tinnu's house has 14 rooms, all rented out After this, we reached the Naka area in search of Tinnu's new luxury house. Near the coaching center, we found his new 2-story house, which looked quite magnificent. Outside this house, we met a student. He told us - This house has 9 rooms on the ground floor. There are 5 rooms on the first floor. Boys live and study downstairs and girls upstairs. The rent for each room is 2700 rupees. We calculated based on the rooms, and the rent was coming to around 37 thousand rupees every month. This house is built on 1500 square feet of space. The location where this house was built, the land rate there is 2500-3000 rupees per square foot. Youth of the neighborhood said - Prospered after connecting with the temple People living here said that 5 months ago, Tinnu had his son's grand wedding in this house. He invited the entire neighborhood and acquaintances. He spent lavishly on the wedding. A young man from the neighborhood said - Ever since Tinnu Chacha got associated with the temple, he has made considerable progress. He also has a hostel near Nishad Raj Chowk. There is also talk that he has purchased 20 to 22 bighas of agricultural land in the Vikramjot area of Basti district. He has a house in Lucknow, where a Scorpio is kept. Here in the Ram Janmabhoomi premises, 3 vehicles run on contract. He receives rent from that. Now read what Tinnu has to say Tinnu spoke to Dainik Bhaskar on mobile. He answered several of our questions. Read them... Question- There are allegations of theft of offerings from Ram Mandir donation boxes? Tinnu- Stories are being fabricated just to defame. If anyone has any evidence, let them present it. The truth will come out. Question- The allegation is that in the last few years your own assets have become worth crores of rupees? Tinnu- One should also provide proof. Everything is online, you can check. Mine and my son's... Question- There is also an allegation that you got 2 bank employees appointed? Tinnu- This is wrong. Question- Everyone says that you are powerful here? Tinnu- No, no... Dr. Anil is here, Champat Rai is here, Gopalji is here. They are in charge. I am an employee. Here no one's word runs, only Ramji's. Question- It was said that you had CCTV deleted 8 months ago? Tinnu- It's all lies. No one has such power. Ask Dr. Anil and Champat Rai. You come, we will show you the footage. (However, upon reaching the premises, Tinnu did not come forward.)

stories.title: Dating app romance costs UP officer ₹25 lakh:Files case after woman refuses marriage
stories.summary: They say love is blind. But when someone falls in love through a dating app and starts spending lakhs of rupees without a second thought, the story can end up in court. Something similar happened to Deepanshu, an Assistant Director in Uttar Pradesh's Fisheries Department. He met a woman named Sunlight on a dating app. What began as friendship gradually turned into a romantic relationship, followed by promises of marriage. As the relationship deepened, Deepanshu not only opened his heart but also his wallet. The spending started with expensive gifts and monthly shopping trips and eventually escalated to the purchase of a plot in his girlfriend's name. According to the complaint, the officer spent ₹25,13,343 over a period of one-and-a-half years. The relationship, however, took a dramatic turn when the woman's family allegedly refused the marriage, claiming that Deepanshu had concealed his caste. The fallout has now reached the courts, with Deepanshu filing a case against the woman and several members of her family. In today's Sunday Big Story, let's understand this story from the beginning… Spent Rs 2 lakh on shopping in 5 months Deepanshu, a resident of Kanpur's Bilhaur area, joined the Uttar Pradesh Fisheries Department in 2023. His first posting was in Varanasi, and a year later he was transferred to Balrampur as an Assistant Director. It was during this period that he created a profile on the dating app TrulyMadly. On June 28, 2024, he connected with a woman named Sunlight through the app. A resident of Hardayalpur in Hardoi, Sunlight was then living in Prayagraj for her studies. What began as casual conversations soon developed into a friendship, and the two started meeting regularly. According to Deepanshu, he gave Sunlight ₹17,000 in cash on July 10, 2024. The following month, during another visit to Prayagraj, he spent ₹21,000 on shopping for her and gifted her a mobile phone worth ₹22,000. He claims he travelled from Balrampur to Prayagraj almost every month, bringing expensive gifts and financial assistance. The spending continued in September, when he bought Sunlight a lehenga, a weight-loss kit and an oxygen concentrator for her ailing father. Between July and December 2024 alone, Deepanshu alleges that he spent nearly ₹2 lakh on cash gifts and purchases for Sunlight. Took Rs 15 lakh personal loan and bought plot in girl's name By 2025, Deepanshu and Sunlight's friendship had turned into love. It was almost decided that the two would get married in the future. On January 28, Deepanshu bought a policy worth 6 lakh rupees annually in Sunlight's name. Sunlight had completed her D.El.Ed in 2019 and was waiting for a teacher recruitment. She expressed her desire to prepare for UPPSC to Deepanshu. Deepanshu agreed and spent one and a half lakh rupees to get her admission in a foundation course at a coaching institute in Prayagraj. Everything between the two was moving very fast. In the month of April, Deepanshu also bought land in Sunlight's name. This 1200 square feet plot was purchased in Takrohi, Lucknow. Sunlight's elder sister Moonlight became a witness in the registry. Deepanshu claims that a personal loan of Rs 15 lakh was taken for this land. Rs 70,000 were given separately for the boundary of the land. In July 2025, when Sunlight came to Balrampur, she bought gold earrings, toriya, and toe rings for her sisters. According to Deepanshu, he spent a total of 25 lakh 13 thousand 343 rupees on Sunlight and her family. Now he wants this money back, for which he has filed a case. When everything was fine, how did things go wrong...? Caste was hidden, that's why Sunlight broke off the relationship To answer this question, we first spoke to Sunlight's family members. Her family consists of mother Uma Devi and brother Albert David. The mother is a Shiksha Mitra at Hardayalpur Kendriya Vidyalaya. She was the Pradhan of Hardayalpur village between 2000 and 2005. Father Ravendra Singh Yadav passed away on April 10, 2026. Sunlight has two elder sisters, the eldest being Moonlight and then Snowhite. Both are government teachers. Brother Albert is doing MBBS from Kanpur. Snowhite says - We had sent our younger sister Sunlight to Prayagraj for studies. We didn't even know whom she came in contact with there? Gradually her lifestyle changed. She started wearing good clothes. Earlier she used to come home every month, later she would come home after several months. When asked, she would say that she has taken a PCS foundation course. I am studying for that. We also felt it was okay. Snowhite says - After some time Sunlight started living in her own world. She had no concern for us. When we asked, she told us about Deepanshu. She said that we will get married in future. We also didn't say anything. But, later it was found out that Deepanshu had hidden his caste. After this, Sunlight separated from him. Deepanshu filed a case against us. Snowhite says - Deepanshu is an officer. Why did he spend money on Sunlight? Did he ask us? Then how is he saying that my sister has cheated him of money? He thinks that I and my other sister are government teachers so we will pay the money, that's why Deepanshu has filed the case. Whereas, the reality is that he has ruined my sister's life. After this incident, my sister has gone into depression. Now let's know Deepanshu's side of the story... The girl's family threatens to implicate in rape case On the allegations of Sunlight's family, Deepanshu says - When our conversation started, just a few days later Sunlight's family came to know everything. These people were suspicious of my job, they asked for proof. We gave it too. The talk of hiding caste is completely false. They knew that I am a Dalit. Inter-caste marriage is not a crime. That's why both had decided that they would get married. Deepanshu says - When I was buying a plot in Lucknow in Sunlight's name, her family members knew about it at that time too. Her elder sister Moonlight herself is a witness to it. I have had good relations with her brother Albert. There was never any kind of problem. Later, these people stopped talking. Now she and her family members use caste-based abuses. They threaten to implicate me in a rape case. We asked Deepanshu what he wants now in this matter? Should those people be punished or should there be a settlement? Deepanshu says - I don't like disputes. If those people return my money, return the Lucknow plot, then I will think about whether to proceed with further action or not.

stories.summary: In Firozabad, the son of a former MLA shot and killed his wife. After that, he also committed suicide by shooting himself. The incident occurred on Saturday night at 9:15 PM. Hearing the sound of gunshots, family members and nearby people reached the spot. There, the MLA's son and his wife were lying soaked in blood. The wife had a bullet wound in her chest and the former MLA's son had a bullet in his head. Upon receiving information, police and the forensic team reached the crime scene. After talking to the family, the bodies were sent for post-mortem. The incident is being attributed to a property dispute. Police are investigating the matter. Now know the complete matter Rakesh Yadav (67), a resident of Dahini village, is the son of Jagdish Yadav who served as a Congress MLA from 1980 to 1985. Currently, Rakesh was living at Subhash Tiraha, Shikohabad. Rakesh has also served as the village Pradhan. He was also the manager of Adarsh Krishna Inter College. The 35 bigha land of Adarsh Krishna Inter College was given on lease to Arjun Singh Yadav of the village. The allegation is that even after the completion of one year's period, Arjun Singh did not vacate the land and maintained possession over it. In May 2025, on court orders, former Pradhan and advocate Rahul Yadav filed a case of embezzlement of two and a half lakh rupees against Rakesh Yadav. The allegation was that Rakesh had embezzled the income from the school's agricultural land. Also, he became the manager through fraudulent means. Rahul Yadav is Rakesh's nephew by relation. There had been discord between the two for a long time. Due to this reason, Rahul Yadav had filed a case against Rakesh. On Saturday, he had gone to court because there was a hearing date for this case. According to family members, after returning from court, he was under considerable stress. Late at night, he shot his wife Rammurty Devi (66) in the chest with a licensed revolver. After that, he shot himself in the head. Hearing the sound of gunshots, family members reached the spot. Both were taken to the hospital. Where doctors declared Rakesh Yadav dead in Shikohabad itself. Seriously injured Rammurty Devi was referred to the Medical College. She also died during treatment there. Police recovered revolver from the scene As soon as information about the incident was received, police reached the spot and started investigation. The forensic team also collected evidence from the crime scene. Police found a licensed revolver at the spot, which is being examined. Rakesh's nephew Gaurav Yadav said that Rakesh Yadav had been under mental stress for a long time due to land disputes and related lawsuits. It was due to this stress that he took this step. SHO Anuj Kumar Rana said, initial investigation suggests the case is related to stress and land dispute. The shot was fired from a licensed revolver. All aspects are being investigated. Daughter said- Had arranged father's bail Daughter Garima Yadav said - Father had been in depression for the past 2 years. A false case under Section 420 was registered against him. He was continuously troubled by this. We had also got him bail. The entire family was living under pressure after this case. Nahar Singh, Vidyaram the lawyer, and many others would come to meet and counsel him. I would tell everyone to please counsel father. In a Section 420 case, there can be a sentence of up to 10 years or life imprisonment. Father had refused to go to court On the 12th, he had a court appearance. He went to court and returned after getting a date. After that, he appeared very tense and shocked. I told him that I would also come along. To this, he said, "Where will you go, Lalli, you are a small child. Where all will you wander in courts with your child." No relative was supporting us We people don't have much knowledge of law. Neither was any relative helping. Nor was anyone supporting us. I am a woman from a respectable family. In such a situation, making repeated rounds of the court was also very difficult for me. Garima said that my sister-in-law has filed a divorce case against the entire family. Not only against me, but serious charges have been filed against my brother and my aunt's son as well. For the past 2 years, the entire family has been living in fear and stress. I went alone with my father to Allahabad to get bail for my brother. There was no male member in the family with us. My aunt is a widow and there was no one to support us. Father used to talk about going to Nepal Garima said that we were spending time in fear. Father often used to say that he would sell all the property and go somewhere else. He even talked about going to Nepal. We would explain to him that he had not committed any crime. But he would say that our grandfather was an MLA. The family's reputation has been tarnished by this matter.

stories.title: SIT uncovers 150 suspects in Ram Mandir donation theft probe:Action against Champat Rai almost certain, trustee Anil Mishra may also be removed
stories.summary: The Special Investigation Team (SIT) probing the alleged theft of donations from the Ram Mandir in Ayodhya has identified around 150 suspects. Of them, nearly 25 individuals may face action. People questioned by the SIT have been instructed not to leave the city until further orders. The SIT is expected to complete its sixth day of investigation on Saturday and return to Lucknow. Sources indicate that the team may submit its report to Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Monday. According to sources, action against Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust General Secretary Champat Rai and trustee Dr Anil Mishra is being considered. Both could be removed from their positions. Ram Mandir construction in-charge Gopal Rao may also face similar action. On Friday, the SIT spent nearly six hours inside the Mandir complex and questioned Champat Rai, Dr Anil Mishra and Gopal Rao separately. The team also interrogated officials of the State Bank of India, including the branch manager and cashier. Investigators also wanted to question Anand, Gopal Rao’s nephew, and Mandir employee Somesh Anand. However, both were unavailable and their phones were reportedly switched off. ₹2 crore recovered so far The SIT has recovered around ₹2 crore based on information provided by five accused — Lavkush, Avneesh, Anukalp, Karune and Ramshankar alias Tinnu. All were associated with counting donations collected at the Mandir. Gold was recovered from Tinnu’s residence on June 13. Officials have not yet disclosed the quantity or value of the recovered items. Opposition raised theft allegations The controversy began after former Uttar Pradesh minister Pawan Pandey alleged on June 7 that between ₹5 crore and ₹7.5 crore had been stolen from the Mandir. Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav also questioned the government's silence and called for judicial scrutiny. Champat Rai denied the allegations, saying no such facts had emerged. As the controversy intensified, BJP leader Dr Rajneesh Singh wrote to the Prime Minister on June 9 seeking a CBI probe. The Prime Minister’s Office sought a report from the Mandir trust the following day. Questions over donations, gold and silver records The SIT is also examining records related to gold, silver and other valuables donated to the Mandir. Investigators reportedly found discrepancies in documentation and are scrutinising staff involved in handling precious metals and donations. Officials are also reviewing donation figures recorded during the Prayagraj Mahakumbh period. More than five crore devotees visited Ayodhya and the Ram Mandir during the event, but the donation amount recorded was less than ₹100 crore, raising questions among investigators. Calls for accountability grow Former IAS officer and Ram Janmabhoomi Mandir Construction Committee chairman Nripendra Mishra described the alleged theft as a serious breach of trust. He said evidence linked to the counting process suggested weak oversight and inadequate vigilance. He also questioned whether the bank fulfilled its responsibilities under the agreement governing donation counting and accounting. Deputy Chief Minister Keshav Prasad Maurya said any wrongdoing would be punished after the SIT submits its findings. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has also said that no guilty person would be spared, regardless of their position. SIT composition The three-member SIT includes: The team is examining financial records, donation management systems and allegations of theft before finalising its report.

stories.title: Rain hits 9 UP districts, heatwave alert in 24:Showers in Prayagraj Sonbhadra; monsoon likely by June 25
stories.summary: The fluctuation in UP's weather continues. Today, Saturday, there is a heatwave alert in 24 districts. There is a possibility of rain in 9 districts, including Saharanpur, Agra, and Jhansi. Clouds have covered most districts since morning. Due to the reduced wind speed, heat and humidity are being felt. Meanwhile, the monsoon has been delayed in the state. After reaching the UP-Bihar border, the monsoon has been stalled near Maharajganj for the last 5-6 days. The Meteorological Department (IMD) says that the monsoon will start advancing from June 23. If favorable conditions persist, the monsoon could enter UP by June 25. According to IMD, rain activities may continue in some parts of Southern UP for the next few days. However, this will not reduce the heat. Humidity will increase. Hot winds are likely to blow, and temperatures are expected to remain above normal in many districts of Eastern UP and Bundelkhand. Earlier, late on Friday night, heavy rain occurred in some areas of Prayagraj. In the morning, Farrukhabad and Kanpur experienced rain with strong winds for about an hour. People got some relief from the heat. Speaking of heat, Banda remained the hottest city in the country with 44.2 °C. Varanasi was second with 43.0 °C. Lucknow's meteorologist, Atul Kumar Singh, said, Seasonal activities in UP are currently limited to scattered levels. There is a possibility of light drizzle in some places, but this will further increase the heat. The mercury will continue to rise till June 24. The heatwave situation will become more severe. The pace of monsoon is also slow. Currently, conditions for monsoon entry have not been formed. One may have to wait at least 5 more days for the monsoon.

stories.title: UP ticket sale expose triggers political storm:Mayawati issues clarification, minister Nishad sets up probe panel
stories.summary: Following Dainik Bhaskar's ‘Ticket Deal Part 1’ and ‘Ticket Deal Part 2’ investigations exposing the alleged sale of MLA tickets, political parties scrambled to contain the fallout. BSP chief Mayawati issued a clarification on social media, while minister Sanjay Nishad announced a party-level probe. The Suheldev Bharatiya Samaj Party, Apna Dal (Sonelal) and Janwadi Party (Socialist) also moved quickly to limit the damage caused by the revelations. Actually, in Bhaskar's sting operation, BSP's UP President Vishwanath Pal demanded 5 lakh rupees for a meeting with Mayawati. He also quoted the rate for an MLA ticket as 3.35 crore rupees. After this sting was published, Mayawati clarified on her X handle, stating: BSP is a true and honest party that follows the path shown by Baba Saheb for the constitutional rights and justice of the Bahujan society. Other parties are trying to defame it.' Mayawati also reiterated her resolve to achieve the target of Mission 2027. Sanjay Nishad said - We have contested elections by supporting people Dr. Sanjay Nishad, National President of Nishad Party and Cabinet Minister in the UP Government, has formed a 4-member committee at the party level after Bhaskar's sting operation, which will investigate the demand for money in ticket distribution within his party. He said, We have contested elections with complete transparency. We have contested elections by providing support. Whatever comes to light, we will take action. On Bhaskar's camera, office bearers of Cabinet Minister Om Prakash Rajbhar and Union Minister Anupriya Patel's parties were exposed demanding money in exchange for MLA tickets. Apart from them, Dr. Sanjay Singh Chauhan, National President of Janwadi Party (Socialist), which allied with SP in the last assembly elections, dealt to give a ticket for 2 crore rupees.

stories.title: Left home to become preacher in Mathura:Hid first marriage, now lives with another woman, alleges wife; couple has 3 children from 25-year marriage
stories.summary: A woman from Sewli village in Haryana's Palwal district has accused her husband of concealing his first marriage, marrying her, and later moving to Mathura where he allegedly adopted a new identity as a religious preacher and married another woman. Pushpa, who has filed a complaint with Palwal SP Nitish Agrawal, said she married Ran Singh around 25 years ago. The couple have three children. She alleged that she discovered about one-and-a-half years after their wedding that Ran Singh had already been married and had hidden the information from her. ‘He left home and became Shri Shyam Guru’ According to Pushpa, Ran Singh left home around 10 years ago and moved to Mathura. There, he allegedly changed his name to "Shri Shyam Guru" and began working as a religious storyteller. She claimed that although he occasionally returned home, he never shared details of his activities or personal life in Mathura. Family learnt about another marriage while searching for him Pushpa alleged that the family later discovered that Ran Singh had married another woman in Mathura. She said the matter came to light when family members tried to contact him for financial assistance during their son's wedding preparations. After failing to reach him for a long period, relatives travelled to Mathura in search of him. According to the complaint, they found that he was living under a new identity and had started a family with another woman. Pushpa alleged that the couple also have a daughter. Claims ancestral land sold without family's knowledge The woman further alleged that Ran Singh used his claimed connections with influential political leaders to convince people that he could arrange jobs and resolve official work. She alleged that he collected money from people on these promises and that some of them later approached the family seeking refunds. Pushpa also claimed that he sold nearly one acre of ancestral land in the village without informing family members. Woman cites earlier criminal case In her complaint, Pushpa also alleged that Ran Singh had previously been jailed in connection with a rape case involving a woman from Naveepur in Uttar Pradesh. She said she chose to continue the marriage despite learning about the case because of family circumstances. Police hand probe to Mundkati police station Police spokesperson Sanjay Kadiyan said the complaint has been forwarded to Mundkati police station for investigation. "The allegations made in the complaint will be verified during the investigation. Further legal action will be taken on the basis of facts that emerge," he said. No response from accused Attempts were made to contact Ran Singh on three mobile numbers regarding the allegations. All three phones were switched off. Messages were also sent seeking his response, but no reply had been received till the filing of this report.

stories.title: Tourists going to Thailand returning as drug couriers:Peddlers receive at Lucknow Airport; 200 crore worth of cannabis seized in 2 months
stories.summary: A flight from Bangkok via Muscat arrived in Lucknow. Mohammad Imran was carrying 8.5 kg of hydroponic weed (cannabis). Imran was a resident of Mumbai. When he reached the immigration counter, the team became suspicious after seeing his travel history. During interrogation, it was revealed that he was a drug courier. He had to deliver the weed to someone in Lucknow. Actually, despite there being a direct flight from Bangkok to Lucknow, he was coming to Lucknow via Muscat. Whereas both the fare and time were more. When his passport was checked, it was found that he had made his first international trip just 6 months ago. He used to drive an auto rickshaw in Mumbai, after which he became a delivery man. Drug agents had given him the job of courier to bring goods from Bangkok without revealing their identity. He had gone from Mumbai to Bangkok. There he was given 17 crystal vacuum polybags wrapped in Camlin carbon paper. His luggage had reached Lucknow while evading X-ray machines in Bangkok and Muscat. The luggage contained 8.5 kg of hydroponic weed, which was worth 8.55 crore rupees. This is just one case, cannabis smugglers are adopting new tactics How is hydroponic ganja being smuggled? How are youth becoming carriers...read the complete report.. Being Made Drug Carriers by Offering Free Thailand Trip Durgesh (changed name) was caught with beads at Lucknow Airport. He had returned after a free trip to Thailand. Stay and food were all free there. He also received 15,000 rupees along with it. Recently, 4 youths were arrested at Lucknow Airport. Durgesh's name was also among them. When they were interrogated, they also revealed the free trip offer along with smuggling. Drugs worth two and a half crores were recovered from them. This incident is from September 2025. Sources connected to the Customs Department reveal that drug smugglers are ensnaring common people, especially youth, in this trade without taking risks themselves. They are executing drug trafficking while keeping themselves behind the curtain. Young people are getting trapped in this due to the lure of free trips. Durgesh was also just 30 years old. He had gone to visit Thailand. It was here that he fell into the smugglers' trap. This is not the first case. International drug networks are continuously ensnaring youth in their web by offering similar deals and commissions. This is the reason why Lucknow has emerged as a new route for hydroponic weed trafficking. Many youth who went to visit Thailand from here are returning as drug couriers, knowingly or unknowingly. Girls trap people into drug syndicate by befriending them According to airport sources, girls are also involved in this nexus in Thailand. Such girls roam around clubs and markets and trap boys who have gone there for leisure, running the drug syndicate. Many young men don't consider this a serious crime initially. They are told that it is legal there, it's just a herbal product, or 'no one will catch you.' In one case, a group of young people who went to Bangkok for a trip returned with packets in separate bags. Each young person was only told to bring their share of the bag. They just had to hand it over to the peddlers outside the airport. Later, during airport inspection, it was discovered that hydroponic weed was hidden in all the bags. The most shocking thing was that two minors were also included in the group. Investigation agencies believe that due to their young age, the network thinks there will be less suspicion from security agencies. 14 smuggling gangs identified, receivers meet outside the airport Airport sources say that the courier's real job is just to get out of the airport. Outside, a car and receiver are already present. Everyone has code names. These are the same names that agents give to the courier in Thailand. After this, they meet outside the airport. Many times the courier doesn't even know where the goods are ultimately going. The receiver has the description, photo and phone number, and after their flight arrives, the receiver themselves chases them. A young man arrested recently had told during interrogation that he just wanted a cut, meaning commission. He was told that if the first delivery was successful, then on every trip ahead you will get lakhs of rupees. I wasn't told whom to give these packets to, I was just told that a call would come after reaching outside the airport. In this work, minors traveling in groups are also being used. Due to the group, the suspicion of security agencies is reduced. In many cases, small quantities are kept in the bags of different members of the same group, so that there is not too much suspicion on any one person. Officials associated with the agency say that most of the hydroponic weed is being brought to Lucknow from Thailand via flights. So far, 14 smuggling gangs connected to this network have been identified. Smugglers are specifically targeting youth who travel abroad on tourist visas. The entire deal from the airport to safe delivery is pre-arranged. Network extends to hotels, beaches, restaurants; they even pack it in cookies According to investigating agencies, the entire drug network is operating in such a way that the real mastermind has not yet come to light. Whenever a smuggling case is caught, the courier is the first to be arrested, but not much is obtained from interrogating them because they don't know anything about the gang. This is why the people ordering the goods and running the network often escape. The smugglers' network extends to airports, hotels, beaches, and restaurants. They first conduct reconnaissance on such people, then make them couriers. Hydroponic weed has a high price in the international market and there is considerable demand for it in India, which is why its smuggling has increased. The methods of smuggling it are quite unique. One such case is from February 2026. At Lucknow Airport, officials laid a trap to catch smugglers. Air Intelligence Unit (AIU) officers spread out across the international terminal. Now they were waiting for the flight arriving from Bangkok. As soon as the flight landed, the AIU officers' circle tightened. Meanwhile, a young passenger was in customs' crosshairs. Sir, what's in your luggage? The nervous passenger started breathing heavily. He said, nothing... why do you think so? The customs officers pulled out cookie boxes from the luggage. The passenger quickly said... sir, it's packed, packed. It's cookies, I'll bring some for you next time too. Customs caught the passenger and seized the cookies. These cookie boxes contained hydroponic buds (marijuana). Its market value was around 2 crore rupees. 2 Thai women arrested with weed worth 20 crores Smugglers are using women as tools in this black market business. On April 6, 2025, two Thai women arriving from Bangkok were caught at Lucknow Airport. During investigation, approximately 20 kg of hydroponic weed worth around 20 crore rupees was recovered from their trolley bags. During interrogation, it came to light that both women were merely couriers and had to deliver to a network in India. Sources connected to the investigation say that drug smugglers have started using female travelers as tools to evade the eyes of security agencies. Our focus is also on Indian female travelers. Many youth are getting trapped in this web due to the lure of earning quick money, living a luxury life, and traveling abroad. But once arrested, serious sections under the NDPS Act are imposed on them, which have provisions for long sentences. Getting bail in such cases is extremely difficult. Now know about the smuggling route and supply chain- Currently only 40% of smuggling is being caught Gang not being caught, hence smuggling continues According to investigation agencies, the biggest reason for this is huge profits. Hydroponic weed purchased at low prices from Thailand is sold at several times higher prices in India. Its demand is rapidly increasing in big cities. Cannabis worth one thousand rupees there sells for approximately 25 thousand rupees here. Additionally, the networks use small couriers, so that the big kingpins don't come directly to the front. That's why even when couriers are caught, the entire gang remains active and continues smuggling by recruiting new people. They also keep adopting new tactics. In the international market, the price of one kilogram of hydroponic weed is said to be around one crore rupees. This is why it is also called the drug of the rich. Thailand's weed also gives a good high, which is why its demand is higher. Ganja worth 29 crores seized from Lucknow Airport Why is more coming from Thailand? Thailand legalized medical and to some extent cannabis in 2022. Following this, large-scale cultivation and sale of cannabis increased there. As a result, high-quality hydroponic weed became easily available there. Through international networks and tourism, its supply started reaching other countries. Taking it in and out of airports is also legal there. Therefore, weed is not caught in scanning either. Why are smugglers bringing more weed? Compared to regular cannabis, its price is several times higher. Supplies worth lakhs of rupees happen in small packets, so the profit is very high. Its demand is increasing in big cities, parties, and among high-profile youth. It has been given a premium drug-like image, due to which customers are willing to pay more. Its supply is also easy. In which countries of the world has it received legal approval? Many countries in the world have decriminalized cannabis, but have allowed its use with several conditions. Countries that have given approval include Argentina, Barbados, Chile, Costa Rica, Croatia, Cyprus, Denmark, Czech Republic, Ecuador, Finland, Germany, Greece, Ireland, Italy, Jamaica, New Zealand, Panama, Jamaica, Peru, Poland, Portugal and Israel among others. Several reasons have been given for approving cannabis here. Such as - its use in medicines and for research purposes. Cannabis has also been approved so that it can be used in diseases like severe pain, cancer and Parkinson's disease. What do legal experts say about cannabis? Former DGP of UP, Vikram Singh explains that cannabis is mainly considered to be of two types. Sativa and Indica. Both are used for medicine and intoxication. Whereas hybrid cannabis is prepared by scientifically crossbreeding Sativa and Indica species.

stories.title: SIT questions donors over missing Ram Mandir offerings:Mahant says garland and 'charan paduka' were given to Tinnu Yadav; no receipt issued for silver offerings
stories.summary: In the Ram Mandir donation theft case in Ayodhya, the Special Investigation Team (SIT) is now contacting devotees who handed jewellery or valuables directly to employees of the temple trust. The SIT is examining when the items were submitted, who received them, and whether any official receipt was issued. On June 18, the SIT recorded the statement of Mumbai-based businessman Anil Vishwakarma. He alleged that his family donated a 3-kg silver garland and a 1-kg silver charan paduka (sacred footwear) for Ram Lalla, but never received a receipt from the temple authorities. Another donor, Anurag Rastogi, North India Head of the Indian Bullion and Jewellers Association, claimed that there is still no trace of the 60 kg silver donated by traders through the association. Bhaskar spoke to both the donors and a local mahant regarding the matter. Family walked 200 km barefoot to offer silver garland and charan paduka Mahant Acharya Vinod Mishra of Ayodhya's Rokadiya Hanuman Temple said Anil Vishwakarma, originally from Jaunpur and now a businessman in Mumbai, had vowed to offer a silver garland and charan paduka to Ram Lalla. According to Mishra, the finely crafted silver garland weighed around 3 kg, while the charan paduka, engraved with 64 sacred symbols, weighed about 1 kg. He said the family, including women and children, walked nearly 200 km barefoot and reached Ayodhya on October 29, 2025. After worshipping the offerings at his ashram, they carried them on their heads to the Ram Mandir. Mishra claimed that at the temple entrance they met Ramashankar alias Tinnu Yadav, who escorted them to the sanctum sanctorum through the VVIP route. The offerings were placed before Ram Lalla and later taken into custody by Tinnu Yadav. Family says receipt was never provided According to Mahant Mishra, when the family later sought photographs of the offering and an official receipt, they were told that the silver would first undergo purity checks by bank officials before being used. On the issue of a receipt, Mishra said Tinnu Yadav allegedly told them it would be issued only after it was seen by "Bhai Sahab", a reference to Trust General Secretary Champat Rai. Mishra alleged that neither the garland was placed on the deity nor was any information shared with the family. He claimed repeated requests for a receipt went unanswered. He further alleged that Tinnu later informed him the silver items had been sent to West Bengal to be melted and converted into silver bricks for making utensils required for temple rituals. "The devotee family felt deeply hurt after hearing this," Mishra said. Donor claims 60 kg silver donated during temple construction is untraceable Anurag Rastogi said bullion traders from across the country contributed small quantities of silver, ranging from 10 to 20 grams each, for the Ram Mandir project. According to him, a total of 60 kg silver was collected and melted into bricks weighing between 1 and 1.25 kg. The names and gotras of donors were inscribed on them. A 1-kg silver kalash was also donated by an association from Rishikesh. Rastogi said that on July 20, 2020, the silver bricks were taken to Ayodhya after receiving approval from Champat Rai. A worship ceremony was conducted at Ramkachehri, where Champat Rai, Dr Anil Mishra and cashier Prakash Gupta were present. He claimed that Dr Anil Mishra and Prakash Gupta accepted the donation and issued a receipt along with a purity certificate. The association had requested that the silver be used during the temple foundation ceremony. Silver lamp and offering bowls also missing, says donor Rastogi said he had separately donated two 1-kg silver lamps, two silver bowls, a 200-gram panchdhatu pestle and a pair of Nag-Nagin idols. He claimed one of the silver lamps was used to light the temple's eternal flame by Dr Anil Mishra and his wife. The lamp was visible in photographs taken during Prime Minister Narendra Modi's visit to Ram Lalla. However, Rastogi alleged that after the completion of the grand temple, neither the silver lamp nor the silver bowls donated for offering bhog to the deity could be found.

stories.title: Padma Shri Jaspal Rana’s mortal remains reach Varanasi:Last rites to be held at Manikarnika Ghat; death occurred yesterday
stories.summary: The body of international shooter Jaspal Rana arrived at Varanasi Airport by charter plane on Saturday afternoon at around 3:52 PM. The body was kept at the air cargo complex located in the old terminal building of the airport. A large number of people paid tribute there. After this, Jaspal Rana's body was taken to Rajghat for the last rites. From here, it will be brought by boat to Manikarnika Ghat, and the last rites will be performed there. The pyre has been prepared for this. At The Casa Resort on Chandmari Ring Road, the body was taken out of the box and placed on a bier. After this, the final journey departed for Manikarnika Ghat. During this, Defense Minister Rajnath Singh's son and Jaspal Rana's brother-in-law, MLA Pankaj Singh, were also present. Pankaj Singh had arrived at the airport around 12:15 PM. Apart from family members, BJP state minister Shankar Giri, former Azamgarh district president Jai Nath Singh, and several public representatives and dignitaries were present at the tribute program. First, see 3 pictures Padma Shri Jaspal Rana's uncle Rajendra Rana said - Jaspal Rana had expressed his wish many times that his last rites be performed at Manikarnika Ghat. Keeping this wish in mind, the family has decided to perform the last rites in Varanasi. Jaspal Rana, 49, passed away on Friday morning. He had been admitted to Max Saket Hospital in Delhi for the past 11 days. His health deteriorated on the flight while returning from Germany, after which he was admitted to the hospital. Manu Bhaker broke down while bidding final farewell to her guru Olympic medalist Manu Bhaker had reached Dehradun on Friday itself to bid a final farewell to her coach Jaspal Rana. Seeing the coach's mortal remains, she could not control herself and broke down, embracing Jaspal Rana's father Narayan Singh Rana. Jaspal Rana's role in Manu Bhaker's career has been extremely crucial. He continuously guided Manu from the junior level to the international stage. Jaspal Rana's training and experience are also considered a major reason behind Manu's two medals at the Paris Olympics. Over 600 Medals, Made History at 2006 Asiad Jaspal Rana is considered one of the most successful players in Indian shooting history. He has more than 600 medals to his name in various national and international competitions. In 1994, he set a world record with a gold medal at the Junior World Shooting Championship in Milan. That same year, he gained international recognition by winning a gold medal at the Hiroshima Asian Games. The 2006 Doha Asian Games are considered a golden chapter in his career. There, he scored a world-equalling 590 points in the 25-meter center fire pistol and won three gold and one silver medal. Friendship with Rahul Gandhi began at the shooting range Jaspal Rana's connections were not limited to the sports world. He had personal relationships with Rahul Gandhi as well as CM Pushkar Singh Dhami. According to some family sources, Rana and Congress leader Rahul Gandhi first met at a shooting range. Their shared passion for shooting brought them closer, and this relationship continued even after they entered politics. After joining Congress in 2012, Jaspal Rana was seen actively participating in party programs. His many meetings and public events with Rahul Gandhi remained a topic of discussion. Upon his demise, Rahul Gandhi also expressed grief, recalling his contribution to Indian shooting. From BJP to Congress, Father Remained in a Different Party After sports, Jaspal Rana also became active in politics. In 2009, he contested the Tehri Lok Sabha seat on a BJP ticket, though he could not win. Later, he joined Congress. At that time, his father Narayan Singh Rana was active in BJP, while Jaspal was campaigning for Congress. The separate political paths of father and son were among the well-known political stories of Uttarakhand during that period. Also connected to Rajnath Singh's family Jaspal Rana's sister, Sushma Singh, is married to Defense Minister Rajnath Singh's son and Noida MLA, Pankaj Singh. Due to this relationship, his family has also been connected to prominent political figures of the country. Jaspal Rana, who remained active in sports, politics, and and social life, has left behind a legacy that includes a long chain of medals, records, disciples, and inspiration. Father was in ITBP, handed Rana a pistol in childhood Jaspal Rana was born on June 28, 1976, in Uttarkashi. However, he was originally from Tehri. His father, Narayan Singh Rana, was deployed in the Indo-Tibetan Border Police, or ITBP. Later, he also became the first Sports Minister of Uttarakhand. He had a special fondness for shooting and it was he who handed his son a pistol at the tender age of 10. The sporting environment in the family was so strong that his sister Sushma Singh and brother Subhash Rana also became national-level shooters. From a young age, Jaspal spent most of his time at the shooting range, and it was from here that the journey began which placed him among the world's best shooters. First medal at the age of 12, Arjuna Award at 18 In the National Shooting Championship held in Ahmedabad in 1988, 12-year-old Jaspal Rana drew the nation's attention by winning a silver medal. After this, he consistently performed brilliantly in national competitions and emerged as the new face of Indian shooting. His talent can be gauged from the fact that he was honored with the Arjuna Award at the mere age of 18. Achieving this feat at such a young age was considered a great achievement in that era.

stories.title: Aligarh’s Sergeant Jitendra Sharma dies in Assam plane crash:Air Force AN-32 aircraft goes down; 5 personnel lose their lives
stories.summary: On Saturday morning at 10 AM, an Indian Air Force AN-32 transport aircraft crashed during landing at Rauria Air Force Station in Jorhat, Assam. Five Air Force personnel, including Sergeant Jitendra Sharma from Aligarh, died in the accident. One pilot was also martyred in the accident. These include Squadron Leader Prashant Singh, Flight Lieutenant Shubham Kumar, Sergeant Jitendra Sharma, Agniveervayu Khemaram Kumawat, and Agniveervayu Danish Alam. Following the accident, the Air Force has ordered a Court of Inquiry for investigation, while the co-pilot is undergoing treatment in the hospital. Danish was from Bihar and Khemaram was from Rajasthan. Sergeant Jitendra Sharma was from Salpur village in Aligarh. The accident occurred when the aircraft was attempting to land at the airbase. After the accident, it caught fire and broke into two pieces. This was an AN-32 cargo aircraft, used for transporting troops and supplies. The cause of the accident has not been revealed. The Indian Air Force stated that the aircraft was on a routine flight. It also appealed not to speculate until the initial results are out. Orders for a Court of Inquiry have been issued. Air Force preparing to replace AN-32 aircraft According to news agency ANI, the Indian Air Force is preparing to replace its old AN-32 and IL-76 transport aircraft. For this, new Medium Transport Aircraft (MTA) will be purchased to meet the future needs for transporting troops, weapons, and military equipment. 3 photos of the accident The fire brigade and army personnel present at the airbase reached the spot and brought the fire under control. AN-32 Cargo to extinguishplane capable of landing even in hilly and difficult terrains The Indian Air Force has a fleet of approximately 100 Antonov AN-32 tactical transport aircraft. Although the IAF initially purchased 125 such Soviet-origin planes, the number of active-duty planes has now reduced to approximately 100. Since 1980, the AN-32 has served as the backbone of the IAF's medium-lift transport capabilities. Due to its robustness during operations in hot weather and high-altitude areas like the Himalayas, it is considered very important. Air Force Aircraft Accidents from January to June January 21, 2026- An IAF trainee aircraft crashed during a routine flight in Uttar Pradesh. Both pilots safely ejected. No civilian casualties were reported. However, a Court of Inquiry was constituted for investigation. February 7, 2026- An HAL Tejas fighter jet veered off the runway during takeoff. Later reports cited a software glitch as the cause. The pilot survived, though he sustained injuries. March 5, 2026- An Su-30MKI crashed during training in Assam's Karbi Anglong region. Both pilots died. One of these pilots was also associated with Operation Sindoor. April 17, 2026- An Air Force fighter jet made a hard landing at Pune International Airport. The plane's 'undercarriage,' meaning the lower part of the aircraft, was damaged, causing it to hit the runway. This closed the runway for 11 hours.

stories.title: Pilgrim bus crash in UP leaves 3 dead, 36 injured:Driver may have dozed off, say passengers; 2 buses collide head-on
stories.summary: Three devotees were killed and at least 36 others injured after a private bus carrying pilgrims from Rajasthan collided head-on with a UP Roadways bus in Uttar Pradesh's Kasganj district early Saturday. The pilgrims, all members of an extended family from Bharatpur, were travelling to Soron for a holy dip in the Ganga when the accident occurred around 4 am. According to passengers, the private bus had left Bharatpur at about 11 pm on Friday. Several passengers alleged that the driver may have dozed off moments before the collision, causing the vehicle to drift into the opposite lane and crash into the oncoming state-run bus. The deceased were identified as Girraj Singh (85) of Farso village, Pitam (65), and Ram Dhakeli (80), both residents of Nagla Kurwariya in Bharatpur's Bayana area. Deepak, one of the passengers, said around 40 family members were travelling together when the accident took place near Kasganj. "The driver appeared to have fallen asleep shortly before the crash," he alleged. The impact left the front portions of both buses badly damaged and triggered panic among passengers. Local residents rushed to the spot and helped rescue those trapped inside the vehicles. Police and ambulance teams shifted the injured to Kasganj District Hospital. After receiving primary treatment, several passengers were referred to hospitals in Bharatpur. Some were admitted to RBM Hospital, while others were taken to private healthcare facilities. Police said an investigation is underway to determine the exact cause of the accident. See other pictures of the accident

stories.title: 1,200 scientists and experts to gather at BHU tomorrow:CM Yogi to inaugurate national convention; AI risks and ethics on agenda
stories.summary: Kashi, the religious and cultural capital, is now going to witness the country's biggest scientific discourse. The 7th National Convention of Vigyan Bharati is being organised on June 13 and 14 under the joint auspices of Banaras Hindu University and the Vedic Science Centre. Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath will participate as the chief guest in the inaugural session of this two-day mega convention on the morning of June 13. This session will set the direction for future discourse related to science, technology, innovation, and national development in the country. Over 1200 stalwarts from India and abroad will gather Approximately 1200 delegates from India and various corners of the world are participating in this two-day national convention. Members of Vigyan Bharati, renowned scientists, researchers, academicians, policymakers, industry representatives, and experts in various technical fields will be seen on one platform at this grand gathering. Vaidya Rajesh Kotecha, Secretary of the Ministry of AYUSH, Government of India, will be the special guest, and Dr. Shekhar C. Mande, President of the Indian National Science Academy, will also be present at the inaugural session. Padma Shri Prof. Ashutosh Sharma to deliberate on artificial intelligence and ethics On the second day of the convention, a special session will be organized on the most important and contemporary topic, 'Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Ethics'. Former Secretary of the Department of Science Technology, Government of India, and Padma Shri awardee Prof. Ashutosh Sharma will lead this session. In this, technical experts and policymakers will deeply deliberate on how to ensure the responsible and ethical use of Artificial Intelligence for the benefit of society. Country's Top think tanks to formulate strategy on 'One Health' and 'Net Zero' According to Dr. Shivkumar Sharma, National Organizing Secretary of Vigyan Bharati, the main objective of this convention is to prepare a concrete action plan for a scientifically empowered and self-reliant India by having meaningful discussions on contemporary scientific and social challenges. For this, two major sessions will be organized: Under the leadership of Dr. B. N. Gangadhar, Chairman of the National Medical Commission, experts related to medicine, health, and research will deliberate on this topic. Under the leadership of Manu Srivastava, Principal Secretary of the Energy Department, Government of Madhya Pradesh, dimensions related to sustainable development and energy transition will be discussed. Former Vice Chairman of NITI Aayog and senior RSS functionaries will also participate During the session, a public lecture will be delivered by renowned economist and former Vice Chairman of NITI Aayog, Dr. Rajiv Kumar. Additionally, a special address by Dr. Krishna Gopal, Sah-Sarkaryavah of Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh, and a special lecture by Sunil Ambekar, All India Prachar Pramukh, have been organized. Prof. Ramnarayan Dwivedi, a member of the steering committee, informed that a comprehensive discussion will also be held on an important proposal related to the "Science, Technology and Innovation Policy for India" on this platform. Concluding session to be held in the presence of Minister of state for defence, Sanjay Seth This two-day event will conclude on June 14. In the closing session, Sanjay Seth, Minister of State for Defence, Government of India, will participate as the chief guest. Along with him, NITI Aayog members Prof. Abhay Karandikar and Prof. Govardhan Das will be present as special guests. Ankit Rai, Regional Organizing Secretary of Vijnana Bharati, stated that this national convention will prove to be a milestone in strengthening the scientific capabilities of the country and realizing the resolve of 'Developed India' by 2047.

stories.title: Speeding Creta mows down 4 in Saharanpur:Mother, son, daughter and granddaughter killed on spot
stories.summary: In Saharanpur, 4 members of a family died in a road accident. The family was on a single motorcycle. A speeding Creta car coming from behind hit them from the rear. The accident was so horrific that all four people on the motorcycle fell 10 feet away from the road into a ditch. The Creta car also overturned and fell into the ditch. Nearby people took all four injured to the hospital, where doctors declared them dead. The accident occurred on Saturday at 2 PM near Dhaulakuan in the Biharigarh area on Behat Road. Eyewitnesses stated that a minor was driving the Creta car. Police are investigating this claim based on the car's registration number. According to the police, Lavish (26) of Malkpur, his mother Rajdulari (55), sister Anjana alias Tannu (20), and three-year-old daughter Ruhi died in the accident. Two pictures of the accident Accident happened while returning home from in-laws' house Ankit, the uncle of the deceased, said - Lavish had gone to his in-laws' house in Kothri with his mother, sister, and daughter Ruhi (3). From there, he was returning to his village Malkpur on a bike. Lavish used to support his family by working as a laborer. He was the second of three brothers. Lavish got married in 2022. He has a wife and a young son at home. Ruhi, who lost her life in the accident, was the elder daughter. Police investigation revealed that the car was being driven by the minor son of Tahir, who lives in Kothri Bahalolpur-2. He fled the scene after the accident. Police have seized the car. The vehicle is said to be registered in Tahir's name. Police are engaged in further action and investigation in the matter.

stories.title: Yogi warns against comments on Akhilesh’s daughter:Says such things will not be tolerated; urges political workers to maintain restraint
stories.summary: CM Yogi reacted for the first time to the objectionable remark made against Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav's daughter, Aditi. He said on Saturday in Azamgarh - A daughter is a daughter, and she should be respected. I was seeing in recent days that some people had made wrong remarks against the daughter of the SP chief. I immediately told the police to register an FIR. No derogatory remark against a daughter will be tolerated. The CM said- We have been brought up with the tradition where it is said that a village's daughter is everyone's daughter, a village's sister is everyone's sister. We have not discriminated. Akhilesh ji, if you preach to others, then preach to your followers as well to exercise some restraint in their language. They should also think before making comments. Yogi said - What kind of language do SP people use towards sisters, deceased people, senior leaders, daughters, and elders? Akhilesh ji, explain it to them. If they don't understand, hand them over to us, we will make them understand. CM Yogi also inaugurated and laid the foundation stone for 39 development projects worth 955 crore in Azamgarh. Minister Omprakash Rajbhar was also present on the stage. Read CM Yogi's 4 major points- 1- Those who divide are not your well-wishers The CM said - Azamgarh is a district where there are handicrafts, artisans, food-providing farmers, and energetic youth. Then why did this district struggle for its identity? Why did a crisis of identity arise before that district? It is with this question that I repeatedly come to Azamgarh, because this pain is not just Azamgarh's, but ours too. Those who divided us, who split us all, they kept getting your support repeatedly, but they are not your well-wishers. 2- Before 2017, Azamgarh was struggling for its identity Yogi said - Remember Azamgarh before 2017, which was struggling for its identity. Back then, there was no university here, no Purvanchal Expressway, no airport was functioning properly, nor was there a music college in Hariharpur. Even Azamgarh's saree was not getting any platform then. There was no place for Mubarakpur's black pottery either. Today, a craftsman associated with black pottery met me and happily said that ever since the double-engine government came to power in Uttar Pradesh, our business has grown many times over. 3- Earlier, the poor had no one to listen to them The Chief Minister said - Earlier, the poor had no one to listen to them, but ever since our government was formed, the work that could not be done for centuries has been completed. Earlier, Azamgarh's name used to come up in every terrorist incident. Youths' jobs were being compromised. There was no scheme for daughters, nor any plan for their safety and advancement. Our government has worked to give due respect to Maharaja Suheldev. 4- Foreign invaders should not be honored The CM said - Earlier, events were held in Bahraich in the name of invaders Salar Mian and Ghazi Mian. When our government came, we said - this will not do. We got it stopped. We said that these are symbols of slavery. Foreign invaders should not be honored. Today, a large statue of Maharaja Suheldev has been installed here. Wherever you go, you will be recognized by Maharaja Suheldev. The Harihar Gharana here is famous all over the world. Here is Bhojpuri artist Dinesh Lal Nirahua, who is working to sweeten people's hearts with his voice. Rajbhar said - This time we will defeat SP in Azamgarh Om Prakash Rajbhar said - People say that Azamgarh is a stronghold of the Samajwadi Party. SP's stronghold means Yadavs' stronghold. Tell me, do Rajbhar, Nishad, Bind, and other castes live here or not? In this election, we will turn the stronghold into a 'gadhahi' (pit). We will work to defeat SP from here. FIR against 4 in Aditi Yadav comment case An FIR was registered in Kanpur-Pratapgarh on Thursday in connection with objectionable posts made on social media regarding Aditi Yadav (23). A case was registered against Bharat Patel, Nageshwar Singh Baghel, and Vinod Yadav on the complaint of Praveen Yadav, National Secretary of the Advocates' Association, in Kanpur. Additionally, on the complaint of Samajwadi Party General Secretary Abdul Qadir Jilani in Pratapgarh, a case was registered against an ID named Sheetla Sujan Kavi. All four are accused of making objectionable posts against Aditi on social media. This tarnished the image of Akhilesh Yadav and his family in society. Therefore, strict action should be taken against them. Read what was said about the objectionable posts on Aditi Yadav -
