stories.title: 4 friends record video before crash:Car speeding at over 100 kmph hits parked truck; all die on spot
stories.summary: Anupam, who lost his life in a road accident in Prayagraj, had his wife fill her hairline with vermilion for the last time. When Anupam's body arrived home from Unnao on Saturday morning, his wife Priya became unconscious. Crying, she sat near the body. During this, a woman brought a vermilion box. A relative applied vermilion on Anupam's hand, then Priya bowed her head and filled her hairline with vermilion, and touching her husband's feet, she burst into tears. Whoever witnessed this scene had tears well up in their eyes. The mother also clung to the body. Crying, she said, 'Show me his face just once. Now I will never get my son back. I beg you, just let me see his face once.' Anupam had died along with his four friends in a road accident on the Ganga Expressway in Unnao on Friday. All four were going to Shimla for a trip. On Saturday, the bodies of the four friends were brought to their homes. The three friends, Uday, Anupam, and Vijay, were cremated at Chhatnag Ghat in Prayagraj, while Aman Kashyap's last rites were performed in his ancestral village, Mandhata in Pratapgarh. See 2 pictures Uday was cremated by his father and Vijay by his brother. On Saturday, the funeral procession of Uday Singh, the only son of his parents, left the house first. Seeing the condition of the parents while bidding farewell to their son, people's eyes welled up. Father Ram Singh lit the pyre. After this, Vijay Kumar's funeral procession began. Vijay's pyre was lit by his elder brother Roshan Lal. Anupam Gupta's father, Ajay Gupta, arrived in Prayagraj from Kolkata in the afternoon. After this, Anupam's last rites were performed. They were going to Shimla in a Tata Punch Anupam Gupta (32), Uday Singh (28), Vijay (40) from Jafarpur Babuganj, Phulpur police station area, and Aman Kashyap (28) from Mandhata, Pratapgarh district, were friends. On Friday morning around 10 am, they left for Shimla in a Tata Punch car. Aman had come to his aunt's house in Babuganj, from where the four friends started their journey together. Around 3:30 PM, their car collided from behind with a truck parked on the side of the road on the Ganga Expressway in Unnao. The impact was so strong that the car was torn to pieces. The front part was badly crushed. All four friends died in the accident. They were all stuck to their seats. The doors were cut to pull all four out of the car. All four friends had their own businesses Anupam Gupta operated a shop named Gupta Mobile Internet in Jafarpur Babuganj. He was married. Meanwhile, Vijay ran a tent house business. His family includes his wife Sunita, two sons Mayank and Eeshanth, and a daughter Ishika. Uday Singh owned a footwear shop and is survived by his wife Khushi and two-year-old son Ayush. Aman Kashyap was unmarried and had come to Babuganj to visit relatives. All four friends were educated Anupam owned a mobile shop, while Vijay was running a tent house business. Uday had a shoe and slipper shop. Aman owned several shops in Pratapgarh. Anupam's parents live in Calcutta. His father works for LIC. Anupam had graduated. He ran a mobile shop. His wife Priya had gone to her maternal home. Anupam's in-laws are in Bhadri Kunda, Pratapgarh. They had been married for two years. Uday Patel alias Babuji was an only child. He owned a shoe and slipper shop. Uday had completed ITI. He had done his apprenticeship from Gujarat in the IFFCO company. He had come home a year ago. Here, he had started a business. Vijay had graduated. Currently, he was doing a tent business.

stories.title: CM Yogi targets foreign forces in speech:Says excessive pesticide use is harming farmland; opens national convention at BHU
stories.summary: Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath said in Varanasi for a long time, there has been a perception in our country that Indians are good for nothing and only foreigners are superior. Foreign powers, leftist ideology, and anti-India elements tried to do this to the country and are still doing so today. On the importance of Ganga, CM Yogi said- In my childhood, my mother used to ask us to cultivate small beds near the house. We would water the plants, add fertiliser, and take care of them. When a plant got infested with insects or didn't bloom, we would complain to our mother about it. Then, my mother would say, 'Don't worry.' After that, she would bring Ganga water in a pot and sprinkle it on the plants. The surprising thing was that within four or five days, those plants would start blooming again. That's when we realized the importance of Ganga. Actually, on Saturday, CM Yogi inaugurated the 7th National Convention of Vigyan Bharati at Swatantrata Bhawan of Kashi Hindu University (BHU). Before this, BHU Vice-Chancellor Prof. Ajit Kumar Chaturvedi welcomed and honored the Chief Minister by presenting him with an angavastra. This national convention of Vigyan Bharati is being organized on June 13 and 14. Approximately 1200 delegates from India and abroad are participating in the 2-day convention. These include members of Vigyan Bharati, scientists, researchers, academicians, policymakers, industry representatives, and experts from various fields. See 3 pictures CM Yogi released the annual report of Vigyan Bharati.

stories.title: CM to gift ₹300 crore development projects today:Programme at Mahuapar in Chillupar; inaugurations for 197 social welfare schemes
stories.summary: Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath will reach Gorakhpur on Saturday afternoon for a three-day tour. On the first day, he will gift development projects worth 300 crore rupees to the Chillupar assembly constituency. These include 319 projects. At the program organised at Gandhi Inter College in Mahuapar, he will inaugurate 122 projects completed at a cost of 152.21 crore rupees and lay the foundation stone for 197 projects to be built at a cost of 143.25 crore rupees. There, the Chief Minister will also address the public gathering. The CM will reach Gorakhpur from Azamgarh. All these projects will not only ease traffic in Chillupar assembly and Bansgaon Lok Sabha constituencies, but will also strengthen education and health facilities, as well as flood protection measures. The program will start at 1 PM. People have arrived at the program venue. The Chief Minister is being awaited. Inauguration of these projects According to the district administration, the projects to be inaugurated include the widening and strengthening of the Uruwa-Dhuriapar-Shahpur Belghat road at a cost of ₹57.81 crore, the newly constructed Government Industrial Training Institute in Kohra Bujurg at a cost of ₹10.81 crore, and the development of smart classes and other facilities in more than 15 primary schools. Similarly, various works undertaken for strengthening the embankments along the Rapti and Saryu rivers are also included. On Sunday evening, the second day of his visit, the Chief Minister will participate in a program organised at Veer Bahadur Singh Sports College, where he will inaugurate and lay the foundation stone for development projects worth approximately ₹950 crore.

stories.title: ₹10 lakh recovered from Ram Mandir employee’s home:Cash hidden in cow dung pile; temple trust requests CM Yogi for probe
stories.summary: The row over claims of a ₹7 crore theft from donations at the Ayodhya Ram Temple is intensifying. According to sources, the temple trust on Saturday requested Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath to order an SIT (Special Investigation Team) probe into the alleged theft. Meanwhile, ₹10 lakh has been recovered from the house of temple employee Lavkush Mishra (27). He had allegedly hidden the cash under a pile of cow dung, while some money was also found inside a box. However, it is not yet known who the money belongs to. Lavkush’s father has also confirmed that the cash was recovered from their house. Sources said Lavkush was responsible for counting donation money at the temple. Lavkush’s father said his son had been working at the Ram Temple for the past four to five months. Lavkush is a resident of Minapur Thakuran Phagauli village in the Rudauli area of Ayodhya. His father, Bacchulal, said, “My son had been working at the Ram Temple for the last four to five months. During this period, the theft incident took place there. Some people came to our house as part of the investigation and carried out a search. During the search, ₹10 lakh was recovered. What had to happen has now happened. The house being built in Faizabad has no connection with my son. To construct the house, I mortgaged 10-12 bighas of farmland.” Villagers said the search team consisted of six people, including two in police uniform and four in plain clothes. The cash was found in cupboards and boxes inside Lavkush’s house, while some money had allegedly been buried under a pile of cow dung. Lavkush previously worked as a car mechanic. Villagers said his financial condition improved rapidly after he got the temple job. Whenever he visited the village, he spent money freely. On one occasion, he reportedly spent ₹50,000 at a liquor shop to treat villagers. Lavkush’s father, Bacchulal, works at the iron market in Ghaziabad. He has three daughters and one son, Lavkush. Lavkush got married eight years ago and has a six-year-old son and a two-year-old daughter. Nripendra Mishra arrived in Ayodhya on Saturday for the second time in five days. He attended a meeting of the temple construction committee. Before the meeting, he was questioned about the donation controversy. Question: What issues will be discussed today?Nripendra Mishra: I do not know. Question: What will be discussed in the temple construction committee meeting?Nripendra Mishra: I have come to review the progress of the construction work. Question: Allegations of a scam involving Ram Temple donations have surfaced. Will that also be discussed? Will you seek information about it?Nripendra Mishra: This is a construction committee meeting. My responsibility is to oversee the construction work. Earlier, after the donation controversy emerged on 7 June, Nripendra Mishra had also visited Ayodhya on 9 June. He held a meeting with members of the temple trust, where issues related to donation funds, their utilisation and financial records were discussed. Former account in charge said that removed after complaining to Champat Rai BJP leader wrote two letters to PM Modi Ayodhya's BJP leader Dr. Rajneesh Singh has written two letters to Prime Minister Narendra Modi. He sent the first letter on 9 June. In it, he wrote that the Ram Temple is a center of faith for millions of devotees. In such a situation, complete transparency is necessary in any allegations or disputes related to offerings, donations, and temple administration. He said that if the allegations made are false, the truth should come out through an investigation. For this, an impartial investigation should be conducted by an independent and high-level agency, such as CBI or ED. Subsequently, on June 11, Dr. Rajneesh Singh wrote a second letter to the Prime Minister. In it, he made 6 demands- What leaders said on the claims of theft System for counting offerings in Temple Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust formed on 5 February, 2020

stories.title: TGT exam solver gang kingpin arrested in Varanasi:₹25,000 reward on him; 14 debit cards fake documents seized
stories.summary: Police have arrested Daulat Kumar, the alleged mastermind of a solver gang involved in the TGT examination in Varanasi, along with his associate Nitish Kumar. A ₹25,000 reward had been announced on Daulat, who had been absconding since the June 4 arrests. Both were caught from the Lakri Mandi area in Chaukaghat and later sent to jail. ACP Chetganj Shubham Kumar said that on June 4, solver Amrit Raj, who was appearing for the TGT exam in place of a candidate at Queen's Inter College, and his accomplice Chhotu Kumar were arrested. During questioning, they identified Daulat Kumar, a resident of Ward No. 2, Temabhela under Gwalpara police station in Bihar's Madhepura district, as the gang's mastermind, prompting a police manhunt and the announcement of a ₹25,000 reward. Apprehended with accomplice from Lakri Mandi According to the ACP, the police had received information that Daulat Kumar was present in the Chauka Ghat timber market area. Based on the information, he was arrested on the night of June 12 after being surrounded. Along with him, Nitish Kumar, a resident of Ratanpura, Supaul district, Bihar, was also apprehended. The police recovered several fake documents, 14 debit cards, and important transaction papers related to examinations from their possession. The recovered documents are being investigated. How he ran the solver gang Gang's network to be investigated Police say that by interrogating the arrested accused, information about other members of the gang and their network is being gathered. It is being investigated which competitive exams this gang has tried to infiltrate so far, and how many people are involved in it. Further legal action will be taken based on the investigation, and a campaign will also be launched to arrest other accused associated with the gang.

stories.title: Varanasi international stadium nears completion:92% work done; director says, 'ground will be match-ready within 30 minutes of rain'
stories.summary: The Ganjari International Cricket Stadium, a dream project of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, is nearing completion, with about 92% of construction work finished, according to Project Director Saroj Shukla. A trial match is planned by the end of this year, while the venue is expected to host its first international match in 2027. Stadium being built on Shiva theme-based architecture Spectator gallery to be crescent-shaped The stadium's roof has been designed inspired by the shape of the moon adorning Lord Shiva's forehead, while the spectator gallery is being developed on the lines of the famous Ganga Ghats' steps in Kashi. This will provide spectators with a unique experience of Kashi's spiritual culture along with the game. Project Director Saroj Shukla informed that a state-of-the-art drainage system has been installed in the ground. Even if it rains continuously for one or two hours, the ground can be made ready for play within just 30 minutes. This facility will place it in the category of the country's select modern cricket stadiums. Prime Minister laid the foundation stone in 2023 Ganjari Cricket Stadium will open new opportunities not only for players from Purvanchal but also for those from surrounding districts and neighboring states. Along with providing an international platform for sporting talents, its operation is expected to bring significant benefits to Varanasi's economy, tourism, and employment sectors. The foundation stone for this ambitious project was laid by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on September 23, 2023.

stories.title: 4 arrested in Lucknow, including UP police constable:CRPF sub-inspector absconding in ₹5 lakh hostage robbery case
stories.summary: Four people, including a UP Police constable, have been arrested in Lucknow for allegedly robbing two men after luring them with investment promises. The victims were called to invest in a private company, held hostage, and robbed of ₹5 lakh. They were also assaulted when they resisted. A CRPF sub-inspector and another accused were allegedly involved and are currently absconding. Police said the case was registered at Chinhat Kotwali on June 11 on a complaint by Prabhakar Singh of Vrindavan Colony. He alleged that his brother Diwakar Singh and friend Anoop Shukla were promised quick returns by investing in a company, but when they arrived with the money, they were robbed and beaten. Used to intimidate by posing as police officers The arrested accused revealed during interrogation that they worked as a syndicate. They would call people in the name of investment, intimidate them by posing as officers from various branches of the police, and extort money from them. They also committed robberies multiple times. DCP East Deeksha Sharma said that during the investigation of the case, the involvement of CRPF Sub-Inspector Jai Prakash Yadav came to light. He is currently absconding. Along with the Sub-Inspector, another accused, Anand Dubey, was also named in this case. Police arrested all four at night The arrested accused include Javed Hussain and Asif, residents of Gorakhpur; Pravesh Tripathi, a resident of Sant Kabir Nagar; and Pooran Singh, a resident of Rajasthan. All were arrested on the night of June 12 near the Hardasikheda canal culvert. Accused constable posted at Chinhat Kotwali DCP East Deeksha Sharma stated that UP Police constable Pooran Singh is currently posted at Chinhat Kotwali. In this case, 4 accused have been arrested. Police teams are continuously raiding to arrest the absconding sub-inspector. Along with this, information about the criminal history of the accused is being gathered from other districts and units.

stories.title: Gorakhpur power revenue drops by ₹5 crore:22 power engineers face action; major defaulters to lose connections
stories.summary: In Gorakhpur, the electricity corporation has taken a tough stance after electricity bill recovery fell behind targets. Revenue collection in May was around ₹5 crore lower than last year, prompting charge sheets against 14 JEs, 5 SDOs, and 3 Executive Engineers. Following the action, engineers have launched campaigns to recover dues from defaulting consumers. Along with ensuring uninterrupted summer power supply, engineers are also responsible for boosting revenue. The Chairman and Managing Director of Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Limited have been continuously reviewing recovery performance. Dissatisfied with Gorakhpur city's May revenue figures, the management initiated action against poorly performing engineers. Bills lower after shift from prepaid to postpaid meters Engineers say that one reason for the decrease in revenue is also the change in the meter system. Earlier, during the prepaid meter system, many consumers had deposited money in advance to avoid power cuts. Later, when the postpaid system was implemented, the same amount was adjusted in the bill. This resulted in lower bills for many consumers and affected recovery. Payment stalled, awaiting one-time settlement scheme Arrears are increasing in rural areas along with metropolitan areas. According to officials, many consumers are waiting for a one-time settlement scheme to arrive, so they are not depositing bills. Meanwhile, some people are citing financial difficulties and saying they will pay later. Superintending Engineer City Ranjeet Chaudhary informed that the campaign for arrears recovery has been intensified. Connections of consumers who owe more than one lakh rupees in electricity bills are being disconnected. Supply will resume only after payment. Action is also being taken against small defaulters. Action will also continue against engineers who show negligence in revenue recovery.

stories.title: Mother's dream, son's deception:22-year-old posed as army brigadier after NEET setbacks; Shahjahanpur police arrest youth
stories.summary: My mother wanted me to become an army officer. My father wanted to make me a doctor. I didn't want to disappoint my parents, so I tried everything. I took the NEET exam twice, but failed. To fulfill my mother's dream, I bought a uniform and became a Brigadier. I also hired two security guards, whom I provided with NGS commando uniforms. I had 'Doctor' and 'Army' written on my car. I also started driving with the army flag installed. This is what 22-year-old fake Brigadier Aryan Verma said. His father is an inspector in the horticulture department, and his mother is a government teacher. He had been roaming around Shahjahanpur wearing a uniform for two months. Former soldiers became suspicious of him. They, along with army officials, laid a trap to catch him. On Friday, the event was organised, and Aryan Verma was called. As soon as he arrived, army officials asked him questions related to the army. He was flustered by one question after another. He got nervous. After this, the officers apprehended him. Under strict interrogation, he confessed to the crime. He narrated his entire story. After this, the army handed him over to the police. See 3 pictures Read the entire incident in sequence Mother is a government teacher, father is an inspector Aryan Verma, a resident of the Roja area, comes from a well-off family and lives in a three-story house. His father, Anil Verma, is an inspector in the Horticulture Department in Powayan, while his mother, Manoj Devi, is a government teacher in Jalalpur. He also has a younger brother studying in Class 4. Failed NEET twice, then posed as army officer After completing intermediate, Aryan was sent to Delhi to prepare for NEET. He appeared for the exam twice but failed both times. During police questioning, he said that due to family pressure, he bought a Brigadier's uniform in Delhi in January, hired two boys, and told his family he had been selected for the Army. He then began moving around in the uniform. Know how officers laid a trap and caught him Fake ID, pistol, and baton recovered A fake pistol, forged documents, a baton (stick), and military insignia were recovered from Aryan. Late Friday night, Naib Subedar Amit Kumar filed a complaint against Aryan. Based on the army's complaint, an FIR was registered against him, and he was handed over to the police. He had also put up an 'Army Brigadier' nameplate outside his house. His car also had 'Army' and 'Doctor' written on it. Admin Commandant Colonel JS Jagran stated that a person roaming under suspicious circumstances in the cantonment area was taken into custody. Objectionable and suspicious material was found in his possession. All aspects are being thoroughly investigated.

stories.title: 22-year-old fake brigadier busted in UP:Hired 2 bogus NSG commandos driver; army officers lured him to an event before arrest
stories.summary: A 22-year-old man posing as a Brigadier was detained in Shahjahanpur by the Military Police. Dressed in a Brigadier's uniform, he was accompanied by two men in NSG commando uniforms and a driver. Authorities recovered a fake Army identity card, a replica pistol, and several Army-related documents. The youth, identified as Aryan Verma (22) from Roza city, had arrived at the Shaheed Sangrahalaya in the Cantonment area in a Harrier SUV carrying an Army flag. His suspicious behavior alerted ex-servicemen and museum staff, who informed the Army, leading to his detention. Full story in detail Fake ID, pistol, and baton recovered Military police recovered a fake army identity card, a fake pistol, and a baton (stick) used by Brigadier-level officers from Aryan's possession. He had also put up a nameplate with the name Brigadier at his house. He had hired a car driver, from whom a fake government identity card was found. In addition, two security personnel were also in NSG commando uniforms. Aryan's father, Anil Verma, is an inspector in the Horticulture Department in the Puwayan area, while his mother, Manoj Devi, is a government teacher in Jalalpur, Sadar Tehsil area. He also has a younger brother in the family, who studies in class four. Army Intelligence is interrogating Considering the seriousness of the matter, a special Army Intelligence team from Bareilly has reached Shahjahanpur. Currently, the youth is being interrogated by military officials. He has not yet been handed over to the local police. Further action will be taken after the army's interrogation is complete. Admin Commandant Colonel JS Jagran stated that a person roaming in suspicious circumstances in the Cantonment area has been taken into custody. Some objectionable and suspicious material has been found in his possession. The matter is being investigated under military rules, and all aspects are being thoroughly examined.

stories.title: UP cop alleges deep-rooted corruption:Constable says 'Posting depends on money'; are police officers really 'Black Englishmen'?
stories.summary: No constable in the police department wants to be involved in bribery, but officers will send them to bring okra for 10 rupees, and the okra costs ₹12. Then, on the way, they will call and say to bring pumpkin too. If they don't bring it, they will be removed, and problems will start. They will have to clean the bathroom. If they don't want to clean the bathroom, then make all arrangements for the sir. This is the statement of a UP Police constable, who is revealing the secrets of bribery in his department. Recently, Constable Sunil Kumar Shukla, posted at Lucknow Police Line, released a video calling police officers 'black Englishmen'. Sunil had said - police officers take money for every task. I myself have had to pay bribes. How much truth is there in Constable Sunil's words, to know this, Dainik Bhaskar's team investigated. We spoke to several policemen on a hidden camera. Some of them clearly stated how the rate for getting duty in lucrative and comfortable places is fixed. How does corruption work from top to bottom? Read the full revelation Know what Constable Sunil had said Constable Sunil Kumar Shukla said, In the Reserve Police Line of Lucknow Police Commissionerate, a zamindari system of loot is being run by 'black Englishmen' i.e., tyrannical officers. A constable-havildar pays 2 thousand rupees to get his duty assigned. RI (Reserve Inspector) sir cuts his share and presents the remaining money at the feet of these 'black English' officers. In a conversation with Bhaskar, Sunil narrated 3 incidents of transactions Incident-1: Money has to be paid to get HRA assigned Not only do you have to pay money to get a duty assigned, but you also have to go twice a year to get HRA assigned. For this, too, you will have to pay 200-200 rupees. Those who have a 'setting' get it done for 100 rupees. This means you will have to pay 100-200 rupees. Incident-2: Medical Babu took ₹4500 bribe from me My wife's delivery took place in Raebareli. I went to Medical Clerk Shailendra Kumar with the bill for a medical reimbursement of 50 thousand rupees. He said that I will get you 45 thousand rupees. In this way, I gave Shailendra Kumar a bribe of 5000 rupees. (In this matter, Clerk Shailendra Kumar, posted in Sitapur, says that he does not know Sunil Shukla, so he cannot say anything) Incident-3: Money goes up through the Guard Commander In Lucknow, too, money is taken in the name of duty. If you have to go on guard (special duty), you will have to pay ₹2 thousand per month, everyone knows this. Constables give, and guard commanders take. Money is collected through the guard commander. Then this money reaches the officers. To find out if Sunil was telling the truth, we spoke to Constable Mohit Kumar (name changed) posted in Kushinagar. At the constable's request, we are not disclosing his name and identity here. Reporter: Sunil Shukla has made serious allegations. Are they true? Constable: Yes, what he said is true. These things happen. Some places have it more, some less. Reporter: How are duties assigned? Constable: The Head Moharrir decides. Those who pay get favorable postings; those who don't are sent to stand at crossroads in the heat. Reporter: Does the location affect the amount paid? Constable: Yes. The more convenient the posting, the higher the payment. Everything works on a fixed system. Reporter: Is there a separate arrangement for crossroads duty? Constable: People who want to earn more pay accordingly and get better postings. It's all about money. Reporter: Does money also go to senior officers? Constable: It's a channel-based system. Money moves step by step from lower levels to higher levels. Reporter: What about police outposts and police stations? Constable: An outpost costs more than a crossroads posting. Those who pay nothing are often sent for post-mortem duty. Reporter: What's difficult about post-mortem duty? Constable: Many expenses come from your own pocket. You handle paperwork, bodies arriving at night, and other responsibilities. After this, we spoke to Constable Vivek Kumar (name changed), posted in Gorakhpur Police for the past 10 years. He also backed Sunil Shukla's claims. Constable: Everything Shukla ji said is true. Not a single word is wrong. Reporter: How widespread is bribery in the police department? Constable: New recruits don't want to take bribes, but the system forces them. If you're sent to buy vegetables worth ₹10 and the cost is ₹12, then more items are added later. If you don't manage it, you'll face trouble and be assigned undesirable work like cleaning bathrooms. Reporter: So other expenses come from your pocket? Constable: Yes. If an unidentified body is found and you're assigned duty, expenses from the post-mortem to the cremation often have to be managed personally. Reporter: Are all officers the same? Constable: No. Officers like Ajay Pal Sharma, Rohit Singh Sajwan, Durga Shakti Nagpal, Akash Kulhari, Navneet Sikera and Aseem Arun are different. They don't create undue pressure and ensure fair working conditions. Reporter: Shukla ji says an honest person cannot survive in the police department. Constable: Absolutely. It's very difficult for an honest person to survive, and if someone tries, it disrupts the existing system for others. Investigation revealed these points Who is Constable Sunil? Constable Sunil Shukla, posted in the Reserve Police Line of Lucknow Police Commissionerate, is a 2015 batch constable. He hails from Pure Ramsevak Mishra village in Gauriganj, Amethi district. His father, the late Harikaran Shukla, was a home guard. His wife, Sudha Tripathi, is posted as a Head Constable in Raebareli. Sunil has released 7 videos in a little over a month. Constable Sunil has been suspended after a departmental inquiry for making and sharing videos on police corruption, thereby tarnishing the department's image, and for ignoring rules. However, even after the suspension, his attitude has not softened. In a video released on May 10, Sunil directly questioned the Chief Minister, asking if he was a criminal, terrorist, or Naxalite, for which police were sent to his house at 1 am.

stories.title: 'Lost my son, yet couldn’t get Katra gang chief punished’:Ghazipur father waits 5 years for justice; alleges police protected criminal
stories.summary: Don’t take my photograph. Those people are dangerous. They have strong connections with the police and politicians. My son's murder case reached the court, but Shankar never appeared even once. As he says this, tears well up in the eyes of Vinod Singh, father of student Anshuman Singh, who was murdered five years ago by Shankar Pandey, the alleged leader of the Katra Gang. Following the recent daylight murder of hotel businessman Vineet Rai in Ghazipur, renewed attention has turned to Anshuman’s case. The court has now issued a non-bailable warrant (NBW) against Shankar. Dainik Bhaskar spoke to Vinod Singh, who has been fighting the murder case. He says: Why would Shankar ever be punished? The Ghazipur police use him for heroin trafficking. The police themselves nurtured and protected him. Kidnapping people, assaulting them and throwing them by the roadside was completely normal for the Katra Gang. He adds, Only after a major crime happened did everyone remember Shankar. Now old cases linked to him are being heard more actively. People know only a few stories about the Katra Gang because the police never recorded most incidents. Shankar got many people killed, but only the murders of Vineet and Anshuman were officially registered against him. Gang formed in class 10, first murder after class 12 Shankar Pandey has a luxurious house spread over nearly 2,000 square feet in the Gausabad area of Ghazipur city. The house is currently locked. His entire family is absconding, while his father is lodged in a jail in West Bengal in a drug trafficking case. Shankar studied in an English-medium school. According to local accounts, he began group rivalries and violent clashes while studying in Class 10 in 2014. After passing Class 12 in 2016, he allegedly turned crime into a full-time profession. That same year, Anshuman Singh from the village of Utarauli in Revatipur also completed Class 12. He had studied at Adarsh Inter College in Ghazipur city and later enrolled in a B.Com course at PG College. After some time, he joined a coaching institute in Lucknow to prepare for competitive examinations. Threats began after dispute with gang member During his school days, Anshuman had a dispute with Satyam Rai and some of his friends, who were associated with the Katra Gang. After the altercation, Shankar allegedly called Anshuman several times and threatened him. Anshuman remained disturbed but never discussed the issue with his family. Vinod Singh recalls, Anshuman had come home during the Holi holidays. We learned from his friends that he was troubled and that some boys were harassing him. We told him to stay in Ghazipur and focus on his graduation studies instead of returning elsewhere. He agreed. First attack foiled by residents Anshuman later began living in a colony in Ghazipur city along with his friend Raghvendra and a relative’s son. Vinod says, Everything was fine until February 2020, when Shankar and members of his gang carried out the first attack. They entered the colony, abused and assaulted Anshuman. However, residents came to help and chased the gang away. While leaving, they threatened, ‘We are going now, but you will not survive. Called for a compromise, then attacked On March 21, 2020, Satyam Rai called Anshuman and asked him to come near the Shah Junaid Pir Dargah in Saklenabad, saying they wanted to settle the dispute. Anshuman went there with his friend Raghvendra. He had no idea that Shankar Pandey and his associates would also be present. When they saw that the group was carrying sticks and rods, they tried to step back. However, the attackers immediately launched an assault. More than 10 youths, including Priyanshu Singh, Saurabh Singh, Bobby Sarkar, Ranjeet, and Abhishek, were allegedly present with Shankar. They brutally beat Anshuman and Raghvendra with sticks, rods, and hockey sticks before pulling out knives. Repeated attacks were made on Anshuman’s legs, arms, and neck. Raghvendra’s jaw was severely fractured. Believing both victims were dead, the attackers fled. People who heard the commotion near the shrine rushed to the spot and took them to a hospital. Anshuman could not be saved. Raghvendra was referred to Varanasi and survived after nearly a month of treatment. Police arrested four, Shankar escaped Vinod Singh says, ‘Based on details provided by Raghvendra, I filed a case against Shankar Pandey, Priyanshu Singh, Bobby Sarkar, Saurabh Singh and seven unidentified attackers.’ Four days later, police arrested Priyanshu, Saurabh, Ranjeet Rajbhar, and Abhishek Kumar from behind Ghazipur Railway Station. However, Shankar managed to evade arrest. BJP booth president says justice remains elusive Vinod Singh has been an active BJP worker for 42 years and currently serves as a booth president in Ghazipur. He says, 'I lost my son. I left no stone unturned. I fought this case from the police station to the courtroom with all my strength. Yet I could not ensure concrete action against Shankar Pandey.' He adds, ‘Only after Vineet was murdered in the same brutal manner did people remember Anshuman. Over the last five to six years, Shankar and his gang have been involved in four or five more murders. They have strong connections with police and politicians. Check Shankar’s record, he has never remained in jail for more than two months. In our case, he never appeared in court. Only his lawyer attended hearings.’ He further claims, ‘Katra Gang member Bobby Sarkar belongs to the family of mafia figure Ranjeet Singh. Their legal system is fixed, they spend some time in jail, and then secure bail.’ Breaking down while narrating his son’s story, Vinod says, ‘Why would Shankar be punished? Police personnel in Ghazipur use him for heroin trafficking. They raised and protected him. Kidnapping people or publicly assaulting them had become very easy for the Katra Gang. Only after this major crime did people realize what kind of criminal he really was.’ Court issues non-bailable warrant The Anshuman murder case is being heard in a Ghazipur court. Assistant District Government Counsel Akhilesh Singh, who is handling the case, said: 'Shankar was repeatedly failing to appear before the court. Police had already announced a reward of ₹1 lakh on him. We placed these facts before Additional District Judge Shakti Singh, after which a non-bailable warrant was issued. He has been ordered to appear before the court on June 25.' Other cases and ongoing search Akhilesh Singh also cited another case in which garment trader Sachin Chaurasia was allegedly assaulted and kidnapped in broad daylight on September 5, 2024, by Shankar Pandey and Kamlesh Chaudhary, who was later killed in a police encounter. According to Singh, traffic congestion prevented the accused from escaping with the victim, forcing them to abandon him and flee. A non-bailable warrant has also been issued in that case. If Shankar fails to appear, proceedings under Sections 82 and 83 can be initiated, declaring him a proclaimed offender and allowing attachment of his properties. Shankar faces 10 criminal cases, including murder, attempted murder, kidnapping, and assault. Two of his close associates, Alok Dubey and Sonu Yadav, are also absconding, with rewards of ₹1 lakh each announced on them. Police are conducting raids in Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal, and Jharkhand. Although Ghazipur police have identified 49 gangs in the district, including the Katra Gang, no member of the gang has yet been arrested in the current crackdown. Shankar’s social media accounts continue to feature videos portraying power and influence, including clips in which police personnel are seen folding their hands before him.

stories.title: Pre-monsoon activity intensifies in UP:Rain in 20 cities, homes flooded in Kanpur; 4 dead in weather-related incidents
stories.summary: Pre-monsoon activity has intensified across Uttar Pradesh, bringing rain to around 20 cities, including Kanpur, Ayodhya, and Unnao. In Lucknow, dark clouds covered the sky at around 7:45 am on Saturday, followed by strong winds and heavy rainfall. Dust storms were reported in Kaushambi and Unnao, while Pratapgarh and Prayagraj witnessed daytime darkness before rain, and strong winds lashed the areas. Heavy rainfall caused waterlogging in several districts. In Hathras, rainwater flooded the Sadar police station premises, while roads were submerged. In Kanpur, rainwater entered residential houses, and several roads in Hardoi were seen inundated. At least four people lost their lives in weather-related incidents. In Unnao, a farmer died after being struck by lightning. In Kasganj, a husband, wife, and their daughter were killed when the roof slab of their house collapsed during the storm and rain. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a rain alert for 54 districts and a thunderstorm warning for 22 cities today. According to the IMD, a fresh western disturbance has become active over the region, strengthening pre-monsoon conditions. As a result, thunderstorms and rainfall are expected to continue for the time being. During the last 24 hours, rainfall was recorded in 15 cities across the state. Jalaun remained the hottest district with a maximum temperature of 40.8°C. See 3 pictures from Friday- Lucknow's senior meteorological scientist, Atul Kumar Singh, said- The spell of pre-monsoon rain has started in UP. Now the spell of storms and rain will continue in the state until the entry of monsoon. In between, the heat will also show its intensity, but the rain will continue to provide relief from it. For now, the spell of storms and rain will continue till 15-16 June. Monsoon will enter the state by its scheduled time, that is, by 20 June. How will the weather be for the next 5 days

stories.title: Five-year-old asks when father will return:Deoria family mourns Merchant Navy worker killed after reported US strike near Hormuz
stories.summary: The family of Shivanand Chaurasia, a 38-year-old Merchant Navy crew member from Deoria district, is mourning his reported death in a U.S. strike while he was serving aboard the Singapore-registered oil tanker MT Settebello. His father, Ramji Chaurasia, said the family had borrowed nearly ₹6 lakh to finance his son’s Continuous Discharge Certificate (CDC), a mandatory seafarer’s document, and training for a maritime career. “We took loans to send him to work at sea. He was the only earning member of the family. We never imagined his first voyage would become his last,” the grieving father said. Ramji said that the hopes of the entire family were tied to Shivanand. After he got the job, happiness had returned to the house. Now there is only silence in the house. The screams and sobs rising from the house are making everyone's eyes moist. His wife is repeatedly fainting. His mother and sisters are in a terrible state from crying. Dainik Bhaskar reached Shivanand's village. Read the report… See 3 pictures Five-year-old son keeps asking for his father Shivanand is survived by his wife Sushila, a five-year-old son, Rajveer, and a two-year-old daughter, Vanika. According to the family, the young boy is unaware of his father’s death and repeatedly asks, “When will Papa come home?” His relatives are struggling to comfort him as the household copes with the tragedy. Journey from village to merchant navy A resident of Surauli village, around 10 km from Deoria district headquarters, Shivanand completed his schooling before leaving home in 2012 in search of work. He worked in several cities, including Dubai, Mumbai, Lucknow, Pune, and Solapur, before completing a Merchant Navy course and obtaining his CDC certification. The family financed the process through loans from relatives and villagers. In September 2025, he joined a shipping company in Singapore as an engine fitter with a monthly salary of around ₹45,000. Father says, ‘Decision to stay on ship proved fatal’ Ramji Chaurasia said the vessel had unloaded oil in China on May 23, after which some colleagues advised Shivaanand to leave the ship and take a break. However, hoping to repay the family’s debts quickly, he decided to remain on board. According to his father, another vessel operated by the same company had suffered technical problems before reaching the Strait of Hormuz, leading to cargo being transferred onto MT Settebello. The family says Shivaanand was killed when the vessel reportedly came under attack near Hormuz on Wednesday. They were informed of the incident through his younger brother, who received communication from the Indian Embassy in Oman. Wife recalls final conversation Sushila said her husband called on Tuesday evening and asked about the children’s well-being. “When the children started crying, he told me to put them to sleep first and call him back later,” she recalled. The call ended, and she never spoke to him again. The following day, after she failed to reach him, relatives eventually informed her that his ship had reportedly been struck. Family appeals for early repatriation of body Sanjay Chaurasia, Shivaanand’s brother-in-law, appealed to the government to ensure the body is brought back to India as soon as possible. He said the family has not yet received a clear timeline regarding the repatriation and is anxiously awaiting official information. Local administration assures assistance Additional District Magistrate Prem Narayan Singh visited the family to offer condolences and assured them that efforts were underway to bring Shivaanand’s remains back to India. Officials expressed hope that the repatriation process could be completed within the next few days. Younger brother returning From Dubai Shivaanand’s younger brother, Ram Pravesh Chaurasia, who had recently moved to Dubai for work, has returned to India after learning of the tragedy. He is expected to reach the family’s ancestral village after arriving in Gorakhpur.

stories.title: Pallavi Patel detained in Varanasi:Scuffle with police during NEET paper leak protest;100 supporters detained
stories.summary: Pallavi Patel, president of Apna Dal (Kamerawadi), and about 100 of her supporters have been arrested by the police in Varanasi. Pallavi Patel was protesting at the BHU gate on Monday over issues including the NEET paper leak. After this, she was going to march to PM Modi's parliamentary office. But the police, citing the lack of permission for the protest, loaded everyone into a van. During this, Pallavi Patel started having difficulty breathing. Then, screaming, she said, 'Open the van door, I get panic attacks.' During this, she also had an altercation with the police. Demand for CBI investigation into paper leak Pallavi Patel demanded a CBI investigation into the NEET paper leak under the supervision of judicial officers. She said, the names of people involved in paper leaks and irregularities should be made public. Action under NSA should be taken against NTA and other examination controlling officers and they should be sent to jail. Pallavi Patel demanded re-examination in view of allegations of rigging in the Uttar Pradesh Lekhpal Recruitment Examination, and immediate release of scorecards to guarantee a transparent UP SI examination. Government should move beyond Pakistan, graveyard and Muslims Before being detained, Pallavi Patel said - Modi, Yogi's double engine government should move beyond the politics of Pakistan, graveyard and Muslims. It should move towards politics that strengthens education, employment and democracy. Youth unemployment, the looting of opportunities in the name of employment, and rigging in education and examinations are now inciting them towards revolution. The youth are angry with this government. See pictures related to the protest Protesters had prepared to march from BHU's Lanka Gate to the Prime Minister's Public Relations Office, 2 kilometers away. The administration tightened security arrangements on the proposed route and deployed police forces. Before the protest, officials of several organizations were placed under house arrest. The administration stated that necessary steps were taken to maintain law and order. Police Commissioner Mohit Agrawal said, "Permission was not taken from the administration for the proposed protest." Car stopped at Jaunpur toll plaza, Pallavi exited via a footpath Upon receiving information about Pallavi Patel's arrival in Varanasi for the protest, police from the respective districts were deployed at the district borders and toll plazas. Around 9 PM on Sunday night, when Pallavi arrived at the plaza in Jaunpur with her convoy, the police tried to cordon her off and stop her. Meanwhile, she got out of the car with two activists and headed towards the field. After walking for about one kilometer with her mobile phone switched off, she reached the main road. She entered the Varanasi border by sitting in a crowded auto-rickshaw. She switched on her mobile phone and sent her location to party officials, who then came to pick her up. They took her to an activist's house in Babatpur, where she stayed overnight. On Monday morning at 11 AM, she arrived to join the protest at the BHU gate.

stories.title: Thief kisses sleeping woman in Bareilly:Holds husband at gunpoint; throws 3-year-old daughter on cot
stories.summary: In Bareilly, 4 thieves broke into a factory worker's house on Sunday night. They reached near a woman who was sleeping on a cot with her 3-year-old daughter in one room. One thief kissed her. Just then the woman woke up. Seeing the thieves, she raised an alarm. At this, the thieves picked up the daughter and threw her on the cot. When the woman's husband, who was sleeping in another room, woke up hearing the noise, the thieves took him hostage. Pointing a pistol, they said - Where have you kept the valuables? Tell us or we'll kill you. During this, the wife ran out of the house with her daughter in her arms. She started screaming upon seeing a police vehicle on the road. When the policemen stopped the vehicle hearing the noise, the thieves who were chasing fled. The case is from Cantt police station area. The woman has filed a case against 4 people at the police station. Forgot to close main door, threatened by showing a pistol A 30-year-old youth living in a village said - I work in a sewing factory. At home, I have a 28-year-old wife and a 3-year-old daughter. On Sunday night, I returned from the factory. After having dinner with the family, I went to sleep. My wife and daughter slept in one room. I went to sleep in another room. I had forgotten to close the main door of the house. Around 3 AM at night, 4 people entered through that door. One of the thieves went to my wife who was sleeping with our daughter in the room. He kissed the wife's face. During this, the wife's sleep was broken. She started screaming loudly. Hearing the noise, I reached the spot, then the thieves pointed a pistol at me. When my daughter started crying, one thief snatched her from my wife's lap and threw her on the cot. They put a noose of towel around my wife's neck and started tightening it. When I protested, they held me hostage in the room. They asked me where the goods are kept? Where are the gold-silver jewelry and money? Tell quickly, otherwise I will shoot you. Police are scanning CCTV Husband said - After this, the wife ran outside shouting with the daughter in her arms. Then one of the thieves threw a stick at her. But the wife came out of the house onto the street. She was running while making noise. The thieves also started running after her. Just then, seeing the police vehicle, the wife started screaming loudly. Seeing the wife running, the policemen stopped the vehicle. She told the police everything. Meanwhile, the thieves fled. Inspector Rakesh Kumar said that a case has been registered against 4 people based on the victim's complaint. CCTV footage installed around the house is being examined. Further action will be taken based on the facts that emerge during the investigation. Drug users gather nearby CO City First Ashutosh Shivam said that the victim family has denied having any kind of dispute with anyone. The victims say that there is a tree near their house, under which some people often sit and consume drugs. The police are investigating keeping this aspect in mind as well and gathering information about suspicious people in the vicinity. Police have examined approximately 10 CCTV footages from the surrounding area. More CCTVs are still being examined. Through these footages, efforts are being made to identify the suspects and trace their activities. The police team is investigating all aspects and claims to reach the accused soon.

stories.title: Girl dies in blast at firecracker factory in Lucknow:1 injured; sound heard up to 2 km away, house completely collapsed
stories.summary: On Monday, a firecracker factory exploded in Lucknow. The sound of the blast was heard up to about 2 kilometers away. The explosion was so intense that the building housing the factory completely collapsed and bricks were scattered everywhere. In the incident, a young woman died, while a young man is seriously injured. Upon receiving information, the Fire Brigade, SDRF, and Bomb Disposal Squad reached the spot. Police are investigating the causes of the explosion. There were no other houses around the firecracker factory, but hearing the sound of the blast, villagers rushed to the spot. The incident occurred in the Nagram police station area. See 3 pictures Explosion occurred in licensed firecracker factory According to police, the explosion occurred in the firecracker factory of Mo. Shafiq (26), a resident of village Devti. The factory is licensed and is located outside the village. A major disaster was averted as there was no population nearby. In the accident, Maria (22) and Mohit were seriously injured. Maria died during treatment. She was the niece of the factory owner. Mohit's condition is critical and his treatment is ongoing. Mohit is a resident of the village. At the time of the incident, he was grazing animals and had come near the factory to drink water. In the preliminary investigation, there is no information about any other casualties. The fire brigade team that arrived after the incident brought the fire under control. Crowd gathered after hearing the explosion sound According to people nearby, the incident occurred around 11:30 AM. The explosion was so loud that its sound was heard up to about one and a half to two kilometers away. Hearing the explosion sound, people from the surrounding area rushed to the spot. Villagers say that if this incident had occurred in the evening, when there is more movement of people, it could have caused major damage. People breathed a sigh of relief due to minimal loss of life. Fire brigade arrived immediately upon receiving information, several vehicles deployed FSO Satyendra Kumar Singh of Gosaiganj Fire Station said that information about the explosion at the firecracker factory was received at 11:18 AM. As soon as the information was received, the fire team left for the spot with vehicles at 11:19 AM. Considering the severity of the fire, two additional fire tenders from PGI Fire Station and one MDRV (Multi Disaster Response Vehicle) from Hazratganj along with several vehicles were sent to the spot. Fire personnel continuously poured water to control the fire and prevented potential danger. As a precautionary measure after the accident, more than 5 ambulances were also deployed at the spot. Debris being removed by JCB After the explosion at the firecracker factory, the Bomb Disposal and Detection Squad (BDDS) also reached the spot. The team has started investigating the site. The causes of the explosion are being ascertained. The entire area has been kept under surveillance for security. Debris is being removed with the help of JCB under the supervision of the administration. The relief and rescue team is conducting a search considering the possibility of any other person being trapped under the debris. According to officials, the actual assessment of the damage can be done after the debris is removed. Factory was running since 1995 Atiq, from the family of factory operator Mohd. Shafiq, told Dainik Bhaskar that they have been in the firecracker manufacturing business since 1995. Earlier his father used to run the factory. About three years ago, after his father's demise, his brother Shafiq has been looking after this work. The factory was built on their private land. According to Atiq, at the time of the accident, workers Suraj and niece Maria were present in the factory premises. Maria had come home during summer vacation and had gone to the factory while roaming around. Suraj was cleaning utensils near the trees outside the factory, so he did not come under the impact of the explosion. Brother Shafiq had come to check the tile work at home. Local youth Mohit was grazing buffalo nearby. He had come to drink water from the tap in the premises. He was injured when a piece of brick hit him during the explosion. Atiq stated that there were three rooms in the factory. Firecrackers were made in one room. Stock was kept in the second. Finished firecrackers were kept in the third. At the time of the accident, approximately three to four kilograms of gunpowder was present in the factory. DCP South Amit Kumar Anand stated- Information was received about an explosion at a licensed firecracker factory in Gram Devti, Thana Nagram. Local police and fire brigade reached the spot upon receiving the information. The fire was brought under control. The causes of the explosion are being investigated.

stories.title: Mother breaks down hugging martyr's coffin:Family told not to view body after officer's advice; air crash claimed son's life
stories.summary: Jitendra Sharma from Aligarh was martyred in an Indian Air Force AN-32 transport aircraft crash in Assam during landing on Saturday morning around 10 am. His mortal remains are expected to reach his native village on Monday around 2 pm. Circle Officer Khair, Sanjeev Kumar Tomar, informed the family that coordination has been completed with concerned officials. It has also been decided that the coffin of martyr Jitendra Sharma will not be opened. Meanwhile, the martyr’s 72-year-old mother, Rajeshwari, has not yet been informed about his death due to her prolonged heart ailment. She has been kept alone at home to avoid any shock, while other family members, including his sisters and brother, have reached the village and are staying at their uncle’s residence. The family remains in deep grief. The village atmosphere is filled with mourning as well as pride, with slogans being raised in honour of the martyr. Banners and hoardings have been put up across the village, paying tribute to his sacrifice. The Indian Air Force AN-32 crash had claimed the lives of Jitendra Sharma and four others. Know who was Sergeant Jitendra Sharma Jitendra Sharma, a resident of village Salpur in Aligarh, was the youngest among seven siblings. In the family, his mother Rajeshwari Devi and two elder brothers Ramakant and Bhupendra live together. He was selected in the Indian Air Force on January 1, 2015. He served the nation for about 11 years. He completed his high school and intermediate education from DRG Inter College, Dhanipura Kurana in the Tappal area. After that, he took coaching in Aligarh and was selected in the Indian Air Force. Jitendra's father Kalicharan alias Karua Sharma had passed away about 12 years ago. After the father's death, mother Rajeshwari Devi raised all the children. Family members said that Jitendra had recently come to the village on leave and returned to duty on June 5. Discussions were also going on in the house regarding his wedding preparations. He had also seen a girl for marriage and the family was about to proceed with the wedding process soon. But before that, he died in the accident, which turned the entire family's happiness into mourning.

stories.title: Commercial flight operations begin at Noida's Jewar Airport:Land-donor farmers meet CM Yogi in Lucknow; Doctor says, 'You should become PM'
stories.summary: Noida's Jewar International Airport has commenced flight operations. On Monday, an IndiGo flight from Lucknow landed at the airport for the first time and was welcomed with a traditional water cannon salute. The aircraft is scheduled to continue onward to Bengaluru with 161 passengers on board. In another flight, around 170 farmers, including 20 women who had given their land for the airport's construction, travelled from Noida to Lucknow to meet Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath. During this, Dr. Hera Rashid told CM Yogi, “The land from which I flew today is the same land where my father once grew crops. There was a time when educational opportunities were limited in our area. As development reached the region, infrastructure and facilities improved. I cleared NEET without any coaching. All this became possible because of the development that took place. I hope to see you become the Prime Minister one day." See Pictures- Among 170 farmers, there are also 20 women farmers. Their land was also acquired for airport construction.Kamlesh, who arrived in Lucknow from Noida, said that she has given 4 bighas of land for the airport construction. Earlier, upon arriving at Lucknow Airport in a wheelchair, farmer Kamlesh said she was delighted with the experience. Another farmer, Rita, said she had given four bighas of land for the airport project and was travelling by air for the first time. “I thoroughly enjoyed it. A journey that would normally take seven hours was completed in just one hour. We will also visit the Ram Temple,” she said. Farmer Shame Mohammad described the trip as a memorable experience for the farming community. “We are extremely happy to be here. Chief Ministers have visited us before, but this is the first time anyone has arranged air travel for farmers. No one has ever given us an opportunity like this,” he said. Hyderabad, Amritsar flights also begin today Regular flight services to Hyderabad and Amritsar will also commence from Jewar International Airport on Monday. From June 16, IndiGo will operate scheduled flights from Noida to Bengaluru and Jammu. Akasa Air is also set to launch daily services from Noida to Bengaluru and Navi Mumbai from June 16. In the coming weeks, flight operations are expected to begin for several other destinations, including Bareilly, Srinagar, Jaipur, Jodhpur, Dharamshala, Bhopal, Chandigarh, Kishangarh and Dehradun.

stories.title: Chinese manjha slits neck of minister's nephew in Bareilly:Scooter rider critical; minister furious over continued sale despite ban
stories.summary: In Bareilly, the neck of a 15-year-old nephew of the Sugarcane Minister of State was cut by Chinese manja. He was going home on a scooter. Suddenly on the flyover, the Chinese manja wrapped around his neck. Before he could understand anything, a significant portion of his neck was cut. Aditya Veer Singh Gangwar fell on the road with his scooter. His entire body was drenched in blood. People nearby immediately took him to a private hospital. The family was informed. The incident occurred on Monday at 1 PM. At that time, the Minister of State was on a tour to Pilibhit. Upon hearing the news of the accident with his nephew, he left the tour and reached Bareilly. Aditya Veer Singh's father Ajay Singh Gangwar is the Block Chief of Lalauri Kheda block in Pilibhit. Mother Seema Gangwar is an officer in the Railways. While Sugarcane Minister of State Sanjay Gangwar is his uncle. The accident occurred on Shyamganj Flyover in the middle of Bareilly city. Minister said - How is manja being sold despite ban? Aditya Veer is undergoing treatment at Ishan Hospital. According to doctors, his condition is still critical. The minister who reached the hospital got furious seeing his nephew's condition. He said - The government has already banned Chinese manja. Despite this, its sale in the market is a serious matter. I will call both the DM and SSP to discuss. Strict action should be taken against those selling Chinese manja. It should also be investigated how it is being supplied in the market. State Minister Sanjay Singh Gangwar said- My nephew Aditya Veer was going from home to the stadium in the morning. On the way, his throat was cut from front to back by Chinese manja. One of his fingers has also been completely severed. He was just in the OT, I came after seeing him and his condition is critical right now. Accident occurred at 6 AM while going to stadium Aditya's family is originally from Pilibhit. However, they also have a house in Premnagar, Bareilly. Aditya studies in class 9. At 6 AM in the morning, he was going to the stadium on a scooter. That's when the accident happened. Many accidents have happened before Accidents due to Chinese manja are continuously occurring in several districts of the state including Bareilly. Despite this, a complete ban on its sale has not been implemented. After the latest incident, questions have once again been raised about the administration's action and effective implementation of the ban.

stories.title: Mukesh Ambani offers prayers at Kedarnath and Badrinath:Performs 'abhishek', donates ₹10 crore; greets devotees chanting 'Jai Shri Ram'
stories.summary: Reliance Industries Chairman Mukesh Ambani visited the Badrinath and Kedarnath shrines in Uttarakhand on Sunday morning, offering prayers at both temples and announcing a donation of ₹10 crore for the two pilgrimage sites. Ambani’s helicopter landed at the Badrinath helipad at around 10 am. About 20 minutes later, he proceeded to the temple and offered prayers to Lord Badri Vishal. He spent nearly 10 minutes performing rituals before meeting office-bearers of the Shri Badrinath-Kedarnath Temple Committee. During the meeting, Ambani announced a contribution of ₹10 crore for the development and management of the two Himalayan shrines. His helicopter then departed from Badrinath at 10.40 am for Kedarnath. The industrialist arrived at Kedarnath at around 11.15 am and reached the temple within minutes. There, he performed jalabhishek of Lord Kedarnath and took part in special puja rituals. As devotees gathered around him and raised chants of “Jai Shri Ram”, Ambani greeted them with folded hands. He also acknowledged devotees who called out his name during the visit. After completing the pilgrimage, Ambani left for Delhi at around noon. This was not his first visit to the Char Dham shrines. He had earlier visited Badrinath and Kedarnath on October 10, 2025. Security personnel from the Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP) accompanied Ambani during his visit to Badrinath and Keda See pictures- Char Dham Yatra crosses 3.7 million pilgrims The annual Char Dham Yatra began on April 19, on the occasion of Akshaya Tritiya, with the opening of the portals of Gangotri and Yamunotri. The first puja at Gangotri was performed in the name of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, in the presence of Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami. The portals of Kedarnath were opened on April 22, followed by Badrinath on April 23. According to the State Emergency Operations Centre, more than 3.7 million pilgrims have visited the four shrines in the 57 days since the yatra began. Kedarnath has recorded the highest footfall with over 1.2 million devotees, followed by Badrinath with more than 1 million visitors. Gangotri has received nearly 600,000 pilgrims, while over 573,000 devotees have visited Yamunotri. Nearly 200 pilgrim deaths reported during yatra A total of 196 pilgrim deaths have been reported so far across the Char Dham circuit and the Hemkund Sahib route during the ongoing pilgrimage season. Kedarnath has recorded the highest number of deaths at 94, followed by Badrinath with 59. Yamunotri has reported 26 deaths, while Gangotri has recorded 17 fatalities. According to the Health Department, most deaths have been linked to pre-existing medical conditions, cardiac arrest and high-altitude-related illnesses. The pilgrimage routes pass through mountainous terrain where reduced oxygen levels and strenuous climbs can aggravate health problems, particularly among elderly devotees and those with underlying medical conditions. Ahead of the yatra, the state government conducted a series of review meetings and directed departments to complete preparations in advance. Authorities have said adequate arrangements were made for healthcare services, doctors and medical staff along the pilgrimage route. The government also issued advisories urging elderly pilgrims and those suffering from high blood pressure, diabetes or heart ailments to undergo medical check-ups before undertaking the journey. Health officials have repeatedly appealed to pilgrims to exercise caution and seek immediate medical assistance if they experience any discomfort during the trek.

stories.title: Owaisi offers alliance to stop BJP in UP:Announces first candidate from Bahraich; says AIMIM seeks respect and equal status
stories.summary: Political activity has intensified ahead of the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi launched his election campaign from Bahraich and announced the party's first candidate. He also indicated that AIMIM is open to forming an alliance to defeat the BJP, although he did not clarify whether the alliance could be with the Samajwadi Party (SP) or the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP). Speaking to reporters on Monday, Owaisi said AIMIM was willing to join an alliance in Uttar Pradesh if the party was treated with respect and given equal status. "We are ready for an alliance to stop the BJP in UP, provided we are treated with respect and given equal status. We are contesting the Assembly elections with full strength," he said. He added that state president Shaukat Ali and party workers were working extensively across the state. Rejects claim that Muslim votes belong to SP When asked whether Muslim voters were firmly behind the Samajwadi Party, Owaisi dismissed the suggestion. "No one is with anyone. AIMIM has emerged strongly. Those making such claims will realise the reality," he said. Addressing a rally in Bahraich, Owaisi urged supporters to unite and strengthen their leadership ahead of the elections. Political analyst calls it pressure politics 'Alliance will harm SP more than help it' Senior journalist Rajendra Kumar said AIMIM's performance in the 2022 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections raises questions about Owaisi's electoral influence. AIMIM contested 95 seats in 2022 and secured around 4.5 lakh votes, but failed to win any seat. According to Kumar, on several constituencies the margin of defeat for SP candidates was lower than the votes secured by AIMIM candidates. He argued that the division of Muslim votes may have hurt the SP in some constituencies. According to Kumar, Owaisi's demand for "equal status" in any alliance effectively translates into a claim for a large share of seats, something unlikely to be accepted by major opposition parties. "Owaisi is doing pressure politics. He can influence results on some seats, but his presence has not benefited opposition parties electorally," Kumar said. 'Has never defeated BJP directly' Kumar further claimed that AIMIM has not won seats by directly defeating the BJP and that its gains in states such as Bihar came largely at the expense of opposition parties. He argued that an alliance with AIMIM would be more beneficial for BSP than SP because BSP currently has less to lose electorally. Owaisi announces first candidate from Matera At Sunday's rally in Bahraich, Owaisi declared AIMIM's Uttar Pradesh president Shaukat Ali as the party's candidate from the Matera Assembly constituency. He said politics should now focus on participation and equality rather than symbolism. Matera is considered a significant constituency because Muslims account for around 45% of its electorate. Of the nearly 3.4 lakh voters, about 1.5 lakh to 1.55 lakh are Muslim. The seat has been held by the Samajwadi Party for three consecutive elections. SP MLA Maria Shah currently represents the constituency, while her husband Yasar Shah had previously won the seat twice. Owaisi's key messages from the Bahraich rally 1. 'Innocent people are being troubled in the name of encounters' Owaisi alleged that innocent youths were being harassed and jailed under the pretext of police encounters and law-and-order actions. He said AIMIM would continue to raise issues related to justice and constitutional rights. 2. References to Bihar and West Bengal Rejecting allegations that AIMIM acts as another party's "B-Team", Owaisi cited developments in Bihar and West Bengal and said many leaders who opposed the BJP later joined it. He claimed AIMIM had survived attempts to weaken the party and continued to maintain its political presence. 3. 'We will not compromise on our beliefs' Owaisi said AIMIM would continue fighting what it considers injustice and would not compromise on its principles despite criticism from opponents. Why Bahraich and Matera are politically important Muslim vote base and historical significance Political observers point to two key reasons behind Owaisi's decision to begin his campaign from Matera. Owaisi's earlier visit to Uttar Pradesh Before the Bahraich rally, Owaisi had visited Lucknow in January 2025 to attend meetings related to the Waqf Amendment Bill. During that visit, he interacted with representatives of the Sunni and Shia Waqf Boards as well as other stakeholders. Who is Asaduddin Owaisi? Asaduddin Owaisi is a Lok Sabha MP from Hyderabad and president of the All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen (AIMIM). The organisation traces its origins to 1927, when it was founded as the Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen (MIM). Following Hyderabad's integration into India, the organisation was banned and later revived in 1957 as AIMIM. The party has remained under the leadership of the Owaisi family for decades. After Abdul Waheed Owaisi and Salahuddin Owaisi, the party is now led by Asaduddin Owaisi.

stories.title: Morena train tragedy video surfaces, people seen being run over:Body parts scattered across 500 metres, collected in bags
stories.summary: An incident unfolded on the Khajuraho–Udaipur Intercity Express after a rumour of a mobile phone explosion and fire spread among passengers. The panic reportedly led to chain pulling, forcing the train to stop between Hetampur and Dhaulpur stations around 4:15 PM on Sunday. In the chaos, several passengers got off the train in fear. Shortly after, four passengers were hit by another passing train, Patalkot Express, and died on the spot. Railway authorities have ordered a high-level investigation into the incident. Victims’ bodies scattered, remains collected for post-mortem Officials said the impact of the accident was so severe that body parts of the deceased were scattered over a stretch of nearly 500 metres. The remains had to be collected and packed for post-mortem procedures. The deceased have been identified as: Railway officials confirm rumour led to chain pulling Jhansi Division PRO Manoj Kumar Singh stated that a passenger falsely spread panic by claiming that a mobile phone had exploded and caused a fire inside the train. This led to chain pulling and passengers rushing out of the train in panic. He added that a six-member committee has been formed to inspect the site, record statements of railway officials and eyewitnesses, and submit a report on the basis of which further action will be taken. Investigation team formed, compensation assured Railway administration has ordered a high-level probe into the incident. Officials confirmed that the committee will examine how the rumour spread and whether safety lapses contributed to the tragedy. Authorities have also assured financial assistance to the families of the deceased. Rescue operation launched after farmer alerts police The accident came to light after a farmer, who had gone into the forest to collect wood, informed the police. At that time, local police teams from Sarai Chhola and Civil Lines were already nearby taking action against illegal sand dumping. They immediately rushed to the spot and informed railway officials. Rescue and recovery operations were launched soon after. Victim family en route to pilgrimage return journey According to a co-passenger, Birma Devi was returning to Jaipur after visiting Bageshwar Dham along with relatives and neighbours when the rumour spread inside the train. Passengers panicked and jumped off the train, leading to the fatal accident. Officials promise support and strict action Morena Superintendent of Police Dharmraj Meena and District Collector Yogesh Kumar Jangid visited the accident site. The SP assured that all possible assistance would be provided to the affected families. Police completed post-mortem examinations during the night and handed over the bodies to relatives. Railway Protection Force (RPF) officials noted that chain pulling incidents are frequently reported between smaller stations in the region, but the exact cause and responsibility will be determined after the official railway investigation.
