stories.title: ₹2 crore Hapur robbery accused killed in encounter:Looted cash and jewellery from businessman's family; carried a reward of ₹50,000
stories.summary: A key accused in the high-profile Hapur robbery case, in which a businessman's family was held hostage and valuables worth nearly ₹2 crore were looted, was killed in a police encounter late on Thursday night. The accused, identified as Shyam (28), carried a reward of ₹50,000 on his head. During the exchange of fire, Head Constable Manoj Kumar also sustained a gunshot injury. According to Superintendent of Police (SP) KG Singh, the encounter took place at around 10:30 pm during a vehicle-checking operation on Bulandshahr Road under the Hapur Nagar police station area. Accused opened fire after being cornered SP KG Singh said a suspicious motorcyclist attempted to flee after spotting the police. Officers pursued him and alerted Hapur Dehat police. A joint police team eventually surrounded the suspect near Godi village. Realising he was trapped, the accused allegedly took cover behind a tubewell and opened fire on the police team. Officers retaliated, and Shyam was critically injured in the exchange. He was rushed to a government hospital, where doctors declared him dead. Mastermind and gang members arrested earlier Earlier, on 7 June, police arrested five members of the gang following a major encounter on Sultanpur Road. Among those arrested was suspended Uttar Pradesh Police constable Vicky Gautam, who police identified as the mastermind behind the robbery. Multiple criminal cases registered against Shyam The deceased accused, Shyam, son of Virendra, was a resident of Surajpur village under Patwai police station in Rampur district. Police said he was wanted in the Hapur robbery case registered on 1 June and had several criminal cases against him, including charges under the Gangster Act, robbery and dacoity. At least four such cases were registered in districts including Moradabad. First, see the pictures- How was the robbery carried out? The robbery took place on 2 June at the residence of businessman Narendra Agarwal. His 17-year-old grandson, Siddhant, had returned home early from a business trip. According to investigators, the robbers had already been waiting nearby. As soon as Siddhant entered the house, four to five armed men followed him inside. The criminals allegedly pointed a pistol at his head before taking businessman Narendra Agarwal, his wife Sushila Agarwal and the household watchman hostage. The gang demanded ₹2 crore in cash. When the businessman said such an amount was not available in the house, the robbers tied up all family members and the watchman using bedsheets. They confined them to a room and spent nearly an hour searching the property. The gang eventually escaped with approximately 1.25 kg of gold jewellery, silver ornaments and cash worth several lakh rupees from cupboards and lockers. After the robbers fled, the family alerted police. Senior officers, including the DIG and SP, arrived at the scene and launched an investigation. CCTV footage from the surrounding area was examined. CCTV footage led to identification The robbery sparked outrage among traders across Hapur. Business associations questioned the law-and-order situation and gave police a 72-hour ultimatum to crack the case, warning of market closures and protests if no progress was made. During the investigation, police recovered CCTV footage from a location around 150 metres from Narendra Agarwal's residence. The footage showed three suspects fleeing on a motorcycle carrying a bag shortly after the robbery. The images helped investigators identify the accused. How police arrested the gang ? Circle Officer (CO) Varun Mishra said that on the night of 7 June, police teams were conducting checks on Sultanpur Road in the Kotwali Dehat area when they spotted five suspicious men riding two motorcycles. When officers attempted to stop them, the suspects accelerated and allegedly opened fire. Police returned fire, injuring Rohit and Shahbe Alam. The area was cordoned off and five accused were arrested. Those arrested were- Cash, Jewellery and Weapons Recovered Police recovered- Gang conducted reconnaissance for four months Investigators found that the gang had conducted detailed surveillance of the businessman's residence before carrying out the robbery. Initially, police believed the reconnaissance had lasted two months. Further investigation revealed the criminals had monitored the house and its occupants for nearly four months. They gathered information on visitors, security arrangements, family routines, the number of people present in the house and even the location of the safe. Police also arrested Guddu of Moradabad and Tinkoo of Sambhal in connection with the case. According to investigators, Tinkoo's father, Satpal, worked as a mason for the businessman for several months. Police claim Tinkoo supplied crucial information regarding the location of the safe and where its key was kept. Investigators believe this is why the robbers were able to go directly to the places where cash and valuables were stored. Suspended constable had criminal history Vicky Gautam, the alleged mastermind, is originally from Amroha and joined the Uttar Pradesh Police in 2016. He was posted in Sitapur until 2024 but was suspended after remaining absent from duty for ten days without authorisation. Police records show he had previously been jailed in criminal cases. On 19 May 2025, he was arrested in Moradabad's Dilari police station area with old currency notes worth approximately ₹1.5 crore. Investigators also discovered that Vicky Gautam and Tinkoo became acquainted while serving time in jail, a connection that later played a key role in planning and executing the Hapur robbery.

stories.title: Is Akhilesh's Samajwadi Party heading for a split?:21 MPs reject Rajbhar's claim saying 'only those with something to hide would leave'
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Cabinet Minister Om Prakash Rajbhar has claimed that the Samajwadi Party (SP) is heading towards a major split. To verify the claim, Dainik Bhaskar contacted all 37 SP MPs elected to the Lok Sabha. Of the 37 MPs, 16 did not respond to calls, while 21 spoke to the newspaper. They were asked two questions- Most MPs rejected Rajbhar's allegation outright, describing him as a political showman who makes controversial statements for publicity. Several said there was no dissatisfaction within the party and that no MP was considering leaving SP. Rajbhar's claim: Dalit, OBC and General category MPs ready to leave Rajbhar alleged that SP leader Ram Gopal Yadav had submitted a list of names to Union Home Minister Amit Shah and suggested that several SP MPs were ready to switch sides. According to Rajbhar, most Dalit, OBC and General category MPs from Purvanchal, excluding Muslim and Yadav MPs, were prepared to leave the Samajwadi Party. SP won 37 Lok Sabha seats in the 2024 General Election, including 17 seats in Purvanchal- Among them, Ghazipur is represented by Afzal Ansari, while Azamgarh is represented by Dharmendra Yadav. Purvanchal MPs reject Rajbhar's allegations Pushpendra Saroj (Kaushambi)- Rajbhar should first look after his own party. Let him tell us how many MLAs remain with him. BJP has been trying to lure us for years. Only those who are afraid change sides. We are not leaving SP." Rajeev Rai (Ghosi)- Rajbhar has developed a habit of boasting. It has become incurable. He is making such statements out of desperation over securing tickets for his sons. The question of SP MPs joining BJP does not arise. Daroga Prasad Saroj (Lalganj)- Only a thief would leave SP. He must be involved in some sort of brokerage. The national president respected everyone and gave them opportunities. Everything else is false. Ram Prasad Chaudhary (Basti)- That is his style. There is no truth in what he says. He is known for making such statements. No SP MP is going anywhere. Sanatan Pandey (Ballia)- SP gave me the opportunity to become an MLA and then an MP. Rajbhar has now made me internationally famous with his comments. SP is not breaking apart. Babu Singh Kushwaha (Jaunpur)- Where is the list he keeps referring to? He should reveal the names of those who are supposedly leaving and explain what they have done wrong. Priya Saroj (Machhlishahr)- I do not wish to comment on someone whose words and actions rarely match. SP defeated him badly in 2024 and will defeat him again in 2027. Every SP MP stands firmly with the leadership. Virendra Singh (Chandauli)- He is trying to prove his usefulness to BJP. When he was with SP, he criticised Yogi Adityanath. Now that he is with BJP, he criticises SP. No one is leaving. Political observers believe Rajbhar's remarks may be aimed at creating a perception of instability within SP. 'Big Split' narrative Rajbhar has repeatedly compared SP's situation to splits witnessed in parties such as Shiv Sena and Trinamool Congress, claiming that a similar development is inevitable in Uttar Pradesh. Such statements may serve as a signal to any disgruntled leaders contemplating a change of allegiance. Interestingly, SP chief Akhilesh Yadav also acknowledged that those driven by fear or personal interest could leave the party, although he maintained confidence in the party's unity. Linking SP leaders to corruption cases Rajbhar has also linked his allegations to investigations into the mining scam and the Gomti Riverfront project. He claims Ram Gopal Yadav is attempting to shield leaders such as Akhilesh Yadav, Shivpal Yadav and Gayatri Prajapati from the consequences of ongoing investigations. Through this narrative, Rajbhar appears to be portraying SP leaders as individuals attempting to protect themselves from legal scrutiny. Other SP MPs also dismiss the claim Akhilesh Yadav (Kannauj)- BJP has broken many parties and persuaded many SP MLAs and MLCs to switch sides in the past. Whoever is driven by fear or self-interest may leave. We need brave people to take on BJP. SP is ready. Iqra Hasan (Kairana)- Rajbhar should examine whether his own MLAs remain with him. I am in SP and will remain in SP. Harendra Malik (Muzaffarnagar)- Rajbhar is trying to return to SP but is not being accepted. He is making such claims only to improve his standing within BJP. Ruchiveera (Moradabad)- He is not a serious politician. He keeps making random statements. In fact, he himself wants to join SP. Devesh Shakya (Etah)- There is no need to attach importance to someone who changes positions constantly. BJP and Rajbhar should focus on managing their own legislators. Mohibullah (Rampur)- SP MPs are united and stand firmly with Akhilesh Yadav. Rajbhar's allegations are completely detached from reality. Aditya Yadav (Badaun)- BJP thrives on conspiracy theories. No SP MP is leaving. Such statements are made simply to attract attention and increase political relevance. Neeraj Maurya (Aonla)- The defeat suffered by Rajbhar's son in 2024 still appears to be troubling him. SP remains united and will perform even better in 2027. Utkarsh Verma 'Madhur' (Kheri)- He speaks without any basis. Rajbhar is nervous because SP is moving towards forming the next government. Anand Bhadauria (Dhaurahra)- There is not an ounce of truth in these allegations. SP leaders cannot compromise with their ideology. Dharmendra Yadav (Azamgarh- My response is the same as that given by Ram Gopal Yadav. Rambhual Nishad (Sultanpur)- SP gave us opportunities and respect. Why would we leave for BJP? Let Rajbhar first demonstrate his own electoral strength. What the Anti-Defection Law says? At least 25 SP MPs would need to defect together Under India's Anti-Defection Law, MPs or MLAs can merge with another party only if at least two-thirds of the legislature party moves together. For SP, which currently has 37 Lok Sabha MPs, at least 25 MPs would have to switch sides collectively. If only 24 or fewer MPs defected, they would lose their Lok Sabha membership and would be required to seek re-election. This makes any large-scale defection significantly more difficult than political rhetoric may suggest. Why BJP wants a larger majority in Parliament The debate over numbers gained significance after the Modi government introduced three Bills in the Lok Sabha between 16 and 18 April 2026. One of these was a Constitutional Amendment Bill aimed at facilitating the implementation of women's reservation before the 2029 elections. The proposal included provisions to increase the maximum strength of the Lok Sabha from 550 to 850 seats through amendments to Articles 81 and 82 of the Constitution. Constitutional Amendment fell short A Constitutional Amendment requires a special majority- During voting in April 2026, 528 MPs were present in the Lok Sabha. To secure passage, the Bill required 352 votes. However- As a result, the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill fell short by 54 votes. Political analysts believe this arithmetic explains why BJP is keen to increase its parliamentary strength and secure broader support in the Lok Sabha. However, based on the responses of SP MPs, Rajbhar's prediction of an imminent split currently finds little support within the Samajwadi Party itself.

stories.title: Monsoon stalls near UP border for 5 days:Heatwave alert in 25 districts; Banda remains hottest city in country
stories.summary: The delayed arrival of the monsoon in Uttar Pradesh has led to a fresh surge in temperatures across the state. After reaching the state's border, the monsoon has slowed significantly and has remained stalled near the Uttar Pradesh–Chhattisgarh border for the past five days. According to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), it could take up to another week for the monsoon to advance and enter Uttar Pradesh. On Friday morning, strong sunshine was reported across most districts. Low wind speeds have increased humidity levels, making conditions more uncomfortable. A rain alert has been issued for 16 districts, while 25 districts remain under a heatwave warning. During the past 24 hours, intense heat has affected large parts of Purvanchal and Bundelkhand. Banda recorded a maximum temperature of 46°C, making it the hottest city in the country. Monsoon progress remains slow The Meteorological Department said weather activity across Uttar Pradesh is currently limited and scattered. While isolated thunderstorms and light drizzle may occur in some areas, these are unlikely to provide any significant relief from the prevailing heat. Forecasters expect temperatures to continue rising over the next five days, with heatwave conditions likely to remain severe during this period. 'No effective weather system Active in UP' Senior meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh said that no effective weather system is currently active over Uttar Pradesh. Atul Kumar Singh said- "At present, no effective weather system is active over Uttar Pradesh. As a result, the monsoon's progress remains slow and conditions are not yet favourable for its entry into the state." According to the Meteorological Department, residents may have to wait approximately another week before the monsoon arrives in Uttar Pradesh. Rain alert in 16 districts, heatwave warning in 25 Although a rain alert has been issued for 16 districts, widespread rainfall is not expected immediately. Meanwhile, 25 districts remain under a heatwave alert as temperatures continue to remain well above normal levels. The combination of intense sunshine, low wind speeds and high humidity has increased discomfort across much of the state. 5-day weather forecast for UP 20 June- Most districts across the state are expected to remain cloudy. Heavy rainfall may occur at isolated locations. 21 June- The weather is likely to remain largely clear across Uttar Pradesh. Strong winds are expected, while cloud movement could trigger light drizzle in some areas. 22 June- Cloud cover is expected across most districts. Parts of eastern Uttar Pradesh may experience heavy rainfall accompanied by strong winds. 23 June- Rainfall is likely in both eastern and western Uttar Pradesh. Strong winds may also occur in several areas. 24 June- Most districts are expected to remain under cloudy skies. Heavy rainfall may occur at isolated locations. Heat likely to persist until monsoon advances With the monsoon stalled near the Uttar Pradesh–Chhattisgarh border and no significant weather system currently supporting its advancement, heatwave conditions are expected to continue across much of the state. stories.title: Ram Mandir theft row:SIT probe reveals missing gold, silver records; management may shift to administrative officials
stories.summary: The alleged theft of offerings worth crores of rupees at the Ram Mandir in Ayodhya has sparked a wider debate over the mandir's administrative structure and whether greater government oversight is needed. The controversy has led to discussions about adopting a management model similar to those at major pilgrimage centres such as Shirdi Sai Baba mandir and Vaishno Devi Shrine, where administrative officers play a key role in governance. Sources indicate that the SIT may recommend expanding the role of government-appointed ex officio members within the trust, with the Ayodhya District Magistrate potentially being given a more prominent supervisory role. If accepted, these recommendations could gradually shift greater management responsibility from trustees and priest to administrative officials. The Special Investigation Team (SIT), which has been probing the case for the past four days, found that key administrative functions of the mandir were largely concentrated in the hands of three individuals, Champat Rai, Dr Anil Mishra and Gopal Rao. They reportedly oversaw the counting of offerings and their deposit into bank accounts. The investigation has also revealed that ex officio members of the trust, including the Ayodhya District Magistrate, the Additional Chief Secretary (Home) and central government-nominated members, were neither actively involved in decision-making nor regularly informed about the mandir's operations. Investigators have also identified shortcomings in the counting of offerings and security arrangements, findings that are likely to form a key part of the SIT's final report. SIT formed following trust's request On 13 June 2026, the Uttar Pradesh Home Department constituted a three-member SIT following a request from the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust. On 15 June, the SIT team, led by Lucknow Commissioner Vijay Vishwas Pant, arrived in Ayodhya and began its investigation from the counting room within the Ram Mandir complex. The team questioned several individuals connected to Mandir operations, including- On 18 June, the fourth day of the investigation, Dr Anil Mishra was questioned for approximately four hours. The SIT subsequently called Tinnu Yadav again for further questioning, interrogating him for around one and a half hours. The team also conducted extensive questioning of employees working in the Mandir basement and reviewed operational procedures with personnel from the bank and Tata Consultancy Services (TCS). In addition, investigators have been recording statements from devotees who donated jewellery, gold and silver ornaments to Ramlala as offerings. Four major irregularities identified The SIT has reportedly uncovered four major areas of concern during its investigation. 1. Offering counting system found lacking transparency Investigators found that the process of removing cash from the 14 donation boxes installed across the Mandir premises, transporting it to the office and subsequently counting it in the designated counting room lacked adequate transparency and security safeguards. According to sources, the system was vulnerable at several stages and did not meet expected standards of accountability. 2. No proper record of gold and silver offerings The SIT reportedly found no comprehensive record of gold and silver jewellery donated by devotees. While cash donation figures were regularly presented during the trust's quarterly meetings, details regarding the quantity and value of precious metal offerings were allegedly not disclosed in a systematic manner. This has raised concerns regarding documentation and inventory management. 3. Recruitment and tender procedures under scrutiny The appointment of security personnel, procurement contracts and recruitment procedures for Mandir employees have also come under suspicion. According to sources, investigators found indications that influential individuals may have played a role in securing jobs for their relatives and associates within the Mandir administration. Tender allocations and procurement decisions are also being examined as part of the probe. 4. Crowd management failures The SIT has reportedly identified shortcomings in multiple aspects of crowd management and visitor services. Areas under scrutiny include- Investigators are examining whether administrative deficiencies contributed to operational failures within the Mandir complex. SIT surprised by influence of Champat Rai's close aide 'Tinnu' According to sources, SIT members were particularly surprised by the influence exercised by Ram Shankar alias Tinnu Yadav within the Ram Janmabhoomi complex. Tinnu Yadav is considered one of the central figures in the investigation and has been questioned extensively by the SIT. Sources suggest that following submission of the investigation report, several employees, including Tinnu Yadav, could face removal from their positions. Legal action may also be recommended against certain individuals, depending on the findings. The investigation has also highlighted concerns regarding security protocols within the Mandir complex. According to sources, while ordinary visitors and even VIP guests are generally prohibited from carrying mobile phones inside the complex, individuals associated with Tinnu Yadav allegedly moved freely without undergoing routine security checks. Sources claim that his guests were accorded treatment comparable to ministerial protocol and were not subjected to the restrictions faced by other visitors. These allegations are being examined as part of the broader inquiry into administrative irregularities. Bank officials point to gaps in the process The SIT also questioned officials from the State Bank of India regarding the counting and deposit of offerings. According to sources, bank officials informed investigators that the contract workers involved in counting donations had been appointed at the recommendation of Trustee Champat Rai. Bank officials reportedly stated that their responsibility begins only when the money reaches them for deposit. They told investigators that they did not know the handling or movement of cash before it arrived at the bank.

stories.title: ₹5 lakh to meet Mayawati, ₹3.35 crore for assembly ticket:BSP UP Chief says, 'Elections are around the corner, full amount must be paid in cash'
stories.summary: ‘When you meet Behanji, carry ₹5 lakh. We will tell her that you want an Assembly ticket. There will be no accounting for those ₹5 lakh. For the ticket, you will have to pay ₹3.35 crore. Deposit ₹1 crore to ₹1.5 crore now, and you will get one to one-and-a-half months for the remaining amount. If the government is formed, we guarantee that you will be made a minister.’ These claims were made by Vishwanath Pal, Uttar Pradesh President of the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP), during conversations with a Bhaskar reporter posing as a prospective Assembly candidate. To investigate the process of obtaining a ticket from the BSP — a party recognised as a national political organisation — a Bhaskar reporter prepared a profile portraying himself as an aspiring politician. He established contacts with BSP leaders and workers before expressing interest in contesting from Lucknow's Bakshi Ka Talab (BKT) Assembly constituency. The first contact was with Shailendra Gautam, BSP's Lucknow district president. Meeting the BSP District President The reporter met Shailendra Gautam at Shailendra Traders near Raghuvar Marriage Hall in Indiranagar, Lucknow. During a conversation in a closed room, Gautam allegedly explained the process for meeting BSP chief Mayawati and discussed the cost of obtaining a party ticket. Reporter: Now tell me, how will I meet Behanji? What do I need to do? Shailendra Gautam: To meet Behanji as a candidate, you will have to bring ₹5 lakh. You will be introduced to Behanji as a claimant from BKT. Behanji herself will speak to you. You will be given an empty envelope there. You will put the money in the envelope and place it on Behanji's table with your own hands. For this seat, Behanji has mentioned one Pandit candidate and one Thakur candidate. The Thakur candidate is already active and moving around in the constituency. Reporter: So, after bringing ₹5 lakh, what happens next? Shailendra Gautam: The ₹5 lakh is only for the meeting. There will be no accounting for it. In a way, it is a gift to Behanji. After that, Behanji's office will tell you the amount that must be deposited for the ticket. You will get one to one-and-a-half months for this. Once the amount is deposited, your candidature will be announced before a crowd of 10,000–15,000 people. After that, you will begin working in the constituency. 'Every seat has a different rate' The reporter then sought details about the amount allegedly required to secure a BSP ticket. Shailendra Gautam: You will have to deposit ₹3.35 crore. Reporter: You mean the remaining ₹3 crore has to be paid later? Shailendra Gautam: No, the total amount is ₹3.35 crore. You will first take ₹5 lakh and meet Behanji. You will receive her blessings. She will tell you to begin preparations. The amount can be deposited either in one instalment or over one to one-and-a-half months. Sometimes people deposit ₹20 lakh, sometimes ₹50 lakh. Those amounts are properly recorded in the register. But the full ₹3.35 crore must be deposited within the stipulated time. Reporter: Suppose I pay in instalments and another person deposits the entire amount before I complete payment. Will my ticket be cancelled? Shailendra Gautam: No, that will not happen. We will manage it. Some flexibility is always possible. Behanji takes care of those who deposit first. 'Many leaders have grown through BSP' Shailendra Gautam: That is why Bhai Umashankar Singh is a star in Behanji's eyes. Whenever the time comes, he delivers. That is why Behanji respects him. Reporter: He is a very influential person. Shailendra Gautam: He was not influential earlier. BSP made him influential. Many such people in the BSP immediately deposit money when asked. Madhogarh's ticket in the Chitrakoot division has already been finalised. The candidate is a Brahmin. The ticket was announced first and he is already campaigning. Barabanki Sadar's ticket has also been finalised. Around 20 to 25 tickets have already been decided. Reporter: Does even a difficult seat cost ₹3.35 crore? Shailendra Gautam: No. Not every seat. Take Lucknow East, for example. The party knows it is a difficult constituency, but we still have to field a candidate. If someone wants to become a leader, let them contest. If the government is formed, Behanji will reward them in some way. The reporter also asked whether Mayawati considered a candidate's political experience. Reporter: Will Behanji not examine my background, considering that I have never been involved in politics? Shailendra Gautam: No. She will only seek information about any cases against you. Just tell her, "Behanji, I was previously involved in business and now I want to serve society by joining the party." Reporter: I would like to meet Behanji through you. Shailendra Gautam: We are organisational people. If someone contributes willingly, that is a different matter. Reporter: Suppose I pay ₹2 crore in cash and ₹1 crore in gold. Will that work? Shailendra Gautam: No. The entire amount must be in cash. I have served as district president for four years and as Lucknow divisional in-charge. Behanji trusts me a great deal. State President quotes the same amount To verify the claims, the reporter approached Uttar Pradesh BSP President Vishwanath Pal. Pal invited the reporter to his private office on the second floor of Shaligram Apartment near 1090 Chauraha in Lucknow. The reporter met him twice. The first meeting was introductory. During the second meeting, another reporter accompanied him while posing as a financier. According to the account, Vishwanath Pal quoted the same figures and outlined the same process as described by the district president. 'Deposit ₹1 crore first' Vishwanath Pal: Suppose ₹1 crore is deposited and no other claimant emerges. We discussed ₹3.35 crore with you. If you later say you cannot pay more and still want to contest, then the party may decide accordingly. Contesting itself requires expenditure. That is why we told you that after paying the ₹5 lakh, you must proceed further. The ₹3.35 crore will be recorded in writing. In some situations, the amount may even be reduced, but that generally happens only if we delay announcing the candidate. Reporter: But that carries a risk. Vishwanath Pal: Exactly. Suppose Behanji becomes angry. There is currently a claimant who gave ₹5 lakh and kept promising to arrange the rest. One day he invited me for tea and showed me ₹1.5 crore in a bag. He said he would arrange another ₹1 crore and deposit ₹2.5 crore. He told me this on 15 April. Since then, he has not answered calls. He was supposed to bring ₹2 crore today. We told him not to come because Behanji had become displeased. We instructed him to collect the full amount before approaching us again. This is regarding the Barabanki Sadar Assembly seat. Reporter: How much time will I get? Vishwanath Pal: As little as possible. If you return after 10 days and someone else has completed the process, your opportunity may be gone. If you decide now, your meeting with Behanji can be scheduled immediately. Reporter: What benefit will I get if I join the BSP? Vishwanath Pal: If the government is formed, I guarantee that I will make you a minister. This is a good seat for us. Nakul Dubey won from here and became a minister. Reporter: After giving ₹5 lakh, how much time will I get? Vishwanath Pal: Paying ₹5 lakh alone means nothing. You should immediately arrange at least ₹1 crore to ₹1.5 crore. You will then get roughly one month to arrange the remainder. Elections are very close. The election announcement could come at any time. Behanji has already called a meeting on the 24th. The reporter then asked whether a person who merely wanted to meet Mayawati and seek blessings would also have to pay. Vishwanath Pal: Azamgarh, Jaunpur and Shahganj have already been announced. Madhogarh has also been announced. One Thakur candidate has been declared. Five candidates have been announced so far. Discussions are continuing for the remaining seats. Only those seats where money has arrived have been announced. Reporter: If this person accompanying me also wants to meet Behanji and seek blessings, will he have to pay another ₹5 lakh? Vishwanath Pal: No. We can arrange a joint meeting. Otherwise, meeting Behanji separately costs ₹2 lakh. Reporter: Whatever remains, we will contribute separately to your service. Vishwanath Pal: We will tell Behanji that these people want to contest and that these are their associates. We will arrange a private meeting. Winning an Assembly election gives a person considerable influence and opportunities. We would like you to bring more than ₹5 lakh on the day of the meeting. Reporter: When can you take me? Vishwanath Pal: Whenever you say. If you want to go now, I can call and arrange it immediately. Reporter: Apart from ₹5 lakh, how much should I bring initially? Vishwanath Pal: Whatever you can arrange. Ultimately, ₹3.35 crore is required. Bring as much as possible because there is very little time. Why did the sting not go further ? The day after the meeting, Vishwanath Pal allegedly informed the reporter that an appointment with Mayawati had been secured. However, the operation was not taken any further. According to the report, security arrangements and checks before meeting the BSP supremo are extremely strict, making it difficult to carry concealed recording equipment. As a result, no further sting operation was conducted. Indications about BSP's Election strategy During the conversations, party leaders also gave indications regarding preparations for the upcoming Assembly elections- About the BSP Founded by Kanshi Ram on 14 April 1984 Kanshi Ram founded the Bahujan Samaj Party on 14 April 1984, the birth anniversary of Dr Bhimrao Ambedkar. The party's election symbol is the elephant. Former Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Mayawati currently serves as the party's national president and has held the office of Chief Minister four times. The BSP advocates for the rights and political representation of Bahujan communities, Dalits, backward classes and other marginalised sections of society. BSP's vote share In the 2022 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, the BSP secured 12.9% of the vote and won just one seat. However, it remained the state's third-largest party in terms of vote share. The party's vote share in recent Assembly elections was- 2007: 30% 2012: 26% 2017: 22% 2022: 12.9% The figures indicate a steady decline in electoral support over the past four Assembly elections, despite the party retaining a significant presence across Uttar Pradesh.

Malik is the ninth government employee terminated this year and faces charges including murder and attempt to murder. This action is part of an ongoing crackdown on terror infrastructure within government institutions.

stories.title: Omar Abdullah cabinet expansion delay stirs NC rumblings, BJP taunts
stories.summary: Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah faces internal pressure from his National Conference party to expand his cabinet, with some members expressing concerns about the performance of current ministers. Opposition BJP claims the delay is due to fear of the NC government collapsing if more berths are filled, a notion the NC dismisses as a bluff.

stories.title: Soldier dies in accidental fire in Jammu & Kashmir’s Poonch
stories.summary: An Army jawan, Naik BD Rao, died early Thursday in Jammu and Kashmir's Poonch district. He was posted with 16 Rashtriya Rifles at Draba. The soldier was on night duty and was found dead at his post. His service rifle allegedly went off accidentally. An inquiry is underway.

stories.title: AI comes to highways: NHAI tool flags defects, contradictions and dispute risks
stories.summary: In a groundbreaking move, the National Highways Authority of India has launched 'Margsarthi', a cutting-edge AI tool that transforms the way contract documents are reviewed. This innovative system cuts down processing time from a matter of days to mere minutes, allowing for unprecedented efficiency.

stories.title: Felt loyal to my CEO, then got laid off: Indian man narrates H-1B ordeal in US, returning to India after 5 years 'feeling completely defeated'
Ram Temple donation row: SIT questions trust member on cash counting
stories.summary: The questioning comes ahead of Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath's scheduled visit to the Ram Temple on Friday. As per the minute-to-minute itinerary issued by Ayodhya District Magistrate Shashank Tripathi, temple trust general secretary Champat Rai has been directed to nominate an individual to oversee arrangements for the chief minister's darshan and pujan.

stories.title: Political philosopher quote of the day: 'Man is born free; and everywhere he is in chains' — Jean-Jacques Rousseau
Jharkhand Rajya Sabha poll defeat: Who ditched Congress - its own MLAs or INDIA bloc allies?
stories.summary: Congress suffered a significant Rajya Sabha election defeat in Jharkhand, losing a seat despite having the required MLA support. The NDA-backed Independent candidate Parimal Nathwani secured victory, highlighting alleged cross-voting and a breakdown in coordination among INDIA bloc allies. This setback follows similar electoral challenges for the Congress in Bihar and Himachal Pradesh.

stories.title: Mukhyamantri Bal Seva Yojana emerges as a lifeline for vulnerable children in Uttar Pradesh
stories.summary: In Uttar Pradesh, the Mukhyamantri Bal Seva Yojana stands as a beacon of hope for vulnerable children. While it started as a response to the COVID-19 crisis, this initiative has broadened its scope to uplift disadvantaged young people through consistent financial help, access to education, digital learning tools, and marriage support.

stories.title: 'Why should a Dalit worry about RSS': BJP MP to Priyank Kharge; gets sharp 'fear none' reply
stories.summary: BJP MP Ramesh Jigajinagi questioned why a Dalit minister, Priyank Kharge, was concerned about the RSS, suggesting he focus on governance. Kharge responded by asserting his fearlessness, drawing strength from BR Ambedkar's ideology and questioning the RSS's stance and the implications of Jigajinagi's remarks.

stories.title: From trade talks to seafarers' security in the Middle East: Foreign Secretary Misri details PM Modi's France visit
stories.summary: Prime Minister Modi's G7 visit saw significant progress on trade deals, with interim agreements nearing finalization with the US and EU, and a CEPA with Canada targeted for year-end. Discussions also focused on West Asian peace, maritime security, and the safety of seafarers.

stories.title: 'Final call': CJP to return to Delhi with June 20 protest over exam irregularities
stories.summary: The Cockroach Janta Party, led by Abhijeet Dipke, is organizing a fresh protest at Delhi's Jantar Mantar on June 20. Students and job aspirants are urged to attend, raising concerns about widespread paper leaks, exam irregularities, and recruitment delays. This demonstration follows previous CJP protests and calls for Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation.

stories.title: Versailles II: Trump signs Iran deal in the one place historians wouldn't recommend
NIA chargesheets Naxal operative over 'keep the revolution alive' funeral speech
stories.summary: In a significant move, the NIA has charged Gade Innaiah, a prominent figure in Naxal activities, with inciting a crowd of 200 during a funeral gathering in October 2025. His actions are believed to have fueled violent Left-wing extremism, as he openly criticized former rebels who had surrendered and aggressively promoted Maoist beliefs through various organization fronts.

stories.title: Quote of the day by JD Vance: 'If The Titanic is going down, I'd rather be on...'
Disability rights activist denied boarding flight in NY while travelling alone in wheelchair
'Look within': CPI(ML), RJD hit back as Congress points fingers after Jharkhand Rajya Sabha shock
stories.summary: CPI(ML) Liberation has denied allegations of cross-voting in the Jharkhand Rajya Sabha election, stating both its MLAs voted for the Congress candidate as decided. The party criticized the Congress for failing to secure its own legislators' support and warned that blaming allies could harm the INDIA bloc.

stories.title: Rahul Gandhi shares Kota rally video, renews appeal for students to sign 'Chhatron Ki Goonj' petition
stories.summary: In a passionate call to action, Rahul Gandhi invited students and aspiring professionals to support the 'Chhatron Ki Goonj' initiative by signing an online petition. This campaign targets the pressing issues of exam paper leaks, educational challenges, soaring tuition fees, and the alarming rate of unemployment.

stories.title: US DOJ probes Iran Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei's links to Wall Street banks: Report
UK school teacher jailed for life for murdering adopted 13-month-old boy after months of abuse
Why can't a marijuana user own gun? US Supreme Court backs Texas man
Dramatic video of Indian scammer Yug B Chauhan sipping on soda before arrest by undercover agents in Michigan
Historic first for Mizoram's ZPM as K Laltluangkima enters Rajya Sabha
stories.summary: Mizoram's Zoram People's Movement has made history by winning its first Rajya Sabha seat. Senior leader K Laltluangkima secured the lone Upper House seat in the state assembly election. He defeated the Mizo National Front candidate. This victory marks a significant milestone for the ZPM party. Laltluangkima becomes the party's inaugural Member of Parliament in the Rajya Sabha.

stories.title: 78% Indians upbeat about economy; jobs, corruption top concerns: Survey
stories.summary: In a world filled with uncertainty, urban Indians stand out with their hopefulness about the nation’s trajectory and economic vitality, sharply contrasting with the global outlook. However, beneath this optimism, the specter of unemployment looms large for many.

stories.title: Karnataka MLC polls: Congress wins 5 seats amid cross-voting; BJP gets 2 seats
stories.summary: The ruling Congress secured a significant victory in the Karnataka legislative council elections, winning five out of seven seats. The BJP claimed the remaining two seats, while the JD(S) candidate lost. The elections saw instances of cross-voting, with Congress candidates reportedly exceeding expectations.

stories.title: Dubai police recovers Rs 76k lost by tourist in mall, sends it to her home country
UK court jails 2 British-Chinese nationals for spying on Hong Kong dissidents
Investor father, orthodontist mother: How Aman Sanger's parents shaped his billion-dollar career
Indian-origin Texas county judge KP George sentenced to 180 days in jail, 5 years' probation for buying new house with election campaign money
PM Modi pitches India as global technology and AI hub at VivaTech 2026 in Paris
stories.summary: At VivaTech 2026, Prime Minister Modi showcased India's technological innovation, proudly articulating the nation’s role as a frontrunner in AI development, robust digital frameworks, and an exciting startup ecosystem.

stories.title: 'How can rights of 150 million users be curtailed': Delhi HC questions Centre over Telegram ban for NEET retest
stories.summary: The Delhi High Court questioned the government's decision to temporarily block Telegram. This action was taken ahead of the NEET-UG 2026 re-examination on June 21. The court asked how the rights of millions of users could be restricted due to concerns about misuse by a few. The government defended its move, citing Telegram's vulnerability to large-scale information dissemination.

stories.title: Jharkhand Rajya Sabha polls: Cross-voting helps NDA-backed Parimal Nathwani win; JMM bags other seat
stories.summary: In the polls that witnessed cross-voting, Nathwani polled 28 votes, comfortably bypassing Congress's Pranav, who bagged 20 votes. The ruling Jharkhand Mukti Morcha (JMM) candidate Baidyanath Ram was elected to the other seat. Ram received 30 votes in the election, while three votes, two from the BJP and one from the Congress, were found invalid, the official told news agency PTI.

stories.title: 22-year-old missing Agniveer found hanging inside vacant Army barrack
stories.summary: Police said preliminary findings indicated that the barrack had been locked from the inside and suggested that the Agniveer had allegedly died by suicide. The body was sent for a post-mortem examination before being handed over to the concerned Army unit. Sources told PTI the autopsy report pointed to death by hanging and indicated that the incident had taken place around two days before the body was found.

stories.title: Meet Steven Schwartz: The Gen Z founder who sold water bottles as a child and built a $1.6 billion company creating 650 millionaires
Jamaican man convicted in US for sex offence involving underage girl allowed entry into UK
Who was Joshua Baer? Capital Factory CEO and millionaire killed in Texas plane crash
stories.summary: The tech scene in Austin is mourning the untimely loss of Joshua Baer, a pioneer who died in a private jet accident near Laredo, Texas. As the founder of Capital Factory, Baer was a beacon of guidance for countless startups, effortlessly bridging the gap between aspiring entrepreneurs and the resources they desperately needed.

stories.title: How Israel seized 1,000 sq km in two years, its biggest territorial expansion in decades
stories.summary: Israel has significantly expanded its military-held territory in Gaza, Lebanon, and Syria since October 2023, encompassing approximately 1,000 square kilometers. This move, described as creating "buffer zones," has displaced millions and raises concerns about permanence, despite not being recognized as new borders. This marks its biggest expansion of its militarily-held territories in years.

stories.title: No good news for Indian Green Card applicants in July 2026 US visa bulletin, EB-1 date backslides by 2 months
TMC implosion, NCP split and Congress question: Why 'ghar wapsi' may not be the answer
Quote of the day by American financier J.P. Morgan: "If you have to ask how much it costs, you can't…"
NEET paper leak: Lessons from India's biggest exam scandal
stories.summary: In light of the recent NEET-UG paper leak, India's examination infrastructure is under fire, revealing significant systemic weaknesses. The fallout from the CBSE's grading mishaps and Bihar's logistical challenges sheds light on ongoing issues that disrupt the process for countless hopeful candidates. As these scandals emerge, questions regarding equity, responsibility, and confidence in the examination framework become increasingly critical.

stories.title: Indian expat Shajeer Venga wins Rs 5 crore grand prize in Sharjah Islamic Bank's lucky draw
German archaeologists uncover 2,000-year-old Celtic prince's grave filled with gold, weapons and a wagon
Evening news wrap: TMC rebellion spills over to party accounts, Shiv Sena UBT's strength test falters; and more
'Telegram now a new dark web': Govt defends ban on app ahead of NEET retest
stories.summary: In an affidavit filed in response to Telegram's plea challenging the government's move to temporarily restrict access to the app ahead of the June 21 NEET-UG retest, the government countered that the "scale of the said channel itself demonstrates the capability of Telegram to facilitate mass dissemination of unlawful examination-related content". "Telegram has become the new dark web, linking threat actors.

stories.title: ‘Ready to sit and talk with them’: Karnataka CM Shivakumar on Mekedatu dam row with Tamil Nadu
stories.summary: Karnataka chief minister DK Shivakumar has expressed readiness to discuss the proposed Mekedatu dam project with Tamil Nadu, emphasizing it will benefit both states. He stated the project, aimed at providing drinking water to Bengaluru and generating power, will not affect Tamil Nadu's allocated Cauvery water share. Karnataka and Tamil Nadu have had a long-standing dispute over the Cauvery river.

stories.title: Renaissance proverb of the day: 'I find that the harder I work...' - a powerful reminder that luck is something you earn
How Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY) is ensure clean fuel for beneficiaries - explained
stories.summary: Launched in 2016, the Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana in India has been a game changer for countless low-income households seeking cleaner cooking options. Especially prominent in Uttar Pradesh, this initiative has not only boosted women's health but also elevated their status by replacing harmful traditional fuels with LPG, illustrating a powerful movement toward sustainability and gender equality.

stories.title: Archaeologists discover 5,000-year-old monument in Wiltshire linked to early Stonehenge traditions
stories.summary: A remarkable 5,000-year-old wooden monument, predating Stonehenge by 500 years, has been unearthed near Bulford, Wiltshire. This discovery, featuring two large posts aligned with the midsummer sunrise and midwinter sunset, suggests sophisticated ancient astronomy and ceremonial traditions were already established. Researchers believe this site may have inspired the later construction of Stonehenge, offering crucial insights into Neolithic communities.

stories.title: Promised shipping jobs, took Rs 1.73 crore: 8 booked in Navi Mumbai scam
stories.summary: A case has been registered by Thane Police against eight suspects, including owners and personnel from a shipping firm, for allegedly conning 75 job applicants out of over Rs 1.73 crore.

stories.title: UAE sets 15 as minimum age for social media use, first Arab nation to impose rule
'Not Bhagwant Mann': AAP cites '1,191 different angles' to defend Punjab CM in 'sacrilege' row
stories.summary: Punjab finance minister and AAP leader Harpal Singh Cheema asserted that a video allegedly showing chief minister Bhagwant Mann in a sacrilegious act is fake. Forensic reports from two independent laboratories confirm the individual in the video is not Mann, suggesting a defamation attempt by the opposition. This comes after the Akal Takht issued an edict against Mann over the clip.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Bruce Lee: "Do not pray for an easy life, pray for…" - the idea that comfort might actually be the enemy
Sanjay Raut does it again: Hurls abuses at rebel MPs who skipped Uddhav's key meeting
Belfast stabbing victim out of induced coma but may lose eye sight : Family reveals
Rs 50 crore each? Meet 6 MPs who could decide the fate of Uddhav Thackeray's Shiv Sena
stories.summary: Uddhav Thackeray's Shiv Sena (UBT) faces a potential major split as at least six of its nine Lok Sabha MPs are reportedly forming a separate group to join Eknath Shinde's faction. This move, dubbed 'Operation Tiger' by Thackeray loyalists who allege MPs are being bribed, could significantly weaken Uddhav Thackeray's party and bolster the NDA in Parliament.

stories.title: 'Tamil Nadu strongly opposes NEP': Governor urges Centre to drop three-language formula in inaugural address
stories.summary: 'Tamil Nadu will continue its two-language policy': Governor reiterates stand in inaugural address, reaffirms opposition to NEP'Tamil Nadu will continue its two-language policy': Governor reiterates stand in inaugural address

US Ambassador Sergio Gor calls on Amit Shah
stories.summary: US Ambassador to India, Sergio Gor, met with Union Home Minister Amit Shah to bolster cooperation against terrorism, drug trafficking, and border security. The discussions aimed at strengthening collaborative efforts to protect citizens from narcotics, secure national borders, and ensure criminals face justice in both countries. This meeting signifies a commitment to enhanced bilateral security partnerships.

stories.title: From fighter jets to ISS: Shubhanshu Shukla marks 20 years in IAF, calls journey 'life well-lived'
stories.summary: Shubhanshu Shukla, the nation’s pioneering astronaut to journey to the ISS, marked his two-decade milestone in the Indian Air Force. Looking back on his remarkable career, he remarked, 'It has been an extraordinary adventure,' transitioning from an elite fighter pilot to the stars.

stories.title: Sea-skimming, terrain-hugging, precision-guided: Inside India's new LRLACM cruise missile
stories.summary: India successfully tested its Long Range Land Attack Cruise Missile (LRLACM), a stealthy weapon designed for precision strikes hundreds of kilometers away. Developed by DRDO, this missile complements the supersonic BrahMos by focusing on low-altitude, terrain-hugging flight to evade radar and penetrate enemy defenses.

stories.title: 'Jumped to save mother': Indian teen dies in New York Central Park after falling from horse carriage
stories.summary: A tragic accident in New York's Central Park claimed the life of 18-year-old Indian student Romanch Mahajan. While on a horse-drawn carriage ride, the vehicle bolted, and Romanch heroically jumped to save his mother, suffering a fatal head injury. The incident has reignited calls to ban horse-drawn carriages in the park.

stories.title: Centre weighs MBBS internship stipend hike after four-year gap
British Amazon delivery driver jailed after making £300,000 helping students cheat in university exams
Saving lives in sky: Texas college students raise $1.85 million for medical cargo drone startup that can deliver life-saving supplies in minutes
Saudi Arabia warns drivers of up to SR900 fines for illegal car window tinting
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia's traffic department is reminding drivers about window tinting rules. Fines of SR500 to SR900 apply for violations. Tinting is allowed but must meet specific transparency standards. The front windshield must remain clear, with exceptions for authorized upper strips. Authorities emphasize clear visibility for safety and security.

stories.title: 'Won't be nuked, think of it, Bibi': Trump reveals how he convinced Netanyahu for Iran-US deal
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump declared a new peace deal with Tehran safeguards Israel from a nuclear threat, a claim made at the G7 summit. He asserted the agreement addresses Israel's primary existential concern, despite reports of Israeli opposition and critical media commentary. Trump also voiced criticism of Netanyahu's regional conduct.

stories.title: How Milan's Olympic Village will become housing for 1,700 students after the 2026 Games
Uddhav Thackeray's show of strength falls flat; only 3 of 9 MPs attend parliamentary meeting despite whip
Amid rebellion, TMC leader asks bank to freeze party accounts; cites 'serious dispute'
Tropical Storm Arthur hits Texas coast with flooding; weakens into low-pressure system as tornadoes threaten Midwest
stories.summary: Tropical Storm Arthur has weakened but its remnants are poised to unleash days of heavy rain and potentially life-threatening floods across the southeastern US. Forecasters warn of significant rainfall totals, with isolated areas expecting up to 20 inches. Coastal communities braced for the deluge, clearing drains and distributing sandbags as a drowning incident near Houston highlighted the dangers of floodwaters.

stories.title: India’s QS surge outgrows IITs, 52 universities on list
Over 150 million users ‘punished’: Telegram
MP high court lifts stay on arrest warrant against TMC MP Abhishek Banerjee
stories.summary: The Madhya Pradesh High Court has lifted an interim stay on an arrest warrant against Trinamool Congress MP Abhishek Banerjee in a defamation case. The warrant was issued following a complaint by former MLA Akash Vijayvargiya. The court dismissed Banerjee's petition after no one appeared on his behalf, indicating a loss of interest in pursuing the matter.

stories.title: One in three TB cases found in Northeast screening had no symptoms
stories.summary: A large-scale TB screening in Northeast India revealed over a third of detected cases in vulnerable groups were asymptomatic, highlighting the challenge of silent infections. This proactive approach, covering millions, is crucial for India's TB elimination goals, with AI tools now aiding early detection and treatment initiation across the region.

stories.title: Fresh setback for Mamata Banerjee: Calcutta HC refuses to stay rebel TMC MLA Ritabrata Banerjee's appointment as LoP
Is Akhilesh's Samajwadi Party headed for a split? UP deputy CM Keshav Maurya claims 25-26 SP MPs ready to break away
$300 billion, sanctions relief, Hormuz reopening: What Iran gets, what US gains from deal
Ram Mandir donations under scrutiny: RJD MP sends legal notice amid irregularity allegations
stories.summary: The Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust has received a legal notice from an RJD MP demanding detailed disclosures on Ram Mandir donations and their expenditure. This follows allegations of financial irregularities, which the Trust has denied. Opposition leaders have called for an investigation and questioned the handling of funds.

stories.title: How a tiny potato beetle became a Cold War weapon: The bizarre story behind East Germany's 'American insect' campaign
‘To be negotiated’: US–Iran interim deal defers final decision on Tehran’s nuclear future
stories.summary: The United States and Iran have reached an interim agreement on Tehran’s nuclear programme, setting in motion a two-month negotiating window aimed at resolving the core dispute between the two countries over Iran’s nuclear ambitions. The United States and Iran have reached an interim agreement on Tehran’s nuclear programme, setting in motion a two-month negotiating window aimed at resolving the core dispute between the two countries over Iran’s nuclear ambitions.

stories.title: First Amendment at 75: The bargain that still shapes India’s rights
stories.summary: India's First Constitutional Amendment in 1951 profoundly reshaped the nation's democracy. It balanced fundamental rights like free speech and property with state needs for public order and social reform. This pivotal change, enacted before the first elections, introduced mechanisms to protect reform laws and expanded grounds for speech restrictions, setting a precedent for ongoing debates.

stories.title: 'I call it deemocracy': Agnimitra Paul's swipe after series of egg attacks on TMC leaders
stories.summary: West Bengal witnesses a surge in egg-throwing incidents targeting Trinamool Congress leaders. BJP leader Agnimitra Paul calls this 'deemocracy', citing public anger over alleged corruption and misgovernance. Recent events include attacks on Kunal Ghosh and Soumitra Banerjee. Residents also targeted a vehicle linked to Madan Mitra. These protests highlight growing public dissatisfaction with the ruling party.

stories.title: Voting begins for election to two Rajya Sabha seats in Jharkhand
stories.summary: Jharkhand is witnessing a keenly contested Rajya Sabha election for two seats today. With three candidates in the fray, including BJP-backed Parimal Nathwani, JMM's Baidyanath Ram, and Congress' Pranav Jha, the focus is on the battle for the second seat. Both ruling and opposition blocs are employing strategies to prevent cross-voting, with MLAs housed in hotels and mock polls conducted.

stories.title: 'Save your MPs': Rajbhar's fresh warning to Akhilesh amid split buzz within the Samajwadi Party
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh minister Om Prakash Rajbhar claims the Samajwadi Party is on the verge of a split, citing internal dissent and a recent Brahmin conference incident. The ruling BJP supports his claims, alleging several SP MPs are ready to defect, while the SP dismisses the allegations as a diversionary tactic ahead of the 2027 elections.

stories.title: ‘Like nuclear, they don't blow up planet’: Trump's U-turn on Iran missiles after deal takes effect
stories.summary: President Trump defended a new US-Iran understanding on ballistic missiles, deeming it unfair for Tehran to be disarmed if regional rivals possess them. He differentiated missile threats from nuclear ones, suggesting a less urgent global risk. US forces will remain in the Gulf post-agreement, with follow-up talks planned.

stories.title: A second exam, a second burden: Inside Sikar's NEET crisis - video
Florida's giant Burmese pythons are doing more than eating wildlife, they are transforming the Everglades by spreading seeds
Union minister Joshi launches green hydrogen certification portal, urges states to boost mission
stories.summary: India's push for green hydrogen gained momentum with the launch of a new certification portal by Union Minister Pralhad Joshi. This initiative aims to streamline regulations and boost domestic manufacturing, evidenced by incentives for electrolyser production and pilot projects in the steel sector. The mission is actively reducing import dependence, with significant agreements for green ammonia supply to fertilizer plants.

stories.title: Chud the Builder’s bond revoked after new footage emerges in Tennessee shooting case
stories.summary: Chud the Builder’s bond in a Davidson County misdemeanor case was revoked after investigators presented footage that allegedly shows him shooting Joshua Fox before being attacked. The evidence challenges his self-defense claim in the May 2026 courthouse shooting. With serious felony charges already pending, Eatherly remains in jail as both cases move through the court system.

stories.title: 'It's signed': US-Iran MoU officially finalized after both sides digitally sign agreement
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian have virtually signed a 14-point memorandum of understanding to end hostilities and reopen the Strait of Hormuz. The agreement, effective immediately, also initiates negotiations on sanctions relief and Iran's nuclear program, marking a significant de-escalation.

stories.title: "I was pressured into unideal agreements": Clavicular's Miami nightclub investment turns into explosive legal battle over unpaid profits
stories.summary: Clavicular has spoken out amid his legal dispute with Miami's Bacara Club, claiming he was "pressured into unideal agreements" after his lawyer alleged he never received profits from a $400,000 investment. While the nightclub's representatives dispute the claims, Clavicular insists the matter will be resolved. The dispute has sparked fresh questions over ownership, unpaid earnings, and the influencer's business partnerships.

stories.title: ITI rankings improve over last year, 466 score over 9 on 10-pt scale
"Skipped Charlie's memorial despite being invited": Candace Owens accuses Blake Neff of proving Charlie Kirk 'was betrayed' in explosive feud
stories.summary: Candace Owens escalated her public feud with Blake Neff by challenging him to a livestream debate over Charlie Kirk's case, claiming Kirk believed in open discussion. She also accused Neff of fueling the belief that Charlie "was betrayed." Neff fired back, alleging Owens skipped discussions and Kirk's memorial. Their exchange has reignited online debate over Kirk's legacy and deepened divisions among conservative commentators.

stories.title: IAF flies 200 sorties in 3-4 days to airlift NEET-UG retest papers to 18 zones
Has Messi aide put Kolkata fiasco blame on TMC ex-minister?
Speaker to hear Abhishek tomorrow on split in TMC
Who’s this new chief, NCPI founders wonder
India FTA by year end, says European Commission president
stories.summary: Prime Minister Modi met with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz and EU leaders Ursula von der Leyen and Antonio Costa at the G7 summit. Discussions focused on the upcoming India-EU Free Trade Agreement, expected to be signed by year-end, and advancements in the India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor. Leaders also welcomed the understanding reached for peace in West Asia.

stories.title: ‘We’re the most famous couple on Insta,’ Meloni jokes with PM Modi at G7; ‘Melodi’ bonhomie takes India-Italy trade, def ties to new heights
stories.summary: A viral moment involving PM Modi and Italian PM Giorgia Meloni, sparked by 'Melody toffees' and a playful Instagram comment, has highlighted the growing bonhomie between the two leaders. This personal connection has translated into a 'Special Strategic Partnership', boosting bilateral trade and revitalizing defense ties with a focus on co-development and industrial collaboration.

stories.title: Can't ask Global South to bear Iran war brunt alone: PM Modi at G7
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi highlighted the ongoing impact of West Asian crises on the Global South, urging international solidarity. He proposed a global skills partnership and an International Mobilisation Partnership for Accelerating Connectivity and Trade (IMPACT) to foster shared growth and resilience.

stories.title: Father arrested for bid to kill girl over 'transgender traits'
stories.summary: A father in Auraiya has been arrested for allegedly attempting to murder his 14-year-old transgender daughter. He reportedly beat her with a stick and threw her into a canal, motivated by her gender identity. The girl survived due to shallow water and was rescued by locals. She is in critical condition.

stories.title: CPM objects to Telangana CM renaming road after Trump
stories.summary: The Communist Party of India (Marxist) has strongly criticized Telangana Chief Minister Revanth Reddy's decision to rename a road near the US Consulate after President Donald Trump. CPM General Secretary MA Baby expressed concern that this move, occurring amidst US military actions, undermines India's sovereignty and anti-imperialist ideals. He urged the Congress high command to intervene and withdraw the decision.

stories.title: Comedy show fallout: Karnataka to issue norms on handling cadavers
stories.summary: Karnataka government will soon issue guidelines for medical students on appropriate behavior and respect towards donated bodies for study. This follows viral clips of students disrespecting cadavers, sparking a debate on ethics. The ethics committee will meet to discuss reinforcing existing guidelines for handling donated bodies.

stories.title: Rahul Gandhi makes INDIA bloc speech public, allies ask: 'Why not ours?'
stories.summary: Rahul Gandhi's public release of his INDIA bloc speech has irked allies, particularly Left parties, who emphasize mutual trust for effective resistance against the BJP. Concerns were raised about Gandhi's remarks on Pinarayi Vijayan and the unilateral release of internal discussions. DMK also reiterated its stance against Congress due to a state-level alliance issue.

stories.title: ExtraEmily addresses backlash after Columbia University resume reveal leaves supporters and critics sharply divided
stories.summary: ExtraEmily responded to critics after a resume showcase clip gained attention online. While some viewers mocked her behavior, many praised her strong academic record, Columbia University achievements, and professional experience. The streamer defended herself during a June 16 broadcast, saying her accomplishments are often overlooked because of the exaggerated personality she displays on stream.

stories.title: Delhi high court seeks government's reply as Telegram challenges ban over NEET retest
stories.summary: The Delhi High Court has asked the Centre for its response on the ban imposed on Telegram, which is challenging the temporary restriction ahead of the NEET-UG retest. The government claims to have "shocking material" to share, citing ongoing issues with channels involved in examination-related activities resurfacing after being blocked.

stories.title: PM Modi seeks 'highest priority' for seafarers in W Asia peace deal in meeting with Trump; US president reiterates he ended 8 wars, mentions G2
stories.summary: PM Modi and President Trump discussed the safety of Indian seafarers amidst a US-Iran peace agreement. Trump acknowledged the risks of the profession while Modi emphasized the importance of maritime security, particularly in the Strait of Hormuz. The leaders also touched upon trade, defense, and geopolitical issues, with Trump expressing confidence in strong US-India ties.

stories.title: Sanjay Raut showers cuss words like confetti
stories.summary: Sanjay Raut's use of expletives to describe defectors marks a new low in political discourse, despite his claims of loyalty. He alleged hefty sums and case settlements were offered to MPs to switch sides. Meanwhile, suspected rebels remained in Delhi, poised to seek recognition as a separate faction, while Sena (UBT) leaders met the Speaker to invoke anti-defection laws.

Nina Lin appears permanently banned from Twitch days after NYC arrest during Knicks celebrations
stories.summary: Twitch streamer Nina Lin's channel is now offline following her arrest during New York Knicks' championship celebrations. Videos showed her on an Amazon van roof before police intervened. stories.summary: Earlier, road transport ministry rolled out the scheme for additional payment for increase in bitumen prices by updating it every month. Prices of bitumen used in highway projects have increased from Rs 49,000 per tonne on Feb 28 to Rs 80,000 a tonne on June 1. “The new policy will be out soon. Highway agencies will pay the differential amount between the base rate and prevailing price of bulk diesel,” said an official.

stories.summary: The latest remarks by a US official sequencing developments that led to the attack seemed aimed at reassuring Indian authorities that US forces had not acted in a reckless manner in launching strikes on Settebello and two other foreign-flagged ships in the past week. However, the US is yet to express any regret for the deaths of Indian mariners.

On this occasion, Pakistan said after the announcement by both Trump and Iran that it would host in Geneva this week the signing of the agreement, which is expected to formally mark the end of the conflict that started on Feb 28.

He directed states and central agencies to ensure that security protocols are strictly followed. NTA said it is working towards resolving all issues, including refunds. News of the US-Iran peace deal promised to remove the dark clouds over aviation and seemed like a good portent for the new airport. A contingent of around 80 business executives also boarded the flight, raising visions of the now sleepy Agra expressway resembling the Dwarka or Gurgaon expressways in the coming years with both sides of the stretch getting developed.

India has a long-term gas supply contract with QatarEnergy’s Ras Laffan facility. UAE’s Habshan Gas Plant was also damaged, disrupting operations. Officials said 60% of the plant’s capacity has been restored. They expect recovery to reach 80% by the end of 2026 and full structural restoration in 2027.

Despite the tensions, the deal is set for signing, with Iran still vowing retaliation.

stories.title: Infrastructure boom, AI fears drive civil engineering’s strong comeback at top IITs
stories.summary: Industry observers believe it is not just opportunities presented by the infrastructure boom; broader economic shifts may also be influencing student choices. “AI fears are accelerating the move toward core branches like civil for students seeking stability,” said Bhushan Jamsandekar, an IIT Madras alumnus. The broader hierarchy of the IIT system, however, remains largely unchanged.

stories.title: Cristiano Ronaldo’s FIFA World Cup journey coincides with Georgina Rodriguez’s biggest professional achievement yet
stories.summary: Georgina Rodriguez has been named the new face of Italian fashion brand Calzedonia, revealing the partnership on social media on June 12, 2026, just one day after the FIFA World Cup began in North America. The announcement adds to a growing modelling portfolio that includes Dior, Moncler, and Charlotte Tilbury. Rodriguez, who has 73 million Instagram followers and her own Netflix series, met partner Cristiano Ronaldo in 2016 while working at a Gucci store in Madrid. Ronaldo is currently competing in his sixth FIFA World Cup, captaining Portugal for the fifth time.

stories.title: Will Modi take up sailor deaths with Trump, asks Congress
stories.summary: Congress said India should put off the upcoming visit of US trade representatives in view of the killings of seafarers and Rubio’s “threatening language” with Jaishankar. Party president Mallikarjun Kharge slammed the PM for his “silence” over the killings. “And you have the audacity to sugarcoat it with the ‘Vishwaguru’ narrative.

stories.title: NEET leak & jobs: Rahul Gandhi to hold town halls across nation
stories.summary: Congress has planned a national outreach that will seek to unite students beyond political affiliations and provide a platform for the affected youth to share their experiences and demand accountability for “repeated examination failures and paper leak scandals”. AICC general secretary KC Venugopal said Rahul will also be holding conventions in Allahabad (July 10), Patna (July 11), and Delhi (July 14).

stories.title: YouTuber Vlad Ncl punched during Dublin livestream as video sparks anti trans debate
stories.summary: Vlad Ncl was punched during a Dublin livestream after a stranger questioned his gender presentation while he was dressed as Natalia. The video quickly spread online, leading to heated debate about public safety, gender bias and prank content. While many condemned the attack, others questioned the risks involved in social experiments. Police have reportedly received video evidence, but no arrest has been announced.

stories.title: Twitch streamer Clavicular revealed his post-surgery face as years of looksmaxxing content came under fire
stories.summary: Braden Peters, better known as Kick streamer Clavicular, went viral after asking viewers not to mock his swollen face following multiple cosmetic procedures. The request sparked strong reactions because of his long history of promoting extreme appearance-focused practices and criticizing looks. The debate has since expanded into a larger discussion about influencer culture, cosmetic trends, and online accountability.

stories.title: Who was Gaspi? Argentine YouTuber dies alongside Oliver Tree in Rio helicopter crash
stories.summary: Gaspar Prim Díaz, known online as Gaspi, was a 23-year-old Argentine YouTuber famous for his street comedy, improvised interviews, and signature greeting “Buenass.” He became one of Argentina’s most popular digital creators and later gained wider attention through La Velada del Año V. Gaspi died in the Rio de Janeiro helicopter crash that also killed singer Oliver Tree and four others.

stories.title: Oliver Tree death: KSI remembers his friend with emotional tribute after tragic helicopter crash
stories.summary: KSI paid tribute to Oliver Tree after reports said the musician and content creator died in a helicopter crash in Rio de Janeiro on June 14, 2026. In an emotional message, KSI remembered his friend as a “lifelong legend” and shared personal photos from their friendship. Fans have since flooded social media with tributes and memories of the 32-year-old artist.

stories.title: Buzz of early poll in Punjab, parties start preparations
stories.summary: The AICC’s decision to constitute a committee under Ajay Maken late Thursday night for a report on the Punjab Congress unit is said to be dictated by urgency for quick changes in the state organisation as needed. AAP is preparing for a scenario of Nov polls, and BJP is also active on Punjab front. Further, there is speculation in Congress whether Uttarakhand polls will also be brought forward.

stories.title: With farmers' income in focus, Bihar govt moves to boost fisheries
stories.summary: The foundation stones will be laid by minister for fisheries and animal husbandry Rajiv Ranjan Singh and Bihar CM Samrat Choudhary. The aqua park will include carp and catfish hatcheries, Brooder incubation units, biofloc systems, a fish feed mill, water quality and disease diagnostic laboratories, involving a total investment of more than Rs 31 crore.

stories.title: Modi tells India’s deep-tech story to the world, Macron backs him up
stories.summary: Before the cameras rolled at the conclave, the PM sat down with global venture capitalists and Indian entrepreneurs — OYO’s Ritesh Agarwal, Ronnie Screwvala and a clutch of international investors among them. Commerce minister Piyush Goyal and principal scientific adviser Ajay Kumar Sood were in the room. “India has emerged not as a consumer of solutions but as a contributor to solutions in the world.

stories.title: Rescued 14 Indians from sinking dhow, says US
stories.summary: S Naval Forces Central Command/US 5th Fleet reposted a news report about the rescue operation that said “upon receiving a distress call from the stranded sailors, a US Navy P-8 aircraft reached the spot and dropped a search-and-rescue kit that included a life raft, which the 14 mariners boarded”. Official sources said that the US Navy had alerted the shore authorities and Indian Navy that a dhow with Indian sailors was sinking about 80 nautical miles east of Ras AI Hadd off the coast of Oman.

stories.title: 'JD was interested in my conversion and...': Usha Vance opens up on husband’s faith
TMC rebels to merge with little-known regional party
stories.summary: In a dramatic development, 20 rebel Trinamool Congress MPs informed Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla that their group has merged with NCPI — which is registered in West Bengal’s Howrah and had contested a few seats in the 2023 Tripura assembly elections — and that they will be backing the BJP-led NDA. Incidentally, “to save your rights, reject political turncoats” was one of the slogans of NCPI.

stories.title: 2x trade in 5 years, nuclear cooperation: Modi-Macron Nice meet
stories.summary: Adoption of an innovation roadmap to deepen cooperation in critical and emerging technology, launch of an economic security dialogue, another working group for AI governance and a declaration to double bilateral trade in the next five years were among the 13 outcomes announced after the meeting. Both sides also looked to ramp up defence cooperation, consistent with India’s Make in India initiative.

stories.title: Donald Trump 'uncomfortable with ageing', says Tucker Carlson as US president turns 80
Who is Austin Franco? US student says he was ‘not interested in working for a Jew’
Abhishek Banerjee urges Lok Sabha speaker not to recognise rebel TMC bloc
stories.summary: Ahead of TMC rebel MPs’ meeting the speaker to seek recognition as “real TMC”, MPs from party chief Mamata Banerjee’s camp Kirti Azad and Sagarika Ghosh submitted Abhishek’s letter — dated June 10, sent through email earlier — at Birla’s residence here, arguing the Constitution does not permit formation of a separate group within an existing political party.

stories.title: Mortal remains of AN-32 crash victims from Jorhat sent to their native places by IAF
stories.summary: The Indian Air Force (IAF) transported the mortal remains of the personnel who lost their lives in the crash of an AN-32 transport aircraft at the Jorhat Air Force Station in Assam on June 13, to their native places for the last rites with full military honours, Defence officials said.

stories.title: Sunday Bloody Sunday: Trump warns Israel not to blow up Iran deal
India, France unveil 13 major outcomes to deepen strategic partnership after PM Modi-Macron talks in Nice
Lookmaxxing streamer Clavicular’s resurfaced 2025 video predicted his Miami future, reality tells a bigger story
stories.summary: An old July 2025 video of Clavicular resurfaced on X on June 14, 2026. In the clip, he talked about moving to Miami, building a business, and enjoying club life. Many people noticed that parts of that vision later became reality. The video has sparked discussion about his career, appearance changes, business ventures, and the path he has taken since then.

stories.title: ‘Armed forces have full freedom’: Rajnath Singh says India knows how to ensure peace
stories.summary: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh declared India's readiness to decisively counter security threats, granting armed forces full autonomy against terrorism. He criticized past governments' soft approach, highlighting current freedom to eliminate terrorists, even across borders. Singh also lauded Maharana Pratap as a symbol of national pride and linked his values to the Modi government's governance philosophy.
